callback-box/docs/migrations.md:5:A migration is a one-shot transformation of card data on disk — schema renames, field strips, layout flips, refactors. The system tracks which migrations a box has had applied so future runs only do the missing work.
callback-box/docs/migrations.md:7:## `cb migrate` is the entry point
callback-box/docs/migrations.md:9:Each box has `config/migrations.jsonl` — append-only JSONL, one `{name, applied-at}` per line — recording which migrations it's seen. `cb migrate` compares against the canonical ordered list in `src/core/migrations.ts` and runs anything missing in order, appending an entry after each success.
callback-box/docs/migrations.md:12:cb migrate                      # status — show applied + pending
callback-box/docs/migrations.md:13:cb migrate --apply              # run all pending in order
callback-box/docs/migrations.md:14:cb migrate --mark-all-applied   # seed the manifest as if every known migration ran
callback-box/docs/migrations.md:15:                                # (legacy box that was already fully migrated before this command existed)
callback-box/docs/migrations.md:18:`cb init` writes a seeded manifest (all-applied) for new boxes automatically — new boxes don't need to run historical migrations. A missing manifest in an existing box is a hard error; the user must explicitly `--mark-all-applied` to declare "this box is already up to date."
callback-box/docs/migrations.md:20:If a migration fails, the manifest is **not** updated for the failing entry and subsequent migrations are not attempted. Fix the underlying problem and re-run; the loop picks up where it stopped.
callback-box/docs/migrations.md:24:1. **Write the script** at `scripts/migrate/<name>.ts`. New migrators should use the shared harness (`scripts/migrate/_harness.ts`), which handles arg parsing, the file walk, dry-run/apply, per-file error collection, and the final warning dump:
callback-box/docs/migrations.md:46:   Existing migrators in this directory predate the harness and still carry their own scaffolding; mirror one (e.g. `scripts/migrate/image.ts`) only if you can't fit the harness's shape.

callback-box/docs/migrations.md:51:   `cb migrate` re-runs partially-applied migrations on retry, and admins occasionally run individual scripts manually for debugging — idempotency makes both safe.
callback-box/docs/migrations.md:53:3. **Be noisy about data loss.** Every migrator must use the `scripts/migrate/_warnings.ts` helper to declare what attrs/children it knows how to map, and warn about anything outside that allow-list.    278	export async function createSchemaRegistry(boxRoot?: string): Promise<SchemaRegistry> {
   279	  const registry = new SchemaRegistry();
   280	  for (const schema of schemas) {
   281	    registry.register(schema);
   282	  }
   283	  if (boxRoot) {
   284	    const { elementSchemas } = await loadBoxSchemas(boxRoot);
   285	    for (const schema of elementSchemas) {
   286	      registry.register(schema);
   287	    }
   288	  }
   289	  return registry;
   290	}

   298	  if (!boxRoot) return schemas;
   299	  const { elementSchemas } = await loadBoxSchemas(boxRoot);
   300	  return [...schemas, ...elementSchemas];
   301	}

   319	  const elementSchemas = await getAllSchemas(boxRoot);
   320	  const boxCardSchemas = boxRoot ? (await loadBoxSchemas(boxRoot)).cardSchemas : [];
   321	  const allCardSchemas = [...cardSchemas, ...boxCardSchemas];
   322	  return [
   323	    ...elementSchemas.filter(s => s.searchable !== false).map(s => s.tagName),
   324	    ...allCardSchemas.filter(s => s.searchable).map(s => s.type),
   325	  ];
   326	}

     1	/**
     2	 * Static scaffold files installed into a box on init.
     3	 *
     4	 * These are the box-local guide/scaffold documents whose content is a large
     5	 * embedded string (tricks scaffolding, the schemas authoring guide, the views

     7	 * no-ops on re-run; the schemas guide goes through the template tracker
     8	 * (refresh-if-unmodified, park-if-edited) so its frontmatter-first rewrite
     9	 * reaches boxes that still carry the old XML-only version. Either way, `cb
    10	 * init` can run repeatedly without clobbering user edits.
    11	 */
    12	
    13	import * as fs from "node:fs/promises";
    14	import * as path from "node:path";
    15	import { installTemplateFile } from "./install-template-file.js";
    16	
    17	const SCHEMAS_CLAUDE_MD = `# Writing Box-Local Schemas
    18	
    19	Box-local schemas let you define new card types inside your box. Each schema is a \`.ts\` file
    20	in \`config/schemas/\` that uses the same tools as built-in schemas.
    21	
    22	**Default to the frontmatter form** (\`cardSchema\`) shown below: it produces standard cards —
    23	YAML frontmatter plus a markdown body. Reach for the legacy \`element()\` / XML form only when
    24	your card needs Markdoc-shaped inline content (see the end of this guide).
    25	
    26	## Creating a Schema
    27	
    28	Create a \`.ts\` file in \`config/schemas/\` that default-exports a \`cardSchema()\`:
    29	
    30	\`\`\`typescript
    31	import { body, cardSchema } from "cardworks";
    32	import { z } from "zod";
    33	
    34	export default cardSchema("my-type", {
    35	  fields: {
    36	    status: z.enum(["draft", "final"]).default("draft"),
    37	    priority: z.enum(["low", "medium", "high"]).optional(),
    38	    body: body(z.string()),  // omit this line if the card has no prose body
    39	  },
    40	  instructions: \\\`# My Type Cards
    41	
    42	Instructions for the agent on how to handle this card type.
    43	These appear in .claude/rules/ and docs/generated/, and are loaded
    44	when the agent reads or edits a matching card file.\\\`,
    45	});
    46	\`\`\`
    47	
    48	The filename becomes the card type: \`config/schemas/task.ts\` → \`*.task.card\` files.
    49	
    50	On disk, a card of this type is YAML frontmatter + markdown body:
    51	
    52	\`\`\`
    53	---
    54	status: draft
    55	priority: high
    56	---
    57	The markdown body (present only when the schema declares a \`body\` field).
    58	\`\`\`
    59	
    60	Key patterns:
    61	- \`cardSchema(type, { fields, instructions? })\` is the entry point. \`fields\` is a flat object
    62	  of Zod validators; nest with \`z.object\` / \`z.array\` as needed.
    63	- \`body(z.string())\` declares the markdown body field — it must be named \`body\`. Omit it for a
    64	  body-less card (then any non-empty body errors on load).
    65	- \`type\` is the discriminator; don't list it under \`fields\`, and the on-disk YAML needn't carry
    66	  it — the filename \`Foo.<type>.card\` supplies it.
    67	- \`title\` and \`contains\` are available on every card type automatically.
    68	
    69	## Available Imports
    70	
    71	From \`cardworks\`:
    72	- \`cardSchema(type, config)\` — define a frontmatter card schema (the default)
    73	- \`body(zodSchema)\` — declare the single markdown body field
    74	- \`element(tagName, config)\` — define a legacy XML schema (see below)
    75	- \`escapeText(str)\` / \`escapeAttr(str)\` — XML-escape helpers (only for \`element()\` schemas)
    76	
    77	From \`zod\`:
    78	- \`z\` — Zod schema builder (z.string(), z.enum(), z.array(), etc.)
    79	
    80	## Optional: Templates
    81	
    82	Export a \`template\` to enable \`cb create\` for your card type. For frontmatter schemas,
    83	\`generate\` returns the card text — a YAML frontmatter block built with \`stringify\` from \`yaml\`:
    84	
    85	\`\`\`typescript
    86	import { cardSchema } from "cardworks";
    87	import { stringify as stringifyYaml } from "yaml";
    88	import { z } from "zod";
    89	
    90	export const template = {
    91	  name: "task",
    92	  description: "A task card",
    93	  argsSchema: z.object({
    94	    title: z.string().describe("Task title"),
    95	    priority: z.enum(["low", "medium", "high"]).optional().describe("Priority level"),
    96	  }),
    97	  generate: (args: { title: string; priority?: string }) => {
    98	    const fields: Record<string, unknown> = { status: "todo", title: args.title };
    99	    if (args.priority !== undefined) fields.priority = args.priority;
   100	    return "---\\n" + stringifyYaml(fields) + "---\\n";
   101	  },
   102	  cardTypes: ["task"],
   103	  defaultForTypes: ["task"],
   104	};
   105	
   106	export default cardSchema("task", {
   107	  // ... schema definition
   108	});
   109	\`\`\`
   110	
   111	## After Adding or Modifying Schemas
   112	
   113	Run \`cb init\` to regenerate rules and documentation:
   114	
   115	\`\`\`bash
   116	cb init .
   117	\`\`\`
   118	
   119	This will:
   120	- Generate \`.claude/rules/card-<type>.md\` (if the schema has \`instructions\`)
   121	- Generate \`docs/generated/card-<type>.md\`
   122	- Register any templates for \`cb create\`
   123	
   124	Schema changes are picked up on the next \`cb\` invocation; a running dev server needs a restart.
   125	
   126	## Legacy: XML / \`element()\` schemas
   127	
   128	Use \`element()\` only when the card body is Markdoc-shaped inline content — nested, attributed
   129	inline structure that doesn't fit YAML frontmatter. This is why the built-in \`guide\` and
   130	\`capture-session\` types still use it. For everything else, prefer \`cardSchema\` above.
   131	
   132	\`\`\`typescript
   133	import { element } from "cardworks";
   134	import { z } from "zod";
   135	
   136	export default element("note", {
   137	  attrs: {
   138	    status: z.enum(["draft", "final"]).default("draft"),
   139	  },
   140	  children: z.array(z.unknown()),
   141	  instructions: \\\`# Note Cards
   142	
   143	Instructions for the agent on how to handle this card type.\\\`,
   144	});
   145	\`\`\`
   146	
   147	A legacy template's \`generate\` emits XML instead of YAML, using \`escapeText\` / \`escapeAttr\` for
   148	interpolated values. See the built-in XML schemas in callback-box's \`src/schemas/\` for examples.
   149	
   150	## Tips
   151	
   152	- Keep schema files focused — one card type per file
   153	- Always include \`instructions\` so the agent knows how to handle the card type
   154	- Test with \`cb validate\` after creating cards of the new type
   155	`;

     1	# Card Schemas
     2	
     3	The schema system registers card types, provides template generators, and validates card XML. Each card type has a tag name, template generator, and optional instructions for agents.
     4	
     5	```ts setup
     6	import {
     7	  MemoSchema,
     8	  QuestionSchema,
     9	  createMemoTemplate,
    10	  createSelectQuestionTemplate,
    11	  createSchemaRegistry,
    12	  getCardTypes,
    13	  getDefaultTemplate,
    14	} from "../src/schemas/index.js";
    15	import { createIntakeJobTemplate } from "../src/schemas/intake-job.js";
    16	import { createCalendarReviewJobTemplate } from "../src/schemas/calendar-review-job.js";
    17	import { WebpageSchema, createWebpageTemplate } from "../src/schemas/webpage.js";
    18	import { parseCard } from "cardworks";
    19	```
    20	
    21	## Schema Registry
    22	
    23	The registry tracks all known card types:
    24	
    25	```
    26	getCardTypes().includes("memo")
    27	=> true
    28	
    29	getCardTypes().includes("question")
    30	=> true
    31	
    32	getCardTypes().includes("intake-job")
    33	=> true
    34	
    35	getCardTypes().includes("calendar-review-job")
    36	=> true
    37	
    38	getCardTypes().includes("webpage")
    39	=> true
    40	
    41	```
    42	
    43	XML schemas have a `tagName`; Phase 2 frontmatter schemas (memo,
    44	email-thread, etc.) carry a `type` instead.
    45	
    46	```
    47	MemoSchema.type
    48	=> memo
    49	
    50	QuestionSchema.type
    51	=> question
    52	
    53	WebpageSchema.type
    54	=> webpage
    55	
    56	```
    57	
    58	The full registry of XML schemas is available via `createSchemaRegistry()`:
    59	
    60	```
    61	const registry = await createSchemaRegistry();
    62	registry.get("memo")
    63	=> «*»
    64	```
    65	
    66	## Templates
    67	
    68	Template generators produce XML card content for the core card types. All templates escape special characters and produce well-formed XML.
    69	
    70	## Memo
    71	
    72	A memo captures a piece of content, optionally with a source. The
    73	content lives in the markdown body; created/source/etc. are in the
    74	YAML frontmatter.
    75	
    76	```
    77	createMemoTemplate("Test content", "test-source")
    78	=>
    79	---
    80	status: new
    81	created: «*»
    82	source: test-source
    83	---
    84	Test content
    85	```
    86	
    87	Source is optional:
    88	
    89	```
    90	createMemoTemplate("Just content")
     1	# Box-Local Schemas
     2	
     3	Boxes define their own card types under `config/schemas/*.ts`. Each file default-exports
     4	either a frontmatter `cardSchema()` (the default for new types) or a legacy XML `element()`
     5	schema. `loadBoxSchemas` discovers both, segregating them by format; box frontmatter schemas
     6	become first-class in the same parse/validate path as built-in ones.
     7	
     8	```ts setup
     9	import * as fs from "node:fs/promises";
    10	import * as path from "node:path";
    11	import * as os from "node:os";
    12	import { initBox } from "../src/core/box.js";
    13	import { loadBoxSchemas, createCardSchemaMap } from "../src/schemas/registry.js";
    14	import { buildLoadContext } from "../src/core/load-context.js";
    15	import { loadCardFromText } from "../src/core/card-io.js";
    16	
    17	async function makeTmpBox() {
    18	  const box = await fs.mkdtemp(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "cb-boxschemas-"));
    19	  await initBox(box, { skipGit: true });
    20	  return box;
    21	}
    22	
    23	// Returns the error class name when a card fails to load, or "no-error".
    24	async function loadErrorName(content, source, ctx) {
    25	  try {
    26	    await loadCardFromText({ content, source, ctx });
    27	    return "no-error";
    28	  } catch (e) {
    29	    return e.constructor.name;
    30	  }
    31	}
    32	
    33	// A frontmatter card type: config in YAML + a markdown body.
    34	const WIDGET_SCHEMA = `import { body, cardSchema } from "cardworks";
    35	import { z } from "zod";
    36	
    37	export default cardSchema("widget", {
    38	  fields: {
    39	    status: z.enum(["new", "done"]).default("new"),
    40	    size: z.number(),
    41	    body: body(z.string()),
    42	  },
    43	  instructions: "# Widget Cards\\n\\nA box-local frontmatter card type.",
    44	});
    45	`;
    46	
    47	// A legacy XML card type, to prove both formats coexist.
    48	const GADGET_SCHEMA = `import { element } from "cardworks";
    49	import { z } from "zod";
    50	
    51	export default element("gadget", {
    52	  attrs: {
    53	    status: z.enum(["on", "off"]).default("off"),
    54	  },
    55	  children: z.array(z.unknown()),
    56	});
    57	`;
    58	
    59	const WIDGET_CARD = `---
    60	size: 3
    61	---
    62	Hello widget body.
    63	`;
    64	
    65	const GADGET_CARD = `<gadget status="on"></gadget>`;
    66	```
    67	
    68	## Loading segregates frontmatter from XML
    69	
    70	Both schema files must exist before the first `loadBoxSchemas` call (results are cached per
    71	box). The loader segregates them: the `cardSchema()` lands in `cardSchemas`, the `element()`
    72	in `elementSchemas`:
    73	
    74	```
    75	const box = await makeTmpBox();
    76	await fs.writeFile(path.join(box, "config/schemas/widget.ts"), WIDGET_SCHEMA);
    77	await fs.writeFile(path.join(box, "config/schemas/gadget.ts"), GADGET_SCHEMA);
    78	
    79	const loaded = await loadBoxSchemas(box);
    80	[loaded.cardSchemas.length, loaded.elementSchemas.length, loaded.cardSchemas[0].type, loaded.elementSchemas[0].tagName].join("|")
    81	=> 1|1|widget|gadget
    82	```
    83	
    84	## Box frontmatter cards load and validate
    85	
    86	`buildLoadContext` merges box frontmatter schemas into the same map built-in cards use, so a
    87	`widget` card parses as the new format with its YAML fields and markdown body:
    88	
    89	``` continue
    90	const ctx = await buildLoadContext(box);
    91	const card = await loadCardFromText({ content: WIDGET_CARD, source: "My.widget.card", ctx });
    92	[card.kind, card.schema.type, card.fields.size, card.fields.status, card.fields.body].join("|")
    93	=> frontmatter|widget|3|new|Hello widget body.
    94	```
    95	
    96	Validation rejects a malformed card — `size` must be a number:
    97	
    98	``` continue
    99	const bad = "---\nsize: not-a-number\n---\n";
   100	await loadErrorName(bad, "X.widget.card", ctx)
   101	=> CardIOError
   102	```
   103	
   104	The legacy XML `gadget` card still loads through the same context:
   105	
   106	``` continue
   107	const gadget = await loadCardFromText({ content: GADGET_CARD, source: "G.gadget.card", ctx });
   108	[gadget.kind, gadget.element.tagName].join("|")
   109	=> xml|gadget
   110	```
   111	
   112	## The box type is a first-class entry in the card-schema map
   113	
   114	`createCardSchemaMap(boxRoot)` includes box frontmatter types alongside the built-ins:
   115	
   116	``` continue
   117	const map = await createCardSchemaMap(box);
   118	map.has("widget")
   119	=> true
   120	```
   121	
   122	``` cleanup
   123	await fs.rm(box, { recursive: true, force: true });
   124	```

    83	export function getRenderers(filePath: string, data: FileData): FileRenderer[] {

The todo claim is directionally right but has a nuance: current frontmatter todo-list cards don’t even feed `TodoListView` an `element`, so the UI likely shows its empty/no-data state before the mutation can run. The mutation itself is still XML-only and would fail on a frontmatter file if called, so the proposed rewrite is still the right fix.

    79	export async function moveDir(params: MoveDirParams): Promise<MoveDirResult> {
    80	  const { ctx, sourcePath, destPath } = params;
    81	  const relSourcePath = path.relative(ctx.boxRoot, sourcePath);

    83	
    84	  // Move the directory

    89	  const filesToStage: string[] = [];

    91

    94	    if (abs === sourcePath) return destPath;

    96	      return destPath + abs.slice(sourcePath.length);
    97	    }

   103	  // relative refs to targets that stayed outside.

   212	  const extraUpdated: Array<{ path: string; refsUpdated: number }> = [];

   217	    if (cardPath === destPath) continue;
   218	    if (cardPath.startsWith(newAttachAbsDir + path.sep)) continue;

   222	        boxRoot: ctx.boxRoot,
   223	        cardAbsPath: cardPath,
   224	        text: original,
   225	        remap,
   226	      });

   228	      await fs.writeFile(cardPath, updated);
   229	      const relPath = path.relative(ctx.boxRoot, cardPath);
   230	      extraUpdated.push({ path: relPath, refsUpdated: count });

     2	 * Card patch + element serialization helpers for the REST API.
     3	 *
     4	 * Split out of `api.ts`. These are the pure, self-contained pieces the
     5	 * `/api/card/*` GET and PATCH handlers lean on:
     6	 *
     7	 * - `PatchOp` — the wire shape of a single patch operation
     8	 * - `navigateToChild` / `parseXmlFragment` — element navigation + fragment parse
     9	 * - `JsonElement` / `sanitizeElement` — JSON-safe element tree for the frontend
    10	 */
    11	
    12	import type { ElementNode } from "cardworks";
    13	
    14	export type PatchOp =
    15	  | { op: "set-attr"; path?: string; attr: string; value: string }
    16	  | { op: "remove-attr"; path?: string; attr: string }
    17	  | { op: "set-text"; path: string; value: string }
    18	  | { op: "append-child"; path?: string; xml: string }
    19	  | { op: "remove-child"; path: string; index: number };
    20	
    21	/**
    22	 * Navigate to a child element by a simple path like "section/ingredients/ing[2]".
    23	 * Segments are tag names; [N] picks the Nth match (0-indexed).
    24	 */
    25	export function navigateToChild(el: ElementNode, pathStr: string): ElementNode | null {
    26	  const segments = pathStr.split("/").filter(Boolean);
    27	  let current: ElementNode = el;
    28	  for (const seg of segments) {
    29	    const match = seg.match(/^(\w[\w-]*?)(?:\[(\d+)])?$/);
    30	    if (!match) return null;
    31	    const tagName = match[1]!;
    32	    const idx = match[2] !== undefined ? parseInt(match[2], 10) : 0;
    33	    const matches = current.children.filter(c => c.tagName === tagName);
    34	    if (idx >= matches.length) return null;
    35	    current = matches[idx]!;
    36	  }
    37	  return current;
    38	}
    39	
    40	/**
    41	 * Parse a simple XML fragment like `<tag attr="val">text</tag>` into an ElementNode.
    42	 * Very basic — handles single elements only.
    43	 */
    44	export function parseXmlFragment(xml: string): ElementNode | null {
    45	  const match = xml.match(/^<(\w[\w-]*)((?:\s+[\w-]+="[^"]*")*)(?:\s*\/>|>([\S\s]*?)<\/\1>)$/);
    46	  if (!match) return null;
    47	  const tagName = match[1]!;
    48	  const attrStr = match[2] ?? "";
    49	  const text = match[3]?.trim();
    50	
    51	  const attrs: Record<string, string> = {};
    52	  const attrRegex = /([\w-]+)="([^"]*)"/g;
    53	  let attrMatch;
    54	  while ((attrMatch = attrRegex.exec(attrStr))) {
    55	    attrs[attrMatch[1]!] = attrMatch[2]!;
    56	  }
    57	
    58	  return {
    59	    tagName,
    60	    attrs,
    61	    children: [],
    62	    text: text || undefined,
    63	    comments: {},
    64	    location: { source: "", startLine: 0, startColumn: 0, endLine: 0, endColumn: 0 },
    65	    dirty: true,
    66	  } as ElementNode;
    67	}
    68	
    69	/**
    70	 * JSON-safe element node for the frontend.
    71	 */
    72	export interface JsonElement {
    73	  tagName: string;
    74	  attrs: Record<string, string>;
    75	  text?: string;
    76	  children?: JsonElement[];
    77	}
    78	
    79	/**
    80	 * Convert an ElementNode to a JSON-safe structure.
    81	 */
    82	export function sanitizeElement(el: ElementNode): JsonElement {
    83	  const result: JsonElement = {
    84	    tagName: el.tagName,
    85	    attrs: {},
    86	  };
    87	
    88	  // Copy string attributes only
    89	  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(el.attrs)) {
    90	    if (typeof value === "string") {
    91	      result.attrs[key] = value;
    92	    }
    93	  }
    94	
    95	  // Include text if present
    96	  if (el.text !== undefined && el.text !== null) {
    97	    result.text = String(el.text).trim();
    98	  }
    99	
   100	  // Recursively process children
   101	  if (el.children && Array.isArray(el.children) && el.children.length > 0) {
   102	    result.children = el.children.map((child) => sanitizeElement(child as ElementNode));
   103	  }
   104	
   105	  return result;
   106	}

callback-box/docs/stack-decisions.md:254:- **`@jsxImportSource` pragma required on schema `.tsx` files.** The frontend's `@backend/*` path alias causes TypeScript to follow the full backend import chain, including `src/schemas/*.tsx` files that use cardworks custom JSX. Without per-file `/** @jsxImportSource cardworks/jsx */` pragmas, the frontend typecheck applies `react-jsx` to those files and reports hundreds of false errors. The cardworks `package.json` also needed a `./jsx/jsx-dev-runtime` export entry.

callback-box/docs/agent-knowledge.md:19:7. **Improvised** — The agent constructs a plausible approach without checking if there's an established one. Unlike guessing (which is about facts), this is about strategy: the agent builds something that works but misses patterns or tools it should have used. Example: writing a custom XML parser when cardworks already has one, or hand-rolling a card file instead of using `cb create`. The result may actually function, which makes it harder to catch than a wrong guess — the problem is that it's not the *right* way, and it'll diverge from conventions. Often a fallback when the agent decides it can figure things out as it goes rather than looking up how things are done.

callback-box/docs/ideas.md:533:2. **Server pulls from GitHub on deploy.** Standard CI/CD pattern, single source of truth, but every deploy is a GitHub roundtrip. Same multi-repo dance for cardworks.
callback-box/docs/ideas.md:701:Benefits: agents already write Markdown fluently, diffs are cleaner, easier to read/edit by hand, no need for the cardworks XML library. Tradeoffs: XML's strict structure prevents malformed cards — Markdown frontmatter is more loosely coupled from the body content.
callback-box/docs/ideas.md:816:Cardworks already exposes the ref graph — `findIncomingRefs(targetPath)` and `findOutgoingRefs(sourcePath)` in `cardworks/src/loader/loader.ts`. The data exists; no read surface does. Obsidian's Backlinks pane is widely considered its most-used navigation surface, and we have a richer (typed, versioned, fragment-addressable) reference model — closing the UI gap is mostly plumbing.
callback-box/docs/ideas.md:846:Where `<fragment>` follows cardworks' existing scheme (`id`, `query(xpath)`, `query-all(xpath)`).
callback-box/docs/ideas.md:998:Fits the existing infrastructure surprisingly well: the `WorktreeCreate` hook already runs setup per worktree, so a `bd ready` call at session start is a natural extension. Per-subproject scoping via labels (`callback-box`, `cardworks`, `clerk`, `agent-doctest`).
callback-box/docs/ideas.md:1052:The repeated failure mode: agent is asked for X, agent writes X from scratch, X already existed under a slightly different name in `src/components/ui/` or `src/lib/` or `cardworks/`. The agent doesn't know what to grep for because the existing thing's name doesn't match the task vocabulary. Result: parallel implementations, drift, the codebase gets harder to navigate over time precisely *because* it has more in it.
callback-box/docs/ideas.md:1054:Idea: an index of available units — UI components, hooks, helpers, schemas, cardworks elements, services — keyed by an embedding of their *purpose* (from JSDoc, the type signature, neighboring usage). The agent, before building anything non-trivial, queries the index with a natural-language description of what it's about to write. The index returns the top few candidates with one-line summaries and file paths. If something fits, the agent reuses; if nothing fits, it proceeds and the index re-embeds the new thing.
callback-box/docs/testing.md:470:Not a test you run manually, but a live validation hook. When an agent writes or edits a `.card` file, the hook calls cardworks' `lintCards` in-process and feeds any issues back as `additionalContext`. This catches XML/schema issues during agent work rather than after.

callback-box/docs/cards-as-markdown.md:40:**Loader dispatch:** `src/core/card-io.ts` `loadCardFile()` returns a discriminated union of `FrontmatterLoadedCard | XmlLoadedCard`. Frontmatter dispatch uses `cardSchemas` (Map keyed by `type:` field); XML falls through to the legacy cardworks `parseCard`. This lets XML and frontmatter cards coexist during and after the migration.

callback-box/docs/cards-as-markdown.md:155:Cards are XML files validated by Zod schemas defined with cardworks `element()`. Filename pattern: `Name.type.card`. Attachments share the basename:
callback-box/docs/cards-as-markdown.md:223:Note: the type (`image`) lives in the filename, not in frontmatter. Schemas move from cardworks `element()` to per-card-type definitions in `.ts` files (Zod for frontmatter shape + Markdoc tag definitions for body content + optional code validators). See the Schema authoring section for details.
callback-box/docs/cards-as-markdown.md:231:The explanation-length test (see Test results section) confirms this is modest, not dramatic: the full Cards section in `CLAUDE.md` is roughly the same length under all three formats. But the *concepts* in the new version are more familiar — bespoke project-specific things (cardworks, `element()`, flat-XML formatting) shrink in favor of widely-known ones (Markdown, YAML, JSON Schema). Familiarity is what reduces friction at authoring time, not section length.
callback-box/docs/cards-as-markdown.md:272:cardworks `element()` was designed around the patterns we use: arrays of unioned child elements with loose order, attribute typing with Zod, ref validation. JSON Schema can express all of this, but `oneOf` arrays of object schemas with discriminator properties are verbose and awkward to author by hand. We'd want to keep authoring schemas in Zod and emit JSON Schema as a build artifact — and as a downstream concern, **review the emitted JSON Schema for agent legibility**, because Zod-derived JSON Schemas can sometimes be ugly enough to undermine the "agents read JSON Schema as docs" benefit. See the schema-authoring section.

callback-box/dist/cli.mjs.map:4:  "sourcesContent": ["/**\n * Duration and budget parsing for scheduled scripts.\n *\n * Duration strings use a numeric value plus a unit suffix\n * (s/m/h/d/w). Budgets are \"LIMIT/WINDOW\" pairs of duration strings.\n */\n\nexport class InvalidDurationError extends Error {\n  constructor(input: string) {\n    super(`Invalid duration: \"${input}\". Use format like \"5m\", \"1h\", \"1d\", \"2w\".`);\n    this.name = \"InvalidDurationError\";\n  }\n}\n\nexport class UnknownDurationUnitError extends Error {\n  constructor(unit: string) {\n    super(`Unknown duration unit: \"${unit}\"`);\n    this.name = \"UnknownDurationUnitError\";\n  }\n}\n\nexport class InvalidBudgetError extends Error {\n  constructor(input: string) {\n    super(`Invalid budget: \"${input}\". Use format like \"10m/5h\".`);\n    this.name = \"InvalidBudgetError\";\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Parse a duration string like \"5m\", \"1h\", \"1d\", \"2w\" into milliseconds.\n *\n * Supported suffixes: s (seconds), m (minutes), h (hours), d (days), w (weeks)\n */\nexport function parseDuration(str: string): number {\n  const match = str.match(/^(\\d+\\.?\\d*)\\s*([dhmsw])$/);\n  if (!match) {\n    throw new InvalidDurationError(str);\n  }\n\n  const value = parseFloat(match[1]!);\n  const unit = match[2]!;\n\n  switch (unit) {\n    case \"s\":\n      return value * 1000;\n    case \"m\":\n      return value * 60 * 1000;\n    case \"h\":\n      return value * 60 * 60 * 1000;\n    case \"d\":\n      return value * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;\n    case \"w\":\n      return value * 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;\n  }\n\n  throw new UnknownDurationUnitError(unit);\n}\n\n/**\n * Parse a budget string like \"10m/5h\" into limit and window in milliseconds.\n * Format: \"LIMIT/WINDOW\" where both use duration syntax (e.g., \"5m\", \"1h\").\n */\nexport function parseBudget(str: string): { limitMs: number; windowMs: number } {\n  const slash = str.indexOf(\"/\");\n  if (slash < 1 || slash >= str.length - 1) {\n    throw new InvalidBudgetError(str);\n  }\n  return {\n    limitMs: parseDuration(str.slice(0, slash)),\n    windowMs: parseDuration(str.slice(slash + 1)),\n  };\n}\n", "/**\n * Scheduled script card schema - declarative scheduling for commands.\n *\n * Scheduled scripts define what to run and when. They live in\n * config/schedules/ and are evaluated by `cb tick` (cron) and\n * `cb wakeup` (on-wakeup scripts).\n *\n * The filename stem is the identity (e.g., check-email.scheduled-script.card).\n */\n\nimport { cardSchema, type CardSchema } from \"cardworks\";\nimport { stringify as stringifyYaml } from \"yaml\";\nimport { z } from \"zod\";\nimport { CronExpressionParser } from \"cron-parser\";\nimport rrulePkg from \"rrule\";\nimport { parseDuration, parseBudget } from \"./scheduled-script-duration.js\";\nconst { rrulestr } = rrulePkg;\n\nexport {\n  InvalidDurationError,\n  UnknownDurationUnitError,\n  InvalidBudgetError,\n  parseDuration,\n  parseBudget,\n} from \"./scheduled-script-duration.js\";\n\n// ============================================\n// Schema\n// ============================================\n\nconst SourceField = z.union([\n  z.string(),\n  z.object({\n    text: z.string().optional(),\n    ref: z.string().optional(),\n  }),\n]);\n\nconst CreateAfterSuccessEntry = z.object({\n  path: z.string(),\n  args: z.record(z.string(), z.string()).optional(),\n});\n\nconst RequiresField = z.object({\n  connectors: z.array(z.string()).optional(),\n});\n\nexport const ScheduledScriptSchema: CardSchema = cardSchema(\"scheduled-script\", {\n  searchable: false,\n  fields: {\n    cron: z.string().optional(),\n    at: z.string().optional(),\n    rrule: z.string().optional(),\n    until: z.string().optional(),\n    \"not-before\": z.string().optional(),\n    \"on-wakeup\": z.boolean().optional(),\n    once: z.boolean().optional(),\n    enabled: z.boolean().optional(),\n    budget: z.string().optional(),\n    \"lock-group\": z.string().optional(),\n    timeout: z.string().optional(),\n    description: z.string().optional(),\n    runs: z.string(),\n    source: SourceField.optional(),\n    \"create-after-success\": z.array(CreateAfterSuccessEntry).optional(),\n    requires: RequiresField.optional(),\n  },\n  instructions: `# Scheduled Script Cards\n\nScheduled scripts define commands to run on a schedule. They live in \\`config/schedules/\\`.\n\n## Schedule Types (mutually exclusive)\n- **cron**: Standard cron expression (e.g., \\`0 6 * * *\\` for 6am daily)\n- **at**: ISO datetime for a one-shot future execution\n- **rrule**: iCalendar RRULE for complex recurrence patterns\n\n## Frontmatter Fields\n- **not-before**: Minimum time since last run. Prevents running more often than this interval even if the schedule says otherwise. Use duration strings: \\`5m\\`, \\`1h\\`, \\`4h\\`, \\`1d\\`.\n- **on-wakeup**: If \\`true\\`, also run opportunistically during \\`cb wakeup\\`, subject to not-before.\n- **once**: If \\`true\\`, the card is deleted after successful execution.\n- **until**: ISO datetime after which this schedule expires.\n- **enabled**: Set to \\`false\\` to disable without deleting.\n- **budget**: Max cumulative runtime within a window. Format: \\`\"LIMIT/WINDOW\"\\` (e.g., \\`\"10m/5h\"\\` = max 10 minutes of runtime in any 5-hour window). Scripts exceeding their budget are skipped until the window clears.\n- **lock-group**: Named concurrency group. Scripts sharing a lock-group won't run concurrently \u2014 if one is already running, others in the same group are skipped.\n- **timeout**: Max runtime for a single run, as a duration string (e.g. \\`25m\\`). Counts only awake time (machine sleep doesn't eat the budget). Default: \\`10m\\`. The run is killed when it exceeds this.\n- **runs**: The command to execute (required). Runs with cwd set to box root.\n- **description**: Human-readable summary of what this schedule does.\n- **source**: Why this schedule exists. Either a plain string, or \\`{text?, ref?}\\` to link to a related card.\n- **create-after-success**: Optional array of \\`{path, args?}\\` entries. Create a card at \\`path\\` after successful execution; \\`args\\` are template arguments. Skipped if the target file already exists.\n- **requires**: Optional \\`{connectors: [name, ...]}\\`. The schedule won't run if any required connector isn't configured for this box.\n\n## Guidelines\n- Set reasonable not-before values to prevent hammering external services.\n- Use on-wakeup for things that should happen whenever the agent is active.\n- For one-shot future tasks, combine \\`at\\` with \\`once: true\\`.`,\n});\n\n// ============================================\n// Field types (raw frontmatter shape)\n// ============================================\n\nexport interface ScheduledScriptFields {\n  type: \"scheduled-script\";\n  cron?: string;\n  at?: string;\n  rrule?: string;\n  until?: string;\n  \"not-before\"?: string;\n  \"on-wakeup\"?: boolean;\n  once?: boolean;\n  enabled?: boolean;\n  budget?: string;\n  \"lock-group\"?: string;\n  timeout?: string;\n  description?: string;\n  runs: string;\n  source?: string | { text?: string; ref?: string };\n  \"create-after-success\"?: Array<{ path: string; args?: Record<string, string> }>;\n  requires?: { connectors?: string[] };\n}\n\n// ============================================\n// Parsed scheduled script (computed/normalized)\n// ============================================\n\nexport interface ScheduleRequirements {\n  connectors: string[];\n}\n\nexport interface ParsedScheduledScript {\n  cron: string | undefined;\n  at: string | undefined;\n  rrule: string | undefined;\n  until: string | undefined;\n  notBefore: string | undefined;\n  onWakeup: boolean;\n  once: boolean;\n  enabled: boolean;\n  runs: string;\n  description: string | undefined;\n  source: { ref?: string; text?: string } | undefined;\n  createAfterSuccess: Array<{ path: string; args: Record<string, string> }>;\n  budget: { limitMs: number; windowMs: number } | undefined;\n  lockGroup: string | undefined;\n  timeoutMs: number | undefined;\n  requires: ScheduleRequirements | undefined;\n}\n\nfunction normalizeSource(src: ScheduledScriptFields[\"source\"]): { ref?: string; text?: string } | undefined {\n  if (src === undefined) return undefined;\n  if (typeof src === \"string\") return { text: src };\n  const out: { ref?: string; text?: string } = {};\n  if (src.ref !== undefined) out.ref = src.ref;\n  if (src.text !== undefined) out.text = src.text;\n  return out;\n}\n\n/**\n * Parse a scheduled-script fields object into a typed structure.\n */\nexport function parseScheduledScript(fields: ScheduledScriptFields): ParsedScheduledScript {\n  return {\n    cron: fields.cron,\n    at: fields.at,\n    rrule: fields.rrule,\n    until: fields.until,\n    notBefore: fields[\"not-before\"],\n    onWakeup: fields[\"on-wakeup\"] === true,\n    once: fields.once === true,\n    enabled: fields.enabled !== false,\n    runs: fields.runs,\n    description: fields.description,\n    source: normalizeSource(fields.source),\n    createAfterSuccess: (fields[\"create-after-success\"] ?? []).map((e) => ({\n      path: e.path,\n      args: e.args ?? {},\n    })),\n    budget: fields.budget !== undefined ? parseBudget(fields.budget) : undefined,\n    lockGroup: fields[\"lock-group\"],\n    timeoutMs: fields.timeout !== undefined ? parseDuration(fields.timeout) : undefined,\n    requires:\n      fields.requires?.connectors && fields.requires.connectors.length > 0\n        ? { connectors: fields.requires.connectors }\n        : undefined,\n  };\n}\n\n// ============================================\n// Schedule evaluation\n// ============================================\n\nexport interface ScheduleCheckContext {\n  lastRun: string | null;\n  now: Date;\n}\n\n/**\n * Check if a scheduled script is due to run.\n */\nexport function isDue(script: ParsedScheduledScript, ctx: ScheduleCheckContext): boolean {\n  if (!script.enabled) return false;\n\n  if (script.until) {\n    const untilDate = new Date(script.until);\n    if (ctx.now > untilDate) return false;\n  }\n\n  if (script.notBefore && ctx.lastRun) {\n    const minInterval = parseDuration(script.notBefore);\n    const elapsed = ctx.now.getTime() - new Date(ctx.lastRun).getTime();\n    if (elapsed < minInterval) return false;\n  }\n\n  if (script.cron) {\n    return isCronDue(script.cron, ctx);\n  }\n\n  if (script.at) {\n    const atDate = new Date(script.at);\n    return ctx.now >= atDate && !ctx.lastRun;\n  }\n\n  if (script.rrule) {\n    return isRruleDue(script.rrule, ctx);\n  }\n\n  return script.onWakeup;\n}\n\n/**\n * Check if a script should run during wakeup (on-wakeup check).\n * Only checks not-before constraint, not the cron/at/rrule schedule.\n */\nexport function isDueForWakeup(script: ParsedScheduledScript, ctx: ScheduleCheckContext): boolean {\n  if (!script.enabled) return false;\n  if (!script.onWakeup) return false;\n\n  if (script.until) {\n    const untilDate = new Date(script.until);\n    if (ctx.now > untilDate) return false;\n  }\n\n  if (script.notBefore && ctx.lastRun) {\n    const minInterval = parseDuration(script.notBefore);\n    const elapsed = ctx.now.getTime() - new Date(ctx.lastRun).getTime();\n    if (elapsed < minInterval) return false;\n  }\n\n  return true;\n}\n\n/**\n * Check if a script is within its runtime budget.\n * Returns true if the script is allowed to run (budget not exceeded).\n * Sums run durations within the budget window. Durations are awake\n * runtime (exec-with-timeout measures them sleep-free), so runs flagged\n * sleepAffected count like any other \u2014 the flag is informational.\n */\nexport function isWithinBudget(\n  budget: { limitMs: number; windowMs: number },\n  opts: { recentRuns: Array<{ ts: string; durationMs: number; sleepAffected?: boolean }> | undefined; now: Date },\n): { allowed: boolean; usedMs: number } {\n  const cutoff = opts.now.getTime() - budget.windowMs;\n  const runs = opts.recentRuns ?? [];\n  let usedMs = 0;\n  for (const r of runs) {\n    if (new Date(r.ts).getTime() >= cutoff) {\n      usedMs += r.durationMs;\n    }\n  }\n  return { allowed: usedMs < budget.limitMs, usedMs };\n}\n\nfunction isCronDue(cronExpr: string, ctx: ScheduleCheckContext): boolean {\n  try {\n    const interval = CronExpressionParser.parse(cronExpr, {\n      currentDate: ctx.now,\n    });\n    const prev = interval.prev().toDate();\n    if (!ctx.lastRun) {\n      return prev <= ctx.now;\n    }\n    return prev > new Date(ctx.lastRun);\n  } catch {\n    return false;\n  }\n}\n\nfunction isRruleDue(rruleStr: string, ctx: ScheduleCheckContext): boolean {\n  try {\n    const rule = rrulestr(rruleStr);\n    const after = ctx.lastRun ? new Date(ctx.lastRun) : new Date(0);\n    const occurrences = rule.between(after, ctx.now, false);\n    return occurrences.length > 0;\n  } catch {\n    return false;\n  }\n}\n\n// ============================================\n// Template\n// ============================================\n\nexport interface ScheduledScriptTemplateOptions {\n  cron?: string;\n  at?: string;\n  rrule?: string;\n  until?: string;\n  notBefore?: string;\n  onWakeup?: boolean;\n  once?: boolean;\n  enabled?: boolean;\n  runs: string;\n  description?: string;\n  source?: string;\n  sourceRef?: string;\n  createAfterSuccess?: Array<{ path: string; args: Record<string, string> }>;\n  budget?: string;\n  lockGroup?: string;\n  requires?: string[];\n}\n\n/**\n * Create a scheduled-script card template (YAML frontmatter + empty body).\n */\nexport [`--skip=${offset}`] : []),\n  ];\n\n  // ASCII record/field separators keep the format unambiguous against\n  // commit messages that contain newlines, colons, or arbitrary text.\n  const RS = \"\\u001E\";\n  const FS = \"\\u001F\";\n\n  let raw: string;\n  try {\n    raw = await git.raw([\n      \"log\",\n      ...grepArgs,\n      ...pageArgs,\n      `--format=${FS}%H${FS}%aI${FS}%s${FS}%b${RS}`,\n    ]);\n  } catch (_e) {\n    // A filtered log over a repo with no matching/any commits throws \u2014 an\n    // empty result set is the expected, non-error outcome here.\n    return [];\n  }\n\n  const entries: GitLogEntryExtended[] = [];\n  for (const record of raw.split(RS)) {\n    if (!record.trim()) continue;\n    const parts = record.split(FS);\n    if (parts.length < 5) continue;\n    const hash = parts[1]!.trim();\n    if (!/^[\\da-f]{40}$/.test(hash)) continue;\n    const body = parts[4]!.trim() || undefined;\n    const trailers = parseTrailersMulti(body);\n    entries.push({\n      hash,\n      date: parts[2]!.trim(),\n      subject: parts[3]!.trim(),\n      body,\n      trailers: Object.keys(trailers).length > 0 ? trailers : undefined,\n    });\n  }\n\n  // Stats fetch applies the same grep filter + pagination so the hashes\n  // line up with `entries`.\n  await attachFilteredStats(git, { logArgs: [...grepArgs, ...pageArgs], entries });\n\n  return entries;\n}\n", "/**\n * Canonical ordered list of box data migrations.\n *\n * `cb migrate` reads this and the per-box manifest at\n * `config/migrations.jsonl` to decide what to run. Each schema is a \\`.ts\\` file\nin \\`config/schemas/\\` that uses the same tools as built-in schemas.\n\n**Default to the frontmatter form** (\\`cardSchema\\`) shown below: it produces standard cards \u2014\nYAML frontmatter plus a markdown body. Reach for the legacy \\`element()\\` / XML form only when\nyour card needs Markdoc-shaped inline content (see the end of this guide).\n\n## Creating a Schema\n\nCreate a \\`.ts\\` file in \\`config/schemas/\\` that default-exports a \\`cardSchema()\\`:\n\n\\`\\`\\`typescript\nimport { body, cardSchema } from \"cardworks\";\nimport { z } from \"zod\";\n\nexport default cardSchema(\"my-type\", {\n  fields: {\n    status: z.enum([\"draft\", \"final\"]).default(\"draft\"),\n    priority: z.enum([\"low\", \"medium\", \"high\"]).optional(),\n    body: body(z.string()),  // omit this line if the card has no prose body\n  },\n  instructions: \\\\\\`# My Type Cards\n\nInstructions for the agent on how to handle this card type.\nThese appear in .claude/rules/ and docs/generated/, and are loaded\nwhen the agent reads or edits a matching card file.\\\\\\`,\n});\n\\`\\`\\`\n\nThe filename becomes the card type: \\`config/schemas/task.ts\\` \u2192 \\`*.task.card\\` files.\n\nOn disk, a card of this type is YAML frontmatter + markdown body:\n\n\\`\\`\\`\n---\nstatus: draft\npriority: high\n---\nThe markdown body (present only when the schema declares a \\`body\\` field).\n\\`\\`\\`\n\nKey patterns:\n- \\`cardSchema(type, { fields, instructions? })\\` is the entry point. \\`fields\\` is a flat object\n  of Zod validators; nest with \\`z.object\\` / \\`z.array\\` as needed.\n- \\`body(z.string())\\` declares the markdown body field \u2014 it must be named \\`body\\`. Omit it for a\n  body-less card (then any non-empty body errors on load).\n- \\`type\\` is the discriminator; don't list it under \\`fields\\`, and the on-disk YAML needn't carry\n  it \u2014 the filename \\`Foo.<type>.card\\` supplies it.\n- \\`title\\` and \\`contains\\` are available on every card type automatically.\n\n## Available Imports\n\nFrom \\`cardworks\\`:\n- \\`cardSchema(type, config)\\` \u2014 define a frontmatter card schema (the default)\n- \\`body(zodSchema)\\` \u2014 declare the single markdown body field\n- \\`element(tagName, config)\\` \u2014 define a legacy XML schema (see below)\n- \\`escapeText(str)\\` / \\`escapeAttr(str)\\` \u2014 XML-escape helpers (only for \\`element()\\` schemas)\n\nFrom \\`zod\\`:\n- \\`z\\` \u2014 Zod schema builder (z.string(), z.enum(), z.array(), etc.)\n\n## Optional: Templates\n\nExport a \\`template\\` to enable \\`cb create\\` for your card type. For frontmatter schemas,\n\\`generate\\` returns the card text \u2014 a YAML frontmatter block built with \\`stringify\\` from \\`yaml\\`:\n\n\\`\\`\\`typescript\nimport { cardSchema } from \"cardworks\";\nimport { stringify as stringifyYaml } from \"yaml\";\nimport { z } from \"zod\";\n\nexport const template = {\n  name: \"task\",\n  description: \"A task card\",\n  argsSchema: z.object({\n    title: z.string().describe(\"Task title\"),\n    priority: z.enum([\"low\", \"medium\", \"high\"]).optional().describe(\"Priority level\"),\n  }),\n  generate: (args: { title: string; priority?: string }) => {\n    const fields: Record<string, unknown> = { status: \"todo\", title: args.title };\n    if (args.priority !== undefined) fields.priority = args.priority;\n    return \"---\\\\n\" + stringifyYaml(fields) + \"---\\\\n\";\n  },\n  cardTypes: [\"task\"],\n  defaultForTypes: [\"task\"],\n};\n\nexport default cardSchema(\"task\", {\n  // ... schema definition\n});\n\\`\\`\\`\n\n## After Adding or Modifying Schemas\n\nRun \\`cb init\\` to regenerate rules and documentation:\n\n\\`\\`\\`bash\ncb init .\n\\`\\`\\`\n\nThis will:\n- Generate \\`.claude/rules/card-<type>.md\\` (if the schema has \\`instructions\\`)\n- Generate \\`docs/generated/card-<type>.md\\`\n- Register any templates for \\`cb create\\`\n\nSchema changes are picked up on the next \\`cb\\` invocation; a running dev server needs a restart.\n\n## Legacy: XML / \\`element()\\` schemas\n\nUse \\`element()\\` only when the card body is Markdoc-shaped inline content \u2014 nested, attributed\ninline structure that doesn't fit YAML frontmatter. This is why the built-in \\`guide\\` and\n\\`capture-session\\` types still use it. For everything else, prefer \\`cardSchema\\` above.\n\n\\`\\`\\`typescript\nimport { element } from \"cardworks\";\nimport { z } from \"zod\";\n\nexport default element(\"note\", {\n  attrs: {\n    status: z.enum([\"draft\", \"final\"]).default(\"draft\"),\n  },\n  children: z.array(z.unknown()),\n  instructions: \\\\\\`# Note Cards\n\nInstructions for the agent on how to handle this card type.\\\\\\`,\n});\n\\`\\`\\`\n\nA legacy template's \\`generate\\` emits XML instead of YAML, using \\`escapeText\\` / \\`escapeAttr\\` for\ninterpolated values. See the built-in XML schemas in callback-box's \\`src/schemas/\\` for examples.\n\n## Tips\n\n- Keep schema files focused \u2014 one card type per file\n- Always include \\`instructions\\` so the agent knows how to handle the card type\n- Test with \\`cb validate\\` after creating cards of the new type\n`;\n\nconst TRICKS_PACKAGE_JSON = JSON.stringify(\n  {\n    name: \"tricks\",\n    private: true,\n    type: \"module\",\n  },\n  null,\n  2\n) + \"\\n\";\n\nconst TRICKS_CLAUDE_MD = `# Writing Tricks\n\nTricks are custom TypeScript scripts that extend your box's capabilities.\nEach trick runs as a standalone subprocess via tsx with its own package context,\nso you can install and import npm packages.\n\n## Structure\n\nEach trick is a directory under \\`tricks/scripts/\\` with an \\`index.ts\\` entry point:\n\n\\`\\`\\`\ntricks/\n  package.json        <- npm dependencies for tricks\n  node_modules/       <- installed packages (gitignored)\n  lib/                <- Shared utilities (import with relative paths)\n  scripts/\n    CLAUDE.md         <- This file\n    clean-inbox/\n      index.ts        <- cb trick clean-inbox\n    summarize/\n      index.ts        <- cb trick summarize\n\\`\\`\\`\n\n**Every trick must be a directory** -- never put a \\`.ts\\` file directly in \\`tricks/scripts/\\`.\n\n## Script Interface\n\nTricks are standalone TypeScript programs. Environment variables provide context:\n\n- \\`CB_BOX_ROOT\\` -- absolute path to the box root\n- \\`CB_TRICK_NAME\\` -- the trick name (e.g. \"clean-inbox\"), useful for usage/help output\n- \\`process.argv.slice(2)\\` -- extra arguments after the trick name\n\n\\`\\`\\`typescript\nimport * as fs from \"node:fs/promises\";\nimport * as path from \"node:path\";\n\nexport const description = \"Short description shown in cb trick list\";\n\nconst boxRoot = process.env.CB_BOX_ROOT!;\nconst trickName = process.env.CB_TRICK_NAME!;\nconst args = process.argv.slice(2);\n\nconst inboxDir = path.join(boxRoot, \"box/inbox\");\nconsole.log(\"Done!\");\n\\`\\`\\`\n\nThe \\`export const description\\` line is parsed (not executed) by \\`cb trick\\` for the listing.\n\n## Running\n\n- \\`cb trick\\` -- list all tricks with descriptions\n- \\`cb trick <name>\\` -- run a trick\n- \\`cb trick <name> arg1 arg2\\` -- pass arguments\n\n## Dependencies\n\nInstall packages into the tricks directory:\n\n\\`\\`\\`bash\ncd tricks && pnpm add <package>\n\\`\\`\\`\n\nThese are available to all tricks via normal imports.\n\n## Shared Code\n\nPut reusable utilities in \\`tricks/lib/\\` and import them with relative paths:\n\n\\`\\`\\`typescript\nimport { helper } from \"../../lib/helper.js\";\n\\`\\`\\`\n\n## Tips\n\n- Use \\`node:fs/promises\\` and \\`node:path\\` for file operations\n- Tricks run via tsx as subprocesses -- no build step needed\n- Keep tricks focused on a single task\n- Use \\`cb\\` commands (via \\`child_process\\`) for card operations\n- The subprocess cwd is \\`tricks/\\`, so package resolution works naturally\n`;\n\nconst VIEWS_CLAUDE_MD = `# Views Directory\n\nThis directory contains agent-generated React components (.tsx files) that render in the browser.\n\n**IMPORTANT: Read \\`docs/generated/views.md\\` before creating or modifying views.** It documents the required file format, the ViewProps API, dependency globs, and embedding syntax. Do not guess the format \u2014 read the doc.\n\n## Quick Reference\n\nEach view must export:\n- \\`name\\` (string) \u2014 display name\n- \\`description\\` (string) \u2014 what the view shows\n- \\`dependencies\\` (string[]) \u2014 glob patterns for cards that affect rendering\n- \\`modes\\` (string[]) \u2014 \\`\"page\"\\`, \\`\"chat\"\\`, or both\n- \\`default\\` function component receiving \\`{ cards, navigate, boxSlug, params }\\`\n\nReact is provided automatically \u2014 do not import it.\n\nFull documentation: \\`docs/generated/views.md\\`\n`;\n\n/**\n * Install tricks scaffold files (package.json, CLAUDE.md) if they don't exist.\n */\nexport async function installTricksFiles(boxRoot: string): Promise<void> {\n  const packageJsonPath = path.join(boxRoot, \"tricks/package.json\");\n  try {\n    await fs.access(packageJsonPath);\n  } catch (_e) {\n    // No tricks package.json yet (fs.access throws ENOENT) \u2014 scaffold it.\n    // The error carries no actionable info; absence is the normal path.\n    await fs.mkdir(path.join(boxRoot, \"tricks\"), { recursive: true });\n    await fs.writeFile(packageJsonPath, TRICKS_PACKAGE_JSON);\n  }\n\n  const claudeMdPath = path.join(boxRoot, \"tricks/scripts/CLAUDE.md\");\n  try {\n    await fs.access(claudeMdPath);\n  } catch (_e) {\n    // No tricks CLAUDE.md yet (fs.access throws ENOENT) \u2014 scaffold it. The error\n    // carries no actionable info; absence is the normal path.\n    await fs.mkdir(path.join(boxRoot, \"views\"), { recursive: true });\n    await fs.writeFile(claudeMdPath, VIEWS_CLAUDE_MD);\n  }\n}\n", "/**\n * Shared logic for installing template-managed files into a box.\n *\n * The bookkeeping problem this solves: callback-box ships templates\n * (procedures, guides, schedules, the personality seed, the root\n * landmark, the briefing). When a template changes upstream, we want to\n * push the new version into boxes \u2014 but only if the local copy hasn't\n * been customised. Hashing the\n * normalized form makes \"did the user edit it\" comparison stable\n * across reinstalls that only differ in timestamp.\n */\n\nimport * as fs from \"node:fs/promises\";\nimport type { Dirent } from \"node:fs\";\nimport * as path from \"node:path\";\nimport { createHash } from \"node:crypto\";\n\nconst VERSIONS_FILE = \"config/template-versions.json\";\nconst TEMPLATE_UPDATES_DIR = \"config/_template-updates\";\n\ninterface VersionsFile {\n  [relPath: string]: {\n    /** sha256 of the (normalized) template content as we last installed it. */\n    sha256: string;\n    \"installed-at\": string;\n  };\n}\n\nexport interface InstallTemplateOptions {\n  /** Box root absolute path. */\n  boxRoot: string;\n  /** Path under boxRoot, e.g. `config/calendar.guide.card`. */\n  relPath: string;\n  /** New template content to install. */\n  templateContent: string;\n  /**\n   * Optional normalizer for content with volatile fields (timestamps).\n   * Both the local file and the template are normalized before hashing\n   * so timestamp-only differences don't read as \"user modified.\"\n   */\n  normalize?: (content: string) => string;\n  /**\n   * sha256 hashes (of the normalized content) of prior stock versions we\n   * shipped before this file was tracked in template-versions.json. A local\n   * file matching one of these is recognized as our own unmodified output and\n   * overwritten with the new template \u2014 the bootstrap path for files that were\n   * installed create-if-missing before adopting the tracker. When editing traits, **always rewrite the body** to reflect the\nupdated traits, experiments, and unresolved notes. friendly lilting tone\"],\n    },\n    tone: [\n      {\n        text: \"Young and genuinely curious \u2014 gets excited when it finds connections, asks \\\"why?\\\" because it actually wants to Used by `compileBriefing` and any other\n * server-side path that needs to render Markdoc-tagged bodies as\n * markdown.\n *\n * **Why not `Markdoc.format()`.** The upstream serializer has several\n * silent-data-loss and non-convergence bugs documented at\n * `docs/implemented-plans/markdoc-format-investigation.md`. Hand-rolling this emitter avoids\n * the whole class of problems by emitting only what we want to emit.\n *\n * **Module layout.** The recursive node walker lives in\n * `markdoc-emit-nodes.ts`; per-tag rendering for the briefing vocabulary\n * (`purpose`, `key-person`, `correction`, `property`, `project-phase`),\n * the recipe vocabulary, and the universal `quote`/`source` tags lives in\n * `markdoc-emit-tags.ts`. Tag names are the canonical\n * authored names (`quote`, `key-person`, etc.), not the post-transform\n * React-component names \u2014 that keeps this module Markdoc-config-aware\n * but not React-aware.\n */\n\nimport Markdoc from \"@markdoc/markdoc\";\n\nimport { emitNode } from \"./markdoc-emit-nodes.js\";\n\n// eslint-disable-next-line import-x/no-named-as-default-member\nconst { parse } = Markdoc;\n\n/**\n * Parse a markdown/Markdoc body and emit it as plain markdown text.\n * Output ends with a single trailing newline.\n */\nexport function emitBodyAsMarkdown(body: string): string {\n  if (body.trim() === \"\") return \"\";\n  const ast = parse(body);\n  const out: string[] = [];\n  emitNode(ast, out);\n  let text = out.join(\"\");\n  // Collapse runs of more than two consecutive newlines down to two.\n  text = text.replace(/\\n{3,}/g, \"\\n\\n\");\n  if (!text.endsWith(\"\\n\")) text += \"\\n\";\n  return text;\n}\n", "/**\n * Per-tag markdown emitters for the backend Markdoc \u2192 markdown emitter.\n *\n * Each tag emits a `**Label:** \u2026` form compatible with the shape the old\n * structured `compileBriefing` produced, so existing agent expectations are\n * preserved. Unknown tags emit their inner content with a stderr warning \u2014\n * the documented default: don't lose content silently.\n *\n * Split out of `markdoc-emit.ts` to keep that file under the line cap and to\n * isolate the (large, vocabulary-specific) tag switch from the core node\n * walker. To avoid a value-import cycle with the walker, the children-emitting\n * callback is passed in rather than imported.\n */\n\nimport type { Node } from \"@markdoc/markdoc\";\n\n/** Recursively emit a node's children \u2014 supplied by the core walker. */\nexport type EmitChildren = (node: Node, out: string[]) => void;\n\n/** Everything a per-tag emitter needs: the node, the output buffer, the walker. */\nexport interface TagCtx {\n  node: Node;\n  out: string[];\n  emitChildren: EmitChildren;\n}\n\n/**\n * Derive a short display name from a card ref. Used for `from=` and\n * `ref=` rendering when no explicit alias is supplied.\n *   `/box/people/dana.person.card` \u2192 \"dana\"\n *   `people/dana`                  \u2192 \"dana\"\n *   `Voice_2026-03-15.memo.card`   \u2192 \"Voice 2026-03-15\"\n */\nexport function displayFromRef(ref: string): string {\n  if (ref === \"\") return \"(missing)\";\n  const noFrag = ref.split(\"#\")[0] ?? ref;\n  const noLead = noFrag.replace(/^\\/+/, \"\");\n  const basename = noLead.includes(\"/\")\n    ? noLead.slice(noLead.lastIndexOf(\"/\") + 1)\n    : noLead;\n  const stripped = basename.replace(/\\.[^.]+\\.card$/, \"\");\n  const humanised = stripped.replace(/[_-]+/g, \" \").trim();\n  return humanised === \"\" ? ref : humanised;\n}\n\n/** Read a string attribute, defaulting to \"\". */\nfunction str(attrs: Record<string, unknown>, key: string): string {\n  return typeof attrs[key] === \"string\" ? attrs[key] : \"\";\n}\n\n/** Collect a node's children into trimmed text. */\nfunction childText(ctx: TagCtx): string {\n  const buf: string[] = [];\n  ctx.emitChildren(ctx.node, buf);\n  return buf.join(\"\").trim();\n}\n\n/**\n * Per-tag markdown emitters. Dispatches to one of three vocabulary groups\n * (universal, briefing, recipe); unknown tags fall back to \"emit inner\n * content + stderr warning\".\n */\nexport function emitTag(ctx: TagCtx): void {\n  if (emitUniversalTag(ctx)) return;\n  if (emitBriefingTag(ctx)) return;\n  if (emitRecipeTag(ctx)) return;\n  const { node, out } = ctx;\n  const tagName = node.tag === undefined ? \"(unnamed)\" : node.tag;\n  console.warn(`markdoc-emit: unknown tag {% ${tagName} %}; emitting inner content only`);\n  ctx.emitChildren(node, out);\n}\n\n/** Universal tags usable across vocabularies: `quote`, `source`. */\nfunction emitUniversalTag(ctx: TagCtx): boolean {\n  const { node, out } = ctx;\n  const attrs = node.attributes;\n  switch (node.tag) {\n    case \"quote\": {\n      // Markdown blockquote. Markdown can't capture the chip UI; the bracketed form is\n      // the closest representation.\n      const content = childText(ctx);\n      const ref = str(attrs, \"ref\");\n      const as = str(attrs, \"as\");\n      const cite = ref === \"\" ? called : displayFromRef(ref);\n      const desc = childText(ctx);\n      const refStr = ref === \"\" ? \"\" : ` [\u2192 ${ref}]`;\n      const roleStr = role === \"\" ? \"\" : ` \u2014 ${role}`;\n      const descStr = desc === \"\" ? \"\" : ` _(test: ${test})_`;\n      out.push(`**Correction:** ${text}${testStr}\\n\\n`);\n      return true;\n    }\n    case \"property\": {\n      const name = str(attrs, \"name\");\n      const address = str(attrs, \"address\");\n      const uncertain = attrs[\"address-uncertain\"] === true;\n      const heading = name !== \"\" ? name : (address !== \"\" ? address : \"(unnamed)\");\n      const addrStr = address !== \"\" && address !== name\n        ? ` \u2014 ${address}${uncertain ? \" (uncertain)\" : \"\"}`\n        : \"\";\n      const desc = childText(ctx);\n      const descStr = desc === \"\" ? \"\" : ` \u2014 ${desc}`;\n      out.push(`**Property:** **${heading}**${addrStr}${descStr}\\n\\n`);\n      return true;\n    }\n    case \"project-phase\": {\n      const date = str(attrs, \"date\");\n      const text = childText(ctx);\n      const dateStr = date === \"\" ? \"\" : ` (${date})`;\n      out.push(`**Current Phase**${dateStr}: ${text}\\n\\n`);\n      return true;\n    }\n    default:\n      return false;\n  }\n}\n\n/** Recipe-vocabulary tags: task, ingredient, step, yield, substitution, subrecipe, recipe-section. */\nfunction emitRecipeTag(ctx: TagCtx): boolean {\n  const { node, out } = ctx;\n  const attrs = node.attributes;\n  switch (node.tag) {\n    case \"task\": {\n      // GFM task checkbox. The Markdoc transform injects this for `[ ]`/`[x]`\n      // prefixes inside list items; in markdown the original form is exactly\n      // what we want.\n      const done = attrs[\"done\"] === true;\n      out.push(done ? \"[x] \" : \"[ ] \");\n      return true;\n    }\n    case \"ingredient\": {\n      const amount = str(attrs, \"amount\");\n      const unit = str(attrs, \"unit\");\n      const name = childText(ctx);\n      const qty = amount === \"\" ? \"\" : `${amount}${unit === \"\" ? \"\" : ` ${unit}`} `;\n      out.push(node.inline ? `**${qty}${name}**` : `- ${qty}${name}\\n`);\n      return true;\n    }\n    case \"step\":\n      out.push(`${childText(ctx)}\\n\\n`);\n      return true;\n    case \"yield\": {\n      const amount = str(attrs, \"amount\");\n      const text = childText(ctx);\n      const base = amount === \"\" ? \"\" : ` _(base ${amount})_`;\n      out.push(`**Yield:** ${text}${base}\\n\\n`);\n      return true;\n    }\n    case \"substitution\": {\n      const forAttr = str(attrs, \"for\");\n      const text = childText(ctx);\n      const forStr = forAttr === \"\" ? \"\" : ` _(for ${forAttr})_`;\n      out.push(`**Substitution${forStr}:** ${text}\\n\\n`);\n      return true;\n    }\n    case \"subrecipe\": {\n      const ref = str(attrs, \"ref\");\n      const text = childText(ctx);\n      out.push(`**Subrecipe:** [\u2192 ${ref}]${text === \"\" ? \"\" : ` \u2014 ${text}`}\\n\\n`);\n      return true;\n    }\n    case \"recipe-section\": {\n      const name = str(attrs, \"name\");\n      if (name !== \"\") out.push(`## ${name}\\n\\n`);\n      ctx.emitChildren(node, out);\n      return true;\n    }\n    default:\n      return false;\n  }\n}\n", "/**\n * Core Markdoc AST \u2192 markdown node walker for the backend emitter.\n *\n * Split out of `markdoc-emit.ts` to keep that file under the line cap. Holds\n * the recursive `emitNode`/`emitChildren` pair plus the block-level helpers\n * (`emitItemChildren`, `emitBlockquote`). Tag rendering lives in the sibling\n * `markdoc-emit-tags.ts`; the walker hands its `emitChildren` to `emitTag` so\n * tag emitters can recurse without a value-import cycle back into this module.\n */\n\nimport type { Node } from \"@markdoc/markdoc\";\n\nimport { emitTag } from \"./markdoc-emit-tags.js\";\n\nexport function emitNode(node: Node, out: string[]): void {\n  if (emitBlockNode(node, out)) return;\n  if (emitInlineNode(node, out)) return;\n  switch (node.type) {\n    case \"inline\":\n      emitChildren(node, out);\n      return;\n    case \"tag\":\n      emitTag({ node, out, emitChildren });\n      return;\n    default:\n      // Tables, html, comments, anything else \u2014 emit children as a graceful\n      // fallback. Briefing bodies aren't expected to use these constructs;\n      // if a card relies on one and it doesn't render, that's a finding for\n      // a future iteration.\n      emitChildren(node, out);\n      return;\n  }\n}\n\n/** Block-level node types. Returns true if handled. */\nfunction emitBlockNode(node: Node, out: string[]): boolean {\n  switch (node.type) {\n    case \"document\":\n      emitChildren(node, out);\n      return true;\n    case \"paragraph\":\n      emitChildren(node, out);\n      out.push(\"\\n\\n\");\n      return true;\n    case \"heading\": {\n      const level = typeof node.attributes[\"level\"] === \"number\" ? node.attributes[\"level\"] : 1;\n      out.push(`${\"#\".repeat(level)} `);\n      emitChildren(node, out);\n      out.push(\"\\n\\n\");\n      return true;\n    }\n    case \"list\":\n      emitList(node, out);\n      return true;\n    case \"item\":\n      // Handled by parent `list`; bare items emit their content with no marker.\n      emitItemChildren(node, out);\n      return true;\n    case \"blockquote\":\n      emitBlockquote(node, out);\n      return true;\n    case \"fence\":\n      emitFence(node, out);\n      return true;\n    case \"hr\":\n      out.push(\"---\\n\\n\");\n      return true;\n    case \"hardbreak\":\n      out.push(\"\\\\\\n\");\n      return true;\n    case \"softbreak\":\n      out.push(\"\\n\");\n      return true;\n    default:\n      return false;\n  }\n}\n\n/** Inline/span node types. Returns true if handled. */\nfunction emitInlineNode(node: Node, out: string[]): boolean {\n  switch (node.type) {\n    case \"text\": {\n      const content = node.attributes[\"content\"];\n      if (typeof content === \"string\") out.push(content);\n      return true;\n    }\n    case \"strong\":\n      out.push(\"**\");\n      emitChildren(node, out);\n      out.push(\"**\");\n      return true;\n    case \"em\":\n      out.push(\"*\");\n      emitChildren(node, out);\n      out.push(\"*\");\n      return true;\n    case \"s\":\n      out.push(\"~~\");\n      emitChildren(node, out);\n      out.push(\"~~\");\n      return true;\n    case \"code\": {\n      const content = node.attributes[\"content\"];\n      if (typeof content === \"string\") out.push(\"`\" + content + \"`\");\n      return true;\n    }\n    case \"link\": {\n      const href = typeof node.attributes[\"href\"] === \"string\" ? node.attributes[\"href\"] : \"\";\n      out.push(\"[\");\n      emitChildren(node, out);\n      out.push(`](${href})`);\n      return true;\n    }\n    case \"image\": {\n      const src = typeof node.attributes[\"src\"] === \"string\" ? node.attributes[\"src\"] : \"\";\n      const alt = typeof node.attributes[\"alt\"] === \"string\" ? node.attributes[\"alt\"] : \"\";\n      out.push(`![${alt}](${src})`);\n      return true;\n    }\n    default:\n      return false;\n  }\n}\n\nfunction emitList(node: Node, out: string[]): void {\n  const ordered = node.attributes[\"ordered\"] === true;\n  let index = 1;\n  for (const item of node.children) {\n    if (item.type !== \"item\") continue;\n    out.push(ordered ? `${index}. ` : \"- \");\n    index++;\n    emitItemChildren(item, out);\n    out.push(\"\\n\");\n  }\n  out.push(\"\\n\");\n}\n\nfunction emitFence(node: Node, out: string[]): void {\n  const content = typeof node.attributes[\"content\"] === \"string\"\n    ? node.attributes[\"content\"]\n    : \"\";\n  // Markdoc parses the fence's first-line argument string as `language`;\n  // the full info-string isn't preserved separately, so we emit just the\n  // language token. Bodies that need post-fence args (e.g. `ts setup`)\n  // can't be round-tripped through here \u2014 same limitation as `format()`.\n  const lang = typeof node.attributes[\"language\"] === \"string\"\n    ? node.attributes[\"language\"]\n    : \"\";\n  out.push(\"```\" + lang + \"\\n\");\n  out.push(content);\n  if (!content.endsWith(\"\\n\")) out.push(\"\\n\");\n  out.push(\"```\\n\\n\");\n}\n\nexport function emitChildren(node: Node, out: string[]): void {\n  for (const child of node.children) emitNode(child, out);\n}\n\n/** Emit a list item's children inline (no marker \u2014 parent emits that). */\nfunction emitItemChildren(item: Node, out: string[]): void {\n  // Items usually contain a single paragraph plus optional nested lists.\n  // Emit paragraph content inline (no trailing blank line); nested lists\n  // get indented.\n  for (const child of item.children) {\n    if (child.type === \"paragraph\") {\n      emitChildren(child, out);\n    } else if (child.type === \"list\") {\n      const buf: string[] = [];\n      emitNode(child, buf);\n      const indented = buf.join(\"\").trimEnd().split(\"\\n\").map((line) => \"  \" + line).join(\"\\n\");\n      out.push(\"\\n\" + indented);\n    } else {\n      emitNode(child, out);\n    }\n  }\n}\n\nfunction emitBlockquote(node: Node, out: string[]): void {\n  const buf: string[] = [];\n  emitChildren(node, buf);\n  const text = buf.join(\"\").trimEnd();\n  for (const line of text.split(\"\\n\")) {\n    out.push(line === \"\" ? \">\\n\" : `> ${line}\\n`);\n  }\n  out.push(\"\\n\");\n}\n", "/**\n * Landmark card schema \u2014 a hand-curated bookmark for a directory.\n *\n * One landmark per directory; the file lives inside the directory it\n * describes (e.g. `store/recipes/Recipes.landmark.card`). A landmark is\n * pure structured metadata (YAML frontmatter, no body) carrying one or\n * more *roles*:\n *\n *   ---\n *   navigation:                      # human-facing surface\n *     label: Recipes\n *     symbol: \uD83C\uDF73\n *     links:\n *       - { ref: Bread.recipe.card, label: the bread }\n *     expand:\n *       - { query: \"*.recipe.card\", order: modified-desc }\n *   destinations:                    # filing targets\n *     - for: [triage]\n *       rules: \"Recipes \u2014 anything describing how to cook a dish.\"\n *       procedure-ref: archive-recipe.procedure.card\n *   ---\n *\n * At least one role should be present; a landmark with neither is inert.\n * See docs/landmarks.md and docs/plans/triage-design.md.\n */\n\nimport { splitCardContent, cardSchema, type CardSchema } from \"cardworks\";\nimport { parse as parseYaml, stringify as stringifyYaml } from \"yaml\";\nimport { z } from \"zod\";\n\n/** Sort order for `expand` fan-out results. */\nexport const LandmarkOrder = z.enum([\"alphabetical\", \"modified-desc\", \"modified-asc\"]);\nexport type LandmarkOrderType = z.infer<typeof LandmarkOrder>;\n\n/**\n * The iconic mark for a landmark. Either an emoji / short text, or an\n * image (`{ src }`, a path relative to the landmark's directory).\n */\nexport const LandmarkSymbol = z.union([z.string(), z.object({ src: z.string() })]);\nexport type LandmarkSymbolData = z.infer<typeof LandmarkSymbol>;\n\n/**\n * A pinned reference to another card. `ref` is a literal path relative to\n * the landmark's directory, validated like any other ref. `label` is an\n * optional display label (falls back to the target's filename title).\n */\nexport const LandmarkLink = z.object({\n  ref: z.string(),\n  label: z.string().optional(),\n});\nexport type LandmarkLinkData = z.infer<typeof LandmarkLink>;\n\n/**\n * Templated fan-out. Runs `query` (a glob, relative to the landmark's\n * directory) and emits one link per match.\n *\n * `template-ref` / `template-label` are placeholder strings substituted\n * per match: `${path}` is the matched card's path (relative to the\n * landmark dir); any other `${field}` reads that field from the matched\n * card's frontmatter (dotted paths allowed, e.g. `${exif.camera}`).\n * When omitted, `template-ref` defaults to `${path}`.\n */\nexport const LandmarkExpand = z.object({\n  query: z.string(),\n  order: LandmarkOrder.optional(),\n  \"template-ref\": z.string().optional(),\n  \"template-label\": z.string().optional(),\n});\nexport type LandmarkExpandData = z.infer<typeof LandmarkExpand>;\n\n/**\n * Chat-feature seed for chats opened from this landmark. Each key is a\n * feature name; only applied at session open.\n */\nexport const LandmarkChatApp = z.object({\n  narration: z.enum([\"on\", \"off\"]).optional(),\n  prose: z.enum([\"on\", \"off\"]).optional(),\n});\nexport type LandmarkChatAppData = z.infer<typeof LandmarkChatApp>;\n\n/**\n * Human-facing navigation role: the bookmark surface shown on the\n * Landmarks page.\n */\nexport const LandmarkNavigation = z.object({\n  label: z.string().optional(),\n  symbol: LandmarkSymbol.optional(),\n  links: z.array(LandmarkLink).optional(),\n  expand: z.array(LandmarkExpand).optional(),\n  \"chat-app\": LandmarkChatApp.optional(),\n});\nexport type LandmarkNavigationData = z.infer<typeof LandmarkNavigation>;\n\n/**\n * Filing-target role: marks the landmark's directory as a destination for\n * one or more *kinds* of content. `for` lists the kinds (e.g. `triage`,\n * `commentary`). `rules`/`procedure-ref` are only meaningful when `for`\n * includes `triage`.\n */\nexport const LandmarkDestination = z.object({\n  for: z.array(z.string()),\n  rules: z.string().optional(),\n  \"procedure-ref\": z.string().optional(),\n});\nexport type LandmarkDestinationData = z.infer<typeof LandmarkDestination>;\n\nconst landmarkFields = {\n  navigation: LandmarkNavigation.optional(),\n  destinations: z.array(LandmarkDestination).optional(),\n};\n\n/**\n * Standalone object schema for the landmark frontmatter, used by\n * lightweight readers (the landmarks router, triage-instructions, etc.)\n * that parse a landmark file directly rather than through the card\n * loader.
