One per directory; the file lives inside the directory it describes, e.g. \\`store/recipes/Recipes.landmark.card\\`. Directories without a landmark are invisible to the Landmarks page and to triage.\n\nA landmark is pure YAML frontmatter (no body) with one or more roles. At least one role should be present.\n\n## \\`navigation\\` (human-facing surface)\n\n\\`\\`\\`yaml\nnavigation:\n  label: Recipes            # short bookmark name; treat like a tab name, not a sentence\n  symbol: \uD83C\uDF73                # emoji/short text, OR { src: images/portrait.webp } for an image\n  links:                    # optional curated links to other cards\n    - ref: Bread.recipe.card  # literal path relative to the landmark's directory; validated\n      label: the bread        # optional; falls back to the target's filename title\n  expand:                   # optional templated fan-out\n    - query: \"*.recipe.card\"  # glob, like cb ls\n      order: modified-desc    # alphabetical (default) | modified-desc | modified-asc\n  chat-app:                 # optional chat-feature seed for chats opened here\n    narration: \"on\"\n    prose: \"off\"\n\\`\\`\\`\n\nIn an \\`expand\\`, \\`template-ref\\` / \\`template-label\\` are placeholder strings substituted per match: \\`\\${path}\\` is the matched card's path, any other \\`\\${field}\\` reads that field from the matched card's frontmatter. When omitted, \\`template-ref\\` defaults to \\`\\${path}\\`.\n\n**Don't add a description or purpose field.** A bookmark seen many times shouldn't carry a paragraph explaining itself. If a landmark genuinely needs prose, write a doc card and link to it.\n\n## \\`destinations\\` (agent-facing filing targets)\n\n\\`\\`\\`yaml\ndestinations:\n  - for: [triage]           # kinds: triage (inbox\u2192triage routing target) and/or commentary\n    rules: \"Recipes \u2014 anything describing how to cook a dish.\"  # read by the triage agent\n    procedure-ref: archive-recipe.procedure.card                # handler run at the handle stage\n  - for: [commentary]       # a commentary-only spot needs neither rules nor procedure-ref\n\\`\\`\\`\n\nA pure routing target (an archive humans don't browse) can have only \\`destinations\\`; a pure bookmark can have only \\`navigation\\`.\n\n**Dedup**: a card appearing in both a hand-listed \\`links\\` entry and an \\`expand\\` result shows once \u2014 hand-listed links come first.`,\n});\n\nexport type Landmark = LandmarkFields;\n\n/**\n * Parse a landmark card's raw text into its typed frontmatter, or null if\n * it has no frontmatter or fails validation. Used by readers that scan\n * landmark files directly (the landmarks router, triage-instructions,\n * list-destinations, feature seeds) instead of going through the card\n * loader.\n */\nexport function parseLandmarkFields(content: string): LandmarkFields | null {\n  const split = splitCardContent(content);\n  if (!split.hasFrontmatter) return null;\n  let fm: unknown;\n  try {\n    fm = parseYaml(split.frontmatterText);\n  } catch (_e) {\n    return null;\n  }\n  const parsed = LandmarkObject.safeParse(fm ?? {});\n  if (!parsed.success) return null;\n  return parsed.data;\n}\n\n/**\n * Template for `cb create` \u2014 produces a starter landmark with a\n * `navigation` role containing label + symbol.\n *\n * Pass `symbol` for an emoji/text symbol, or `symbolSrc` for an image\n * path (relative to the landmark's directory).\n */\nexport function createLandmarkTemplate(options: {\n  label: string;\n  symbol?: string;\n  symbolSrc?: string;\n}): string {\n  const navigation: Record<string, unknown> = { label: options.label };\n  if (typeof options.symbolSrc === \"string\" && options.symbolSrc !== \"\") {\n    navigation.symbol = { src: options.symbolSrc };\n  } else if (typeof options.symbol === \"string\" && options.symbol !== \"\") {\n    navigation.symbol = options.symbol;\n  }\n  const yamlText = stringifyYaml({ navigation });\n  return `---\\n${yamlText}---\\n`;\n}\n", "/**\n * Absolute path to the callback-box package root.\n *\n * Resolved by walking up from this module's location until we find the\n * `callback-box` package.json. This is bundle-safe: under tsx this module\n * lives at `src/lib/`, and in the esbuild bundle it lives at `dist/`, but\n * either way the upward walk lands on the same package root \u2014 so callers\n * can build paths to `bin/`, `templates/`, `tsconfig.json`, etc. without\n * hard-coding a `../..` depth that only holds for one source layout.\n *\n * Prefer this over `import.meta.dirname` + `../..` for anything that points\n * at a fixed asset relative to the package root.\n */\nimport { existsSync, readFileSync } from \"node:fs\";\nimport { dirname, join } from \"node:path\";\n\nclass PackageRootNotFoundError extends Error {\n  constructor() {\n    super(\"package-root: could not locate the callback-box package root\");\n    this.name = \"PackageRootNotFoundError\";\n  }\n}\n\nfunction findPackageRoot(): string {\n  let dir = import.meta.dirname;\n  for (;;) {\n    const pkgPath = join(dir, \"package.json\");\n    if (existsSync(pkgPath)) {\n      try {\n        const pkg = JSON.parse(readFileSync(pkgPath, \"utf-8\"));\n        if (pkg.name === \"callback-box\") return dir;\n      } catch (_e) {\n        // Unparseable package.json \u2014 keep walking up.\n      }\n    }\n    const parent = dirname(dir);\n    if (parent === dir) {\n      throw new PackageRootNotFoundError();\n    }\n    dir = parent;\n  }\n}\n\nexport const PACKAGE_ROOT = findPackageRoot();\n", "/**\n * Generate `.claude/rules/` files from card schemas and connector-specific\n * file rules. Each card type with `instructions` gets a rule file that\n * auto-loads when an agent reads or edits a matching card file. Connector\n * rules cover non-card files (e.g. `.ics`).\n *\n * Called from `cb init`. Not a standalone CLI command \u2014 invoke `cb init`\n * to regenerate rules in a box.\n */\n\nimport { join } from \"node:path\";\nimport { mkdir, writeFile, readdir, unlink } from \"node:fs/promises\";\nimport { schemas, cardSchemas, loadBoxSchemas } from \"../schemas/registry.js\";\n\nexport interface ConnectorRule {\n  /** Rule filename without .md extension, e.g. \"connector-calendar\" */\n  name: string;\n  /** Glob patterns for paths: frontmatter */\n  paths: string[];\n  /** Instructions content */\n  instructions: string;\n}\n\n/**\n * Static connector rules for non-card file types.\n */\nexport const connectorRules: ConnectorRule[] = [\n  {\n    name: \"connector-calendar\",\n    paths: [\"store/calendar/**/*.ics\"],\n    instructions: `# Calendar Event Files (.ics)\n\nThese are Google Calendar events synced via \\`cb wakeup\\`. Each file is a single VEVENT in iCalendar format.\n\n## Key properties\n\nStandard iCalendar: SUMMARY, DESCRIPTION, LOCATION, DTSTART, DTEND, STATUS, TRANSP (OPAQUE=busy, TRANSPARENT=free).\n\nCustom properties track the source calendar:\n- \\`X-CB-CALENDAR-ID\\` \u2014 the Google Calendar ID this event belongs to\n- \\`X-CB-CALENDAR-NAME\\` \u2014 display name of the calendar\n- \\`X-CB-CALENDAR-ROLE\\` \u2014 access role: \\`owner\\`, \\`writer\\`, or \\`reader\\`\n\n## Editability\n\n- **owner/writer calendars**: You can edit the event fields (summary, description, location, times, transparency). Modified .ics files are pushed back to Google Calendar on the next \\`cb wakeup\\`.\n- **reader calendars**: These are subscribed/read-only calendars (e.g. school calendars). Do NOT edit these files \u2014 changes cannot be synced back.\n- **Events organized by others on your own calendar**: You can generally only change your own attendee response (PARTSTAT), not the event details.\n\n## Filename format\n\n\\`{YYYY-MM-DD}_{shortId}.ics\\` \u2014 the date is the event start date, shortId is derived from the Google event ID.\n\n## Querying\n\nUse \\`cb calendar today\\`, \\`cb calendar upcoming\\`, or \\`cb calendar <timespan>\\` (e.g. \\`cb calendar 2w\\`) to query events from the CLI. These read from the local .ics files \u2014 no API calls needed.`,\n  },\n];\n\n/**\n * Generate rules files from schema instructions and connector rules.\n *\n * Called by `cb init`.\n */\nexport async function generateRules(boxRoot: string): Promise<string[]> {\n  const rulesDir = join(boxRoot, \".claude\", \"rules\");\n  await mkdir(rulesDir, { recursive: true });\n\n  // Clean up old generated rules (card-* and connector-*)\n  try {\n    const existing = await readdir(rulesDir);\n    for (const file of existing) {\n      if (\n        (file.startsWith(\"card-\") || file.startsWith(\"connector-\")) &&\n        file.endsWith(\".md\")\n      ) {\n        await unlink(join(rulesDir, file));\n      }\n    }\n  } catch (e) {\n    // Directory may not exist yet, that's fine \u2014 nothing to clean up.\n    if ((e as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code !== \"ENOENT\") {\n      console.debug(\"Skipping old-rule cleanup (rules dir not readable):\", e);\n    }\n  }\n\n  const generated: string[] = [];\n\n  // Load box-local schemas alongside built-in ones. ...cardSchemas.map(s => s.type),\n  ];\n}\n\n/**\n * Get the card types that belong in content search indexes \u2014 every type\n * whose schema doesn't set `searchable: false`. Refs to children use the \\`attach/\\` virtual prefix.\n\nFrontmatter:\n- \\`status\\` \u2014 new \u2192 transcribing \u2192 transcribed (audio done) \u2192 intake-complete (images described, timeline assembled) \u2192 extracted (records pulled into a catalog directory).\n- \\`session-id\\` \u2014 links back to the capture API.\n- \\`time\\` \u2014 \\`{ start, end?, duration? }\\`.\n- \\`images\\` / \\`audio-clips\\` / \\`files\\` \u2014 manifests of the child card refs.\n\nBody \u2014 the assembled transcript, a timeline of transcribed speech interleaved with:\n- \\`{% image ref=\"photo-001.image.card\" /%}\\` \u2014 where a photo was taken (description/filename come from the referenced image card).\n- \\`{% silence duration=\"15s\" /%}\\` \u2014 gaps of 10+ seconds.\n\nThe transcript is generated by \\`assemble-timeline\\`; agents read it to extract records but shouldn't usually hand-edit it.`,\n});\n\n/** Frontmatter-only object schema (the body field lives outside Zod). */\nconst CaptureSessionObject = z.object({\n  status: CaptureSessionStatus.default(\"new\"),\n  \"session-id\": z.string(),\n  time: SessionTime.optional(),\n  images: z.array(z.string()).optional(),\n  \"audio-clips\": z.array(z.string()).optional(),\n  files: z.array(z.string()).optional(),\n});\nexport type CaptureSessionFrontmatter = z.infer<typeof CaptureSessionObject>;\n/** Back-compat alias. */\nexport type CaptureSession = CaptureSessionFrontmatter;\n\n/**\n * A capture session's parsed frontmatter plus its raw transcript body, or\n * null if the text has no frontmatter / fails validation. Used by the\n * timeline assembler and other readers that work with the card directly.\n */\nexport interface ParsedCaptureSession {\n  frontmatter: CaptureSessionFrontmatter;\n  body: string;\n}\n\nexport function parseCaptureSession(content: string): ParsedCaptureSession | null {\n  const split = splitCardContent(content);\n  if (!split.hasFrontmatter) return null;\n  let fm: unknown;\n  try {\n    fm = parseYaml(split.frontmatterText);\n  } catch (_e) {\n    return null;\n  }\n  const parsed = CaptureSessionObject.safeParse(fm ?? {});\n  if (!parsed.success) return null;\n  return { frontmatter: parsed.data, body: split.body };\n}\n\n/**\n * Template for creating a capture session card \u2014 frontmatter manifests with\n * an empty transcript body (filled in later by `assemble-timeline`).\n *\n * `imageRefs`, `audioRefs`, `fileRefs` are bare child-card filenames\n * (e.g. `photo-001.image.card`). They're emitted with the `attach/` virtual\n * prefix, pointing into the session's attach scope.\n */\nexport function createCaptureSessionTemplate(options: {\n  sessionId: string;\n  startedAt: string;\n  endedAt?: string | null;\n  imageRefs: string[];\n  audioRefs: string[];\n  fileRefs?: string[];\n}): string {\n  const duration = options.endedAt\n    ? formatDuration(new Date(options.endedAt).getTime() - new Date(options.startedAt).getTime())\n    : undefined;\n\n  const time: Record<string, string> = { start: options.startedAt };\n  if (options.endedAt) time.end = options.endedAt;\n  if (duration !== undefined) time.duration = duration;\n\n  const fields: Record<string, unknown> = {\n    status: \"new\",\n    \"session-id\": options.sessionId,\n    time,\n    images: options.imageRefs.map((ref) => `attach/${ref}`),\n    \"audio-clips\": options.audioRefs.map((ref) => `attach/${ref}`),\n  };\n  const fileRefs = options.fileRefs ?? [];\n  if (fileRefs.length > 0) fields.files = fileRefs.map((ref) => `attach/${ref}`);\n\n  return `---\\n${stringifyYaml(fields)}---\\n`;\n}\n\n/**\n * Format a duration in milliseconds to a human-readable string like \"4m2s\" or \"1h15m\".\n */\nfunction formatDuration(ms: number): string {\n  const totalSeconds = Math.floor(ms / 1000);\n  const hours = Math.floor(totalSeconds / 3600);\n  const minutes = Math.floor((totalSeconds % 3600) / 60);\n  const seconds = totalSeconds % 60;\n  if (hours > 0) {\n    return minutes > 0 ? `${hours}h${minutes}m` : `${hours}h`;\n  }\n  if (minutes > 0) {\n    return seconds > 0 ? `${minutes}m${seconds}s` : `${minutes}m`;\n  }\n  return `${seconds}s`;\n}\n", "/**\n * Record card schema \u2014 generic extracted units from capture sessions.\n *\n * Records are domain-flexible: a home inventory item, an archived document,\n * a recipe, a contact \u2014 whatever discrete thing was captured. The card's\n * markdown body is the textual content of the record (a document body, a\n * letter, recipe instructions) \u2014 empty when the record represents\n * something with no textual content (e.g., a couch).\n */\n\nimport { body, cardSchema, type CardSchema } from \"cardworks\";\nimport { stringify as stringifyYaml } from \"yaml\";\nimport { z } from \"zod\";\n\nexport const RecordStatus = z.enum([\"draft\", \"reviewed\", \"archived\"]);\nexport type RecordStatus = z.infer<typeof RecordStatus>;\n\nconst SourceEntry = z.object({\n  ref: z.string(),\n  time: z.string().optional(),\n  note: z.string().optional(),\n});\n\nconst DateEntry = z.object({\n  value: z.string(),\n  note: z.string().optional(),\n});\n\nconst PersonEntry = z.object({\n  name: z.string(),\n  ref: z.string().optional(),\n  role: z.string().optional(),\n  notes: z.string().optional(),\n  note: z.string().optional(),\n});\n\nconst LocationEntry = z.object({\n  text: z.string().optional(),\n  ref: z.string().optional(),\n});\n\nconst MeasureEntry = z.object({\n  value: z.string(),\n  note: z.string().optional(),\n});\n\nexport const RecordSchema: CardSchema = cardSchema(\"record\", {\n  fields: {\n    status: RecordStatus.default(\"draft\"),\n    name: z.string(),\n    description: z.string().optional(),\n    sources: z.array(SourceEntry).optional(),\n    dates: z.array(DateEntry).optional(),\n    persons: z.array(PersonEntry).optional(),\n    location: LocationEntry.optional(),\n    measures: z.array(MeasureEntry).optional(),\n    language: z.string().optional(),\n    triage: z.string().optional(),\n    notes: z.string().optional(),\n    body: body(z.string()),\n  },\n  instructions: `# Record Cards\n\nRecords are generic extracted units \u2014 discrete things pulled from\ncapture sessions or other sources. A record might be a home inventory\nitem, an archived document, a recipe, a contact, or any other\nidentifiable thing.\n\n## Frontmatter fields\n\n- \\`name:\\` \u2014 Always present. Use **absolute paths** for refs\n  (starting with /, e.g.\n  \\`/box/inbox/capture-.../session.capture-session.card\\`). The\n  optional \\`time\\` pinpoints a moment in a transcript. Where the thing is, was, or\n  relates to.\n- \\`measures:\\` \u2014 Array of \\`{value, note?}\\`. Natural language with\n  number and unit together: \\`\"2 pages\"\\`, \\`\"7 feet\"\\`, \\`\"1200 USD\"\\`.\n- \\`language:\\` \u2014 Only include when notable.\n- \\`triage:\\` \u2014 Only used when a triage procedure is active.\n- \\`notes:\\` \u2014 Anything that doesn't fit elsewhere \u2014 observations,\n  caveats, follow-up items.\n\n## Body (markdown)\n\nThe actual textual content of the record \u2014 a document body, recipe\ninstructions, letter text, etc. Empty when the record represents\nsomething with no textual content.\n\n## Guidelines\n\nUse only fields that are appropriate for the domain. The two are intentionally\n * separate card types so triage code that globs `*.email-message.card`\n * doesn't pick up an outbound draft and try to process it like a\n * received email.\n *\n * Example (reply draft):\n *\n *   ---\n *   type: email-outbound\n *   status: draft\n *   to: alice@example.com\n *   subject: Re Weekend plans\n *   in-reply-to:\n *     ref: msg-001.email-message.card\n *   ---\n *   Sounds good \u2014 let's meet at 11.\n *\n *   We can do the usual place.\n */\n\nimport { body, cardSchema, type CardSchema } from \"cardworks\";\nimport { stringify as stringifyYaml } from \"yaml\";\nimport { z } from \"zod\";\n\nexport const EmailOutboundSchema: CardSchema = cardSchema(\"email-outbound\", {\n  fields: {\n    status: z.enum([\"draft\", \"sent\"]).default(\"draft\"),\n    to: z.string(),\n    cc: z.string().optional(),\n    bcc: z.string().optional(),\n    subject: z.string(),\n    \"in-reply-to\": z.object({ ref: z.string() }).optional(),\n    \"gmail-draft-id\": z.string().optional(),\n    \"gmail-draft-url\": z.string().optional(),\n    body: body(z.string()),\n  },\n  instructions: `# Authoring Outbound Emails\n\nYou compose an email by writing an \\`email-outbound\\` card. Headers live\nin the YAML frontmatter; the message body is the markdown body of the\ncard. The Gmail connector picks the card up on the next sync and\ncreates a Gmail draft for the user to review and send.\n\n## Required fields (frontmatter)\n\n- \\`to:\\` \u2014 recipient address(es), comma-separated\n- \\`subject:\\` \u2014 subject line. For replies, prefix with \\`Re:\\` to match\n  the source thread's subject.\n\nThe card's body is the email body. Markdown subset only:\n\\`**bold**\\`, \\`*italic*\\`, \\`[text](url)\\`. Nothing else.\n\n## Optional fields\n\n- \\`cc:\\` and \\`bcc:\\` \u2014 additional recipients\n- \\`in-reply-to.ref:\\` \u2014 for replies, points at the source\n  \\`email-message\\` card. Use a path **relative to the draft's\n  directory** (typically just \\`msg-NNN.email-message.card\\` since the\n  draft sits in the same thread directory). The connector reads the\n  source card's \\`message-id\\` and \\`thread-id\\` to set Gmail threading\n  headers \u2014 if the ref doesn't resolve, the upload fails rather than\n  silently lose threading.\n\n## Placement\n\n- **Reply drafts** go inside the existing thread's \\`.attach/\\` next to\n  the source message, e.g.\n  \\`box/inbox/email/thread-X.attach/draft-001.email-outbound.card\\`. This\n  keeps the conversation co-located.\n- **New emails (no thread)** go in a fresh directory under\n  \\`box/inbox/email/\\`.\n\n## Lifecycle\n\n- \\`status: draft\\` (default) \u2014 the connector uploads to Gmail's Drafts\n  folder on next sync and stamps the card with \\`gmail-draft-id:\\` and\n  \\`gmail-draft-url:\\`. Share the URL with the user so they can review\n  and send. Once stamped, the draft is **not** re-uploaded; editing\n  the card after upload doesn't update the Gmail draft (yet).\n- Deleting the card does **not** delete the Gmail draft \u2014 once Gmail\n  has it, the user owns it.\n\n## Threading checklist for replies\n\n1. Place the draft in the **same directory** as the source message.\n2. Set \\`in-reply-to.ref:\\` pointing at the specific message you're\n   replying to.\n3. Set \\`subject: Re: <original subject>\\`.\n4. Don't set \\`status\\` explicitly \u2014 it defaults to \\`draft\\`.`,\n});\n\nexport interface EmailOutboundFields {\n  type: \"email-outbound\";\n  status: \"draft\" | \"sent\";\n  to: string;\n  cc?: string;\n  bcc?: string;\n  subject: string;\n  \"in-reply-to\"?: { ref: string };\n  \"gmail-draft-id\"?: string;\n  \"gmail-draft-url\"?: string;\n  body: string;\n}\n\n/**\n * Build the file content for an outbound draft card.\n *\n * For replies, set `inReplyToRef` to the path of the source email-message\n * card relative to the directory the draft will be written into (typically\n * just `msg-NNN.email-message.card`).\n */\nexport function createEmailOutboundTemplate(options: {\n  to: string;\n  cc?: string;\n  bcc?: string;\n  subject: string;\n  body: string;\n  inReplyToRef?: string;\n}): string {\n  const fields: Record<string, unknown> = {\n    status: \"draft\",\n    to: options.to,\n  };\n  if (options.cc !== undefined && options.cc !== \"\") fields[\"cc\"] = offset: true }),\n    source: z.string(),\n    priority: z.enum([\"normal\", \"low\"]).default(\"normal\"),\n    description: z.string(),\n    items: z.array(z.object({ ref: z.string() })),\n  },\n  instructions: `# Processing Intake Jobs\n\nAn intake job means new items have arrived in the inbox and need triage.\n\n## Steps\n\n1. Without\n   a guide:\n   - **Move** to a permanent location (e.g., \\`store/\\` or\n     \\`box/pool/\\`) if it's worth keeping\n   - **Trash** with \\`cb rm <path>\\` if it's not useful\n   - **Ask** the user a question if you need guidance (create a\n     question card)\n5. When all items are triaged, commit your work\n6. Run \\`cb finish {thisJobFile}\\` to complete the job\n\n## Important\n\n- Commit your work as you go\n- The \\`cb finish\\` command only deletes the job file \u2014 make sure your\n  actual work is committed first\n- Read items before deciding \u2014 don't judge by filename alone`,\n});\n\nexport interface IntakeJobFields {\n  type: \"intake-job\";\n  status: string;\n  created: string;\n  source: string;\n  priority: \"normal\" | \"low\";\n  description: string;\n  items: Array<{ ref: string }>;\n}\n\nexport function createIntakeJobTemplate(options: {\n  created?: string;\n  source: string;\n  description: string;\n  items: string[];\n  priority?: \"normal\" | \"low\";\n}): string {\n  const fields: Record<string, unknown> = {\n    status: \"pending\",\n    created: options.created ?? new Date().toISOString(),\n    source: options.source,\n    priority: options.priority ?? \"normal\",\n    description: options.description,\n    items: options.items.map((ref) => ({ ref })),\n  };\n  return `---\\n${stringifyYaml(fields)}---\\n`;\n}\n", "/**\n * Calendar review job card schema \u2014 a job to review calendar changes.\n *\n * Created by the google-calendar connector when events are added,\n * updated, or deleted. Read this job card to find the changes (\\`changes:\\` array)\n2. Check for an applicable guide \u2014 see the compiled reference in\n   \\`docs/generated/\\` if available\n3. For each change, follow the guide's triage rules and actions.\n   Without a guide:\n   - **New events**: Does the user need to prepare anything? Create a\n     memo or reminder if so.\n   - **Updated events**: Note what changed (time, location, etc.).\n     Flag significant changes.\n   - **Deleted events**: Note the cancellation. Usually no action\n     needed.\n4. Most changes need no action \u2014 just review and move on\n5. If something needs user attention, create a question card\n6. When done reviewing, commit any work and run\n   \\`cb finish {thisJobFile}\\`\n\n## Important\n\n- Most calendar changes are informational \u2014 don't over-react\n- Only create tasks/questions for changes that genuinely need\n  preparation\n- Commit your work before running \\`cb finish\\``,\n});\n\nexport interface CalendarChangeInput {\n  action: \"new\" | \"updated\" | \"deleted\";\n  ref?: string;\n  summary: string;\n  icsContent?: string;\n}\n\nexport interface CalendarReviewJobFields {\n  type: \"calendar-review-job\";\n  status: string;\n  created: string;\n  source: string;\n  priority: \"normal\" | \"low\";\n  description: string;\n  changes: Array<{\n    action: \"new\" | \"updated\" | \"deleted\";\n    ref?: string;\n    summary: string;\n    ics?: string;\n  }>;\n}\n\nexport function createCalendarReviewJobTemplate(options: {\n  created?: string;\n  source: string;\n  description: string;\n  changes: CalendarChangeInput[];\n  priority?: \"normal\" | \"low\";\n}): string {\n  const fields: Record<string, unknown> = {\n    status: \"pending\",\n    created: options.created ?? new Date().toISOString(),\n    source: options.source,\n    priority: options.priority ?? \"normal\",\n    description: options.description,\n    changes: options.changes.map((c) => {\n      const entry: Record<string, unknown> = {\n        action: c.action,\n        summary: c.summary,\n      };\n      if (c.ref !== undefined) entry[\"ref\"] = c.ref;\n      if (c.icsContent !== undefined) entry[\"ics\"] = c.icsContent;\n      return entry;\n    }),\n  };\n  return `---\\n${stringifyYaml(fields)}---\\n`;\n}\n", "/**\n * Telegram message card schema \u2014 outbound messages to Telegram chats.\n *\n * Agents create these cards in `box/output/` with `status: pending`.\n * The telegram connector sends them during sync, then deletes the card\n * on success or stamps it with an error on failure.\n */\n\nimport { cardSchema, type CardSchema } from \"cardworks\";\nimport { stringify as stringifyYaml } from \"yaml\";\nimport { z } from \"zod\";\n\nexport const TelegramMessageStatus = z.enum([\"pending\", \"sent\", \"failed\"]);\nexport type TelegramMessageStatusValue = z.infer<typeof TelegramMessageStatus>;\n\nconst TelegramResponse = z.object({\n  \"sent-at\": z.string().datetime({ offset: true }),\n  \"message-id\": z.string(),\n});\n\nexport const TelegramMessageSchema: CardSchema = cardSchema(\"telegram-message\", {\n  fields: {\n    status: TelegramMessageStatus.default(\"pending\"),\n    \"chat-id\": z.string(),\n    text: z.string(),\n    response: TelegramResponse.optional(),\n    error: z.string().optional(),\n  },\n  instructions: `# Sending Telegram Messages\n\nTo send a message to a Telegram chat, create a card in\n\\`box/output/\\` with the \\`.telegram-message.card\\` extension.\n\n## Required frontmatter\n- \\`chat-id:\\` \u2014 The Telegram chat ID (negative for groups)\n- \\`text:\\` \u2014 The message text (max 4096 chars), sent as plain text.\n\n## Lifecycle\n1. On failure: \\`status\\` becomes \\`failed\\`, an \\`error\\` field is added.\n   Failed cards are not retried \u2014 fix or delete them.`,\n});\n\nexport interface TelegramMessageFields {\n  type: \"telegram-message\";\n  status: TelegramMessageStatusValue;\n  \"chat-id\": string;\n  text: string;\n  response?: { \"sent-at\": string; the agent appends one trailing\n * message (its reply) or seen-marker (acknowledge without replying).\n */\n\nimport { cardSchema, type CardSchema } from \"cardworks\";\nimport { stringify as stringifyYaml } from \"yaml\";\nimport { z } from \"zod\";\n\nconst ParticipantEntry = z.object({\n  ref: z.string(),\n});\n\nconst MessageEntry = z.object({\n  kind: z.literal(\"message\"),\n  id: z.string().optional(),\n  sender: z.string(),\n  \"sender-id\": z.string().optional(),\n  time: z.string().datetime({ offset: true }).optional(),\n  sent: z.string().datetime({ offset: true }).optional(),\n  text: z.string(),\n});\n\nconst SeenEntry = z.object({\n  kind: z.literal(\"seen\"),\n  \"callback-in\": z.string().optional(),\n  \"wait-for\": z.string().optional(),\n  text: z.string().optional(),\n});\n\nconst ThreadEntry = z.discriminatedUnion(\"kind\", [MessageEntry, SeenEntry]);\n\nexport const ChatThreadSchema: CardSchema = cardSchema(\"chat-thread\", {\n  searchable: false,\n  fields: {\n    \"chat-id\": z.string(),\n    connector: z.string(),\n    description: z.string().optional(),\n    participants: z.array(ParticipantEntry).optional(),\n    entries: z.array(ThreadEntry).default([]),\n  },\n  instructions: `# Processing Chat Threads\n\nA chat thread is an accumulating conversation from a messaging connector (e.g. Telegram). Your job references a thread file \u2014 read it to see the conversation.\n\n## Thread structure (YAML frontmatter)\n\nTop-level fields:\n- \\`chat-id:\\` and \\`connector:\\` \u2014 identify the chat\n- \\`description:\\` \u2014 what this chat is (e.g. \"Family group chat\")\n- \\`participants:\\` \u2014 array of \\`{ref: people/...}\\` linking to people cards\n- \\`entries:\\` \u2014 chronological array of messages and seen-markers\n\nEach entry has a \\`kind\\` discriminator:\n- \\`kind: message\\` with fields \\`sender\\`, \\`sender-id?\\`, \\`time?\\`, \\`sent?\\`, \\`id?\\`, \\`text\\`\n- \\`kind: seen\\` with fields \\`callback-in?\\`, \\`wait-for?\\`, \\`text?\\`\n\n## Guidelines\n\nCheck for a \\`chat.guide.card\\` file in the same directory as the thread file. If it exists, read it \u2014 it contains per-chat behavioral guidelines (when to respond, tone, topics to watch for). The last \\`kind: seen\\` or \\`kind: message\\` with \\`sender: agent\\` marks the boundary of what was previously processed. Everything after that boundary is new.\n\nIf the last entry is already yours (\\`seen\\` or agent message) and there are no new messages after it, check whether the seen entry has a \\`text:\\` \u2014 that's a note from your previous self about what to do next.\n\n## Responding\n\nYou MUST leave exactly one trailing entry at the end of \\`entries:\\`:\n\n- A message entry with \\`kind: message, sender: agent, text: \"Your response\"\\` \u2014 to send a message. Use this for casual/social messages, messages not directed at you, or when there's nothing useful to add.\n\n### When to respond vs. acknowledge\n- Respond to direct questions, requests, or when you have genuinely useful information\n- Acknowledge (\\`kind: seen\\`) casual chatter, messages between other people, or when silence is appropriate\n- When in doubt, acknowledge rather than respond \u2014 unsolicited messages are annoying\n\n### Scheduling follow-ups\n- \\`{kind: seen, callback-in: 30m, text: \"Check if anyone answered Alice's question\"}\\` \u2014 you'll be re-invoked in 30 minutes if no new messages arrive\n- The \\`text\\` of a seen entry is a note to your future self \u2014 write what you plan to check or do\n\n## Important rules\n- Only append ONE entry to the end of Run \\`cb finish {thisJobFile}\\` to complete the job\n\n## Important\n\n- The directive was written by the agent that created the question \u2014\n  follow it faithfully\n- Read the original question's memo and context for background\n- Commit your work before running \\`cb finish\\``,\n});\n\nexport interface QuestionFollowupJobFields {\n  type: \"question-followup-job\";\n  status: string;\n  created: string;\n  source: string;\n  description: string;\n  \"question-ref\": { ref: string };\n  directive: string;\n  answer: string;\n}\n\nexport function createQuestionFollowupJobTemplate(options: {\n  description: string;\n  questionRef: string;\n  directive: string;\n  answer: string;\n  created?: string;\n}): string {\n  const fields: Record<string, unknown> = {\n    status: \"pending\",\n    created: options.created ?? new Date().toISOString(),\n    source: \"question-answer\",\n    description: options.description,\n    \"question-ref\": { ref: options.questionRef },\n    directive: options.directive,\n    answer: options.answer,\n  };\n  return `---\\n${stringifyYaml(fields)}---\\n`;\n}\n", "/**\n * Todo list card schema \u2014 human-oriented task lists.\n *\n * Todo lists group related action items. Items can be nested\n * (sub-items within items) and have free-form details and agent\n * notes. Everything is structured frontmatter \u2014 no markdown body.\n */\n\nimport { cardSchema, type CardSchema } from \"cardworks\";\nimport { stringify as stringifyYaml } from \"yaml\";\nimport { z } from \"zod\";\n\nexport const TodoItemStatus = z.enum([\"pending\", \"done\", \"cancelled\", \"deferred\"]);\nexport type TodoItemStatusType = z.infer<typeof TodoItemStatus>;\n\nconst ItemSchema: z.ZodType<TodoItem> = z.lazy(() =>\n  z.object({\n    name: z.string(),\n    status: TodoItemStatus.default(\"pending\"),\n    completed: z.string().datetime({ offset: true }).optional(),\n    details: z.string().optional(),\n    \"agent-notes\": z.string().optional(),\n    items: z.array(ItemSchema).optional(),\n  }),\n);\n\nexport interface TodoItem {\n  name: string;\n  status: TodoItemStatusType;\n  completed?: string | undefined;\n  details?: string | undefined;\n  \"agent-notes\"?: string | undefined;\n  items?: TodoItem[] | undefined;\n}\n\nexport const TodoListSchema: CardSchema = cardSchema(\"todo-list\", {\n  fields: {\n    name: z.string(),\n    details: z.string().optional(),\n    \"agent-notes\": z.string().optional(),\n    items: z.array(ItemSchema).optional(),\n  },\n  instructions: `# Todo Lists\n\nTodo lists are human-oriented action items. They are NOT agent jobs \u2014\nthey track things people need to do (errands, purchases, projects,\ncalls, etc.). Agents may create and maintain them but the work is for\nhumans.\n\n## Structure\n\nFrontmatter:\n- \\`name:\\` \u2014 display name for the list\n- \\`details:\\` \u2014 free-form description of the list's purpose/context\n- \\`agent-notes:\\` \u2014 notes for agents about how to handle this list\n  (not shown to users)\n- \\`items:\\` \u2014 array of items, each \\`{name, status, completed?,\n  details?, agent-notes?, items?}\\`. Items can nest via their own\n  \\`items\\` field.\n\nStatus values: \\`pending\\`, \\`done\\`, \\`cancelled\\`, \\`deferred\\`.\n\nWhen an item is completed, set \\`status: done\\` and add a \\`completed\\`\nfield with the ISO datetime.\n\n## Storage\n\nActive todo lists live in \\`store/todos/\\`. Filename:\n\\`List_Name.todo-list.card\\`.\n\n## Lifecycle\n\n- **All done/cancelled** \u2192 move to \\`store/archive/done/\\`\n- **All done/cancelled/deferred** (at least one deferred) \u2192 move to\n  \\`store/archive/deferred/\\`\n- **Any pending** \u2192 stays in \\`store/todos/\\`\n\n## Guidelines\n\n- Keep item names short and actionable\n- Use \\`details\\` for supporting info, not the item name\n- Use \\`agent-notes\\` for context the agent should remember (e.g.,\n  \"Boxholder mentioned this during the Feb 22 voice memo\")\n- Don't create separate todo lists for single items \u2014 add to an\n  existing relevant list if one exists\n- When extracting todos from voice memos or other inputs, group\n  related items into lists by topic`,\n});\n\nexport interface TodoListFields {\n  type: \"todo-list\";\n  name: string;\n  details?: string;\n  \"agent-notes\"?: string;\n  items?: TodoItem[];\n}\n\nexport function createTodoListTemplate(options: {\n  name: string;\n  details?: string;\n  items?: Array<{ name: string; status?: string | undefined }>;\n}): string {\n  const fields: Record<string, unknown> = {\n    name: options.name,\n  };\n  if (options.details !== undefined && options.details !== \"\") {\n    fields[\"details\"] = options.details;\n  }\n  if (options.items !== undefined && options.items.length > 0) {\n    fields[\"items\"] = options.items.map((it) => ({\n      name: it.name,\n      status: it.status === undefined ? \"pending\" : it.status,\n    }));\n  }\n  return `---\\n${stringifyYaml(fields)}---\\n`;\n}\n", "/**\n * Person card schema \u2014 key people referenced from briefings.\n *\n * Person cards live at `people/First_Last.person.card`. Identity, contact\n * info, and aliases live in the frontmatter; the markdown body is freeform\n * \"notes\" context.\n *\n * Referenced from briefing cards via the `key-people[].ref` field.\n */\n\nimport { body, cardSchema, type CardSchema } from \"cardworks\";\nimport { stringify as stringifyYaml } from \"yaml\";\nimport { z } from \"zod\";\n\nexport const PersonStatus = z.enum([\"active\", \"inactive\", \"archived\"]);\nexport type PersonStatusType = z.infer<typeof PersonStatus>;\n\nexport const PersonSchema: CardSchema = cardSchema(\"person\", {\n  fields: {\n    status: PersonStatus.default(\"active\"),\n    name: z.string(),\n    called: z.array(z.string()).optional(),\n    role: z.string().optional(),\n    contact: z.string().optional(),\n    body: body(z.string()),\n  },\n  instructions: `# Person Cards\n\nPerson cards track key people referenced in briefings and throughout\nthe box.\n\nThey live at \\`people/First_Last.person.card\\`. The filename uses the\nperson's name with underscores.\n\n**Frontmatter:**\n- \\`name:\\` \u2014 Full name. Required.\n- \\`called:\\` \u2014 Array of aliases / nicknames. Include if the boxholder\n  uses these names (e.g., [\"Dad\", \"Papa\"]).\n- \\`role:\\` \u2014 Relationship or function (e.g., \"Ledger subject \u2014\n  boxholder's father\", \"Financial advisor\").\n- \\`contact:\\` \u2014 Freeform contact info (phone, email, address).\n- \\`status:\\` \u2014 \\`active\\` (default), \\`inactive\\`, or \\`archived\\`.\n\n**Body (markdown):** freeform notes / context about the person.\n\n**When to create a person card:**\n- When adding someone to a briefing's \\`key-people:\\` \u2014 always create\n  the person card if it doesn't exist.\n- When a person keeps coming up and you need a place to consolidate\n  info about them.\n\n**Filename convention:** \\`people/First_Last.person.card\\` \u2014 use the\nperson's actual name, not a slug or alias.`,\n});\n\nexport interface PersonFields {\n  type: \"person\";\n  status: PersonStatusType;\n  name: string;\n  called?: string[];\n  role?: string;\n  contact?: string;\n  body: string;\n}\n\nexport function createPersonTemplate(options: {\n  name: string;\n  called?: string;\n  role?: string;\n}): string {\n  const fields: Record<string, unknown> = {\n    status: \"active\",\n    name: options.name,\n  };\n  if (options.called !== undefined && options.called !== \"\") {\n    fields[\"called\"] = [options.called];\n  }\n  if (options.role !== undefined && options.role !== \"\") {\n    fields[\"role\"] = options.role;\n  }\n  return `---\\n${stringifyYaml(fields)}---\\n`;\n}\n", "/**\n * Sheet card schema \u2014 metadata for a Google Sheets spreadsheet synced to the box.\n *\n * Pure frontmatter. Each tab's JSON data lives in the card's `.attach/`\n * scope; each entry in `sheets:` is a `{ref, title, gid}` object pointing\n * at one tab file.\n *\n * Example file layout:\n *   store/drive/Budget.sheet.card\n *   store/drive/Budget.attach/Summary.json\n *   store/drive/Budget.attach/Expenses.json\n */\n\nimport { cardSchema, type CardSchema } from \"cardworks\";\nimport { stringify as stringifyYaml } from \"yaml\";\nimport { z } from \"zod\";\n\nconst SheetTab = z.object({\n  ref: z.string(),\n  title: z.string(),\n  gid: z.string(),\n});\n\nexport const SheetSchema: CardSchema = cardSchema(\"sheet\", {\n  fields: {\n    \"drive-id\": z.string(),\n    status: z.enum([\"synced\", \"error\", \"new\"]).optional(),\n    title: z.string(),\n    modified: z.string(),\n    link: z.string(),\n    owner: z.string(),\n    sheets: z.array(SheetTab),\n  },\n  instructions: `# Sheet Cards\n\n**Location:** Anywhere in the box, commonly \\`store/drive/\\`.\n\nEach synced Google Spreadsheet has a \\`.sheet.card\\` metadata file plus\nan attach scope (\\`{basename}.attach/\\`) containing one JSON file per\nsheet tab. The \\`sheets:\\` field lists \\`{ref, title, gid}\\` entries\npointing into that scope.\n\n## Data format\nEach tab is a JSON file with one row per line. Cell values are:\n- Plain values: strings, numbers, booleans, or null\n- Formula cells: \\`{\"f\": \"=SUM(A1:B1)\", \"v\": \"$42.00\"}\\` \u2014 \\`f\\` is the\n  formula, \\`v\\` is the computed display value\n\n## Reading spreadsheet data\n1. Read the card to understand structure: title, tabs, Google link\n2. Read the JSON tab files \u2014 plain values are bare, formula cells have\n   both the formula and computed result\n\n## Editing spreadsheet data\nEdit the JSON file directly and commit. For plain cells, just change\nthe value. For formula cells, edit the \\`f\\` field (the \\`v\\` field will\nbe updated on next sync). On next sync (\\`cb wakeup\\` or\n\\`cb drive sync\\`), local changes are pushed to Google Sheets. Do NOT\nmodify the card frontmatter \u2014 it is managed by the connector \u2014 with one\nexception: \\`contains:\\` is agent-owned and survives sync; set it freely\n(\\`cb contains update\\`).\n\n## Moving spreadsheets\nMoving the card moves its attach scope (with the tab data inside)\natomically \u2014 the \\`drive-id\\` field maintains the link to Google Drive.`,\n});\n\nexport interface SheetFields {\n  type: \"sheet\";\n  \"drive-id\": string;\n  status?: \"synced\" | \"error\" | \"new\";\n  title: string;\n  modified: string;\n  link: string;\n  owner: string;\n  sheets: Array<{ ref: string; title: string; gid: string }>;\n}\n\nexport function createSheetTemplate(options: {\n  driveId: string;\n  title: string;\n  modified: string;\n  link: string;\n  owner: string;\n  sheets: Array<{ ref: string; title: string; gid: string }>;\n  status?: \"synced\" | \"error\" | \"new\";\n}): string {\n  const fields: Record<string, unknown> = {\n    \"drive-id\": options.driveId,\n    status: options.status === undefined ? \"synced\" : options.status,\n    title: options.title,\n    modified: options.modified,\n    link: options.link,\n    owner: options.owner,\n    sheets: options.sheets,\n  };\n  return `---\\n${stringifyYaml(fields)}---\\n`;\n}\n", "/**\n * Doc card schema \u2014 a generic in-box document.\n *\n * The minimal \"I have a document with a title and a body\" card. Use this\n * whenever an agent would otherwise reach for a plain `.md` file: design\n * notes, plans, reference material, scratch documents, README-style\n * pages. Distinct from `gdoc`, which is the synced Google Doc type.\n *\n * Body is markdown. No timestamps \u2014 git history is the source of truth\n * for creation/modification.\n */\n\nimport { body, cardSchema, type CardSchema } from \"cardworks\";\nimport { stringify as stringifyYaml } from \"yaml\";\nimport { z } from \"zod\";\n\nexport const DocSchema: CardSchema = cardSchema(\"doc\", {\n  fields: {\n    title: z.string(),\n    body: body(z.string()),\n  },\n  instructions: `# Doc Cards\n\nA doc card is a generic typed document with a title and a markdown body.\n\n**Use \\`.doc.card\\` instead of \\`.md\\` by default.** Plain markdown files\nare still allowed for things like READMEs, generated docs, or\nattachments, but a fresh document an agent creates for design notes,\nplans, reference material, scratch work, or any prose worth keeping\nshould be a doc card. The card form gives the document a title field\nseparate from the filename, lets it participate in card-wide tooling\n(\\`cb validate\\`, the file browser, refs), and keeps the box's content\ntyped.\n\n## Frontmatter\n\n- \\`title:\\` \u2014 required, free-form. The display title; can differ from\n  the filename.\n\n## Body\n\nThe doc's body lives **inline in the .doc.card file itself**, after\nthe closing \\`---\\` of the frontmatter. Plain markdown. Headings,\nlists, code blocks, links, etc. \u2014 anything markdown supports. Don't\nput the body in a separate \\`.md\\` file beside the card; the card *is*\nthe document.\n\nA minimal doc card on disk:\n\n\\`\\`\\`\n---\ntitle: Trip Report\n---\n# Trip Report\n\nWe drove down on Friday...\n\\`\\`\\`\n\nReferences to other cards use the standard ref form (frontmatter\n\\`{ref: \"...\"}\\` or inline markdown links to card paths).\n\n## Embedding images and other files\n\nFiles the doc references \u2014 images, attachments, supporting media \u2014 go\ninside the doc's own **attach scope**: a sibling directory named\n\\`<basename>.attach/\\` (where \\`<basename>\\` is the card's filename\nwithout the \\`.doc.card\\` suffix). Refer to them from the body using\nthe scoped form \\`attach/<filename>\\`.\n\nLayout for a doc with an embedded image:\n\n\\`\\`\\`\nstore/notes/Trip_Report.doc.card\nstore/notes/Trip_Report.attach/photo.jpg\n\\`\\`\\`\n\nAnd the doc's body:\n\n\\`\\`\\`markdown\n# Trip Report\n\n![A view from the cabin](attach/photo.jpg)\n\nWe drove down on Friday...\n\\`\\`\\`\n\nThe image lives inside \\`Trip_Report.attach/\\` (the card's scope), not\nat the top level or in a shared \\`images/\\` directory. Moving or\nrenaming the card moves the whole scope atomically.\n\n## When NOT to use a doc card\n\n- A synced Google Doc \u2014 use \\`.gdoc.card\\` (managed by the drive\n  connector).\n- A captured note or voice memo \u2014 use \\`.memo.card\\`.\n- A structured record extracted from something \u2014 use \\`.record.card\\`.\n- An ad-hoc README that lives next to code/config rather than being\n  content in its own right \u2014 plain \\`.md\\` is fine.\n\n## No timestamps\n\nDoc cards intentionally have no \\`created\\` or \\`modified\\` field. Git\nalready tracks both authoritatively (\\`git log --diff-filter=A\\` for\ncreation, \\`git log\\` for any change). Don't add them.`,\n});\n\nexport interface DocFields {\n  type: \"doc\";\n  title: string;\n  body: string;\n}\n\nexport function createDocTemplate(options: { title: string; body?: string }): string {\n  const fields: Record<string, unknown> = {\n    title: options.title,\n  };\n  const bodyText = options.body ?? \"\";\n  const bodyTail = bodyText === \"\" ? \"\" : `${bodyText}${bodyText.endsWith(\"\\n\") ? \"\" : \"\\n\"}`;\n  return `---\\n${stringifyYaml(fields)}---\\n${bodyTail}`;\n}\n", "/**\n * Gdoc card schema \u2014 metadata for a Google Docs document synced to the box.\n *\n * Pure frontmatter. The actual document content lives in a markdown file\n * inside the card's `.attach/` scope; `content.ref` points at it.\n * Lossy upstream features (comments, footnotes, etc.) are enumerated in\n * `lossy:` so agents know what won't survive a push.\n *\n * Example file layout:\n *   store/drive/Project_Notes.gdoc.card\n *   store/drive/Project_Notes.attach/Project_Notes.md\n *\n * Distinct from the generic `doc` schema (`src/schemas/doc.tsx`), which\n * is a freeform document with no upstream sync \u2014 use that when an agent\n * would otherwise reach for a plain `.md` file.\n */\n\nimport { cardSchema, type CardSchema } from \"cardworks\";\nimport { stringify as stringifyYaml } from \"yaml\";\nimport { z } from \"zod\";\n\nconst LossyType = z.enum([\n  \"comments\",\n  \"footnotes\",\n  \"images\",\n  \"drawings\",\n  \"equations\",\n  \"suggestions\",\n  \"tables\",\n]);\n\nexport type GdocLossyType = z.infer<typeof LossyType>;\n\nconst LossyItem = z.object({\n  type: LossyType,\n  count: z.coerce.number(),\n});\n\nexport const GdocSchema: CardSchema = cardSchema(\"gdoc\", {\n  fields: {\n    \"drive-id\": z.string(),\n    status: z.enum([\"synced\", \"error\", \"new\", \"conflict\"]).optional(),\n    title: z.string(),\n    modified: z.string(),\n    revision: z.string().optional(),\n    link: z.string(),\n    owner: z.string(),\n    content: z.object({ ref: z.string() }),\n    lossy: z.array(LossyItem).optional(),\n  },\n  instructions: `# Gdoc Cards\n\n**Location:** Anywhere in the box, commonly \\`store/drive/\\`.\n\nEach synced Google Doc has a \\`.gdoc.card\\` plus a markdown file inside\nthe card's \\`.attach/\\` scope (e.g.\n\\`Project_Notes.attach/Project_Notes.md\\`). The \\`content.ref:\\` field\npoints at it.\n\nNot to be confused with \\`.doc.card\\` \u2014 that's the generic in-box\ndocument type with no upstream sync.\n\n## Editing\nEdit the \\`.md\\` file and commit. On the next sync the change pushes\nback to Google Drive (markdown is converted to Doc format on the\nserver). Do not modify the card frontmatter \u2014 it is managed by the\nconnector \u2014 with one exception: \\`contains:\\` is agent-owned and\nsurvives sync; set it freely (\\`cb contains update\\`).\n\n## Conflicts\nIf the upstream Doc was edited in Drive between your last pull and\nyour push, the card \\`status\\` becomes \\`conflict\\` and the upstream\nversion is written next to the local \\`.md\\` as \\`{basename}.remote.md\\`\n(inside the attach scope). Resolve by merging the two files, deleting\nthe \\`.remote.md\\`, and committing \u2014 the next sync will push the\nresolved version.\n\n## Lossy content\nThe \\`lossy:\\` field enumerates features in the upstream Doc that don't\nsurvive markdown export (comments, footnotes, embedded images,\ndrawings, equations, suggestions, complex tables). When present,\npushing local edits will replace those features with the markdown\nbody \u2014 destroying them. If \\`lossy\\` is non-empty and a push is\nintended, surface the loss to the user before committing.\n\n## Moving docs\nMoving the card moves its attach scope (and the \\`.md\\` inside)\natomically \u2014 the \\`drive-id\\` field maintains the link to Google Drive.`,\n});\n\nexport interface GdocFields {\n  type: \"gdoc\";\n  \"drive-id\": string;\n  status?: \"synced\" | \"error\" | \"new\" | \"conflict\";\n  title: string;\n  modified: string;\n  revision?: string;\n  link: string;\n  owner: string;\n  content: { ref: string };\n  lossy?: Array<{ type: GdocLossyType; count: number }>;\n}\n\nexport function createGdocTemplate(options: {\n  driveId: string;\n  title: string;\n  modified: string;\n  revision?: string;\n  link: string;\n  owner: string;\n  contentFile: string;\n  lossy?: Array<{ type: GdocLossyType; count: number }>;\n  status?: \"synced\" | \"error\" | \"new\" | \"conflict\";\n}): string {\n  const fields: Record<string, unknown> = {\n    \"drive-id\": options.driveId,\n    status: options.status === undefined ? \"synced\" : options.status,\n    title: options.title,\n    modified: options.modified,\n    link: options.link,\n    owner: options.owner,\n    content: { ref: `attach/${options.contentFile}` },\n  };\n  if (options.revision !== undefined && options.revision !== \"\") {\n    fields[\"revision\"] = options.revision;\n  }\n  if (options.lossy !== undefined && options.lossy.length > 0) {\n    fields[\"lossy\"] = options.lossy;\n  }\n  return `---\\n${stringifyYaml(fields)}---\\n`;\n}\n", "/**\n * Commentary card schema \u2014 review-and-comment on a host card from inside a box.\n * See `docs/plans/box-commentary-surface.md` and `docs/plans/extfile-card.md`.\n *\n * **Attach-only:** a commentary card lives in a host card's `.attach/` scope and\n * its bare `{% source %}` anchors target the containing card \u2014 an `extfile`\n * (live external file), a `webpage` (captured page), or an in-box `doc`. It\n * carries no target of its own (no `defaultHref`/`defaultRef`/`targets`).\n *\n * Body-bearing (like `doc`/`briefing`): the body is markdown commentary whose\n * `{% source %}` anchors quote the spans being commented on. Markdoc validation\n * of those tags lives in `card-lint.ts`, scoped to this card type.\n */\n\nimport { body, cardSchema, type CardSchema } from \"cardworks\";\nimport { stringify as stringifyYaml } from \"yaml\";\nimport { z } from \"zod\";\n\nexport const CommentarySchema: CardSchema = cardSchema(\"commentary\", {\n  fields: {\n    title: z.string().optional(),\n    // Captured-web-page metadata (set by the clerk capture flow): the original\n    // page URL, the capture date (YYYY-MM-DD), and an in-box ref to the frozen\n    // snapshot. Rendered as a header; all optional.\n    source: z.string().optional(),\n    captured: z.string().optional(),\n    frozen: z.string().optional(),\n    body: body(z.string()),\n  },\n  instructions: `# Commentary Cards\n\nA commentary card holds the boxholder's anchored remarks about a **host card**.\nIt is **attach-only**: it lives in the host's \\`.attach/\\` scope\n(\\`<host-basename>.attach/<name>.commentary.card\\`) and the host's view surfaces\nthe remarks inline. The host is whatever the commentary annotates:\n\n- an **\\`extfile\\`** card \u2014 to comment on a live external file (repo docs/source,\n  across worktrees). This is the way to review an out-of-box file: make an\n  \\`extfile\\` pointer, then attach the commentary to it.\n- a **\\`webpage\\`** card \u2014 to comment on a captured page.\n- an in-box **\\`doc\\`** \u2014 to comment on a box document.\n\nA commentary card carries **no target of its own** \u2014 no \\`defaultHref\\`,\n\\`defaultRef\\`, or \\`targets\\`. The containing host card *is* the target, and bare\n\\`{% source %}\\` anchors point at it.\n\n## Body \u2014 quote-then-remark\n\nEach comment is a \\`{% source %}\\` anchor (the span being commented on) followed\nby your remark as ordinary prose:\n\n\\`\\`\\`\n{% source pos=\"body; heading: Track A (#track-a); ~line 210\"\n          version=\"sha256:9f3a1c2b git:7ffeae4\" %}\n{% quote %}the exact span the user selected{% /quote %}\n{% /source %}\n\nThis overstates it \u2014 placement is composer-only, so it isn't a clean superset.\n\\`\\`\\`\n\nThe \\`{% source %}\\` (with inner \\`{% quote %}\\`) holds the **selected span,\nverbatim**. Your comment is the prose *after* it, outside the tag.\n\n## Turning a \\`<user-selection>\\` into an anchor\n\nWhen the boxholder selects text in a rendered target and sends it (a\n\\`<user-selection ref|href=\"\u2026\" pos=\"\u2026\">\u2026</user-selection>\\` in their message),\nappend a \\`{% source %}\\` block:\n\n- **Body** = the selected span, **escaped to valid Markdown/Markdoc** \u2014\n  code-wrap \\`<\u2026>\\`, escape a stray \\` \\`\\` \\`, \\`{%\\`, or \\`%}\\` so a span that\n  contains markup neither breaks the tag nor renders wrong. This is faithful\n  rendering of what was shown, not paraphrase.\n- Target: leave the anchor **ref-free** \u2014 a bare \\`{% source %}\\` points at the\n  containing host card (the \\`extfile\\`/\\`webpage\\`/\\`doc\\` this commentary is\n  attached to). Add an explicit \\`ref\\`/\\`href\\` only in the rare case the\n  selection was against a *different* card. Always write \\`version\\` markers\n  measured from the file (\\`sha256:\\` content hash, plus \\`git:\\` when tracked).\n- Copy \\`pos\\` (and \\`placement\\`, if present) from the selection.\n\nYour own framing stays *outside* the tag, as prose. One commentary card per\nhost.`,\n});\n\n/**\n * Build an empty commentary card to live inside a host document's attach scope\n * (e.g. a `.webpage.card`'s `<basename>.attach/`). Capture provenance lives on the host\n * webpage card, not here.\n */\nexport function createCommentaryTemplate(options: { title?: string | undefined }): string {\n  const hasTitle = options.title !== undefined && options.title !== \"\";\n  const yamlText = hasTitle ? stringifyYaml({ title: options.title }) : \"\";\n  return `---\\n${yamlText}---\\n`;\n}\n", "/**\n * Webpage card schema \u2014 a captured external web page, stored in-box.\n *\n * The card *is* the page: its markdown body is the readable rendering (Defuddle\n * extraction), and a frozen, self-contained HTML snapshot rides alongside in\n * the card's `.attach/` scope. Frontmatter carries capture provenance \u2014 the\n * original URL, when it was captured, and a ref to the frozen snapshot.\n *\n * Produced by the clerk browser extension (\"Comment on this page\" and \"Save\n * page\") and rendered by `WebpageView`. A webpage card is a snapshot of an external\n * page at capture time \u2014 edit it sparingly.\n */\n\nimport { body, cardSchema, type CardSchema } from \"cardworks\";\nimport { stringify as stringifyYaml } from \"yaml\";\nimport { z } from \"zod\";\n\nexport const WebpageSchema: CardSchema = cardSchema(\"webpage\", {\n  fields: {\n    title: z.string().optional(),\n    // The original page URL the capture came from.\n    source: z.string(),\n    // Full ISO instant of capture; the renderer formats it in the viewer's\n    // local zone. {};\n  // TEMPORARY \u2014 diagnose unexpected writes to the callback-box source repo\n  // (`.callback-box/` and `docs/generated/` showing up here as untracked).\n  // Remove once the caller is identified.\n  if (boxRoot.endsWith(\"/callback/callback-box\") || boxRoot.endsWith(\"/src/callback/callback-box\")) {\n    console.warn(`[generateDocs:DIAG] called with boxRoot=${boxRoot}`);\n    console.warn(new GenerateDocsAgainstSourceError().stack);\n  }\n\n  // Fast path: skip if no input files changed and source code unchanged.\n  // Skipped entirely when force is set \u2014 see GenerateDocsOptions.force for why.\n  const markerPath = join(boxRoot, GENERATE_MARKER);\n  const inputMtime = await newestInputMtime(boxRoot);\n  const currentCommit = await getCallbackBoxCommit();\n  if (await canSkipGeneration({ markerPath, inputMtime, currentCommit, force: options.force ??
