Split from views-doc.ts for the line cap.\n */\n\nexport const dependenciesAndParamsSection = `## Dependencies\n\nThe \\`dependencies\\` array controls two things:\n1. **Which data is loaded** \u2014 matching \\`.card\\` files arrive parsed in \\`cards\\`;\n   any other matching file arrives as metadata in \\`files\\`\n   (\\`{path, size, mtimeMs}\\` \u2014 fetch content with \\`readFile\\`/\\`fileUrl\\`)\n2. **When to re-render** \u2014 the view refreshes automatically when matching files change\n\nUse glob patterns relative to the box root:\n- \\`\"box/inbox/**/*.card\"\\` \u2014 all cards in the inbox\n- \\`\"store/archive/**/*.record.card\"\\` \u2014 all record cards in the archive\n- \\`\"store/todos/**/*.card\"\\` \u2014 all todo cards\n- \\`\"box/**/*.card\"\\` \u2014 everything in box/\n- \\`\"store/playground/Playground.attach/**/*.jsonl\"\\` \u2014 a card's attachment files\n\n### Reading a card's attachments\n\nA card's extra data usually lives in its attach scope. The card's\n\\`attachments\\` listing (or a dependency glob into the \\`.attach/\\` dir) tells\nyou what exists; \\`readFile\\` fetches content on demand. Attachments can be\nvery large \u2014 fetch only what you render. A byte-range tail is the right way\nto show \"recent entries\" from an append-only log:\n\n\\`\\`\\`tsx\nexport const dependencies = [\n  \"store/playground/*.card\",\n  \"store/playground/Playground.attach/**/*.jsonl\",\n];\n\nexport default function PlaygroundHistory({ files, readFile }) {\n  const [entries, setEntries] = useState([]);\n  const log = files.find((f) => f.path.endsWith(\"sessions/history.jsonl\"));\n  useEffect(() => {\n    if (!log) return;\n    // Tail the last 64KB \u2014 enough for recent entries, cheap for a huge log.\n    readFile(log.path, { start: -65536 }).then((text) => {\n      const lines = text.split(\"\\\\n\").filter(Boolean);\n      // A tail can start mid-line; drop the first line unless we read from byte 0.\n      if (log.size > 65536) lines.shift();\n      setEntries(lines.map((line) => JSON.parse(line)));\n    });\n  }, [log && log.path, log && log.mtimeMs]);\n  return <ul>{entries.map((e, i) => <li key={i}>{e.summary}</li>)}</ul>;\n}\n\\`\\`\\`\n\n\\`mtimeMs\\` in the effect deps makes the view re-fetch when the log grows.\nFor images and audio, don't fetch \u2014 render \\`<img src={fileUrl(f.path)} />\\`.\n\n### Writing files from a view\n\nViews can create, overwrite, and append to box files (everything except\n\\`.card\\` files \u2014 cards validate, so they go through the card API or\n\\`cb create\\`). A ViewFile is an identity + version: its \\`etag\\` is the\nversion token. The conflict-safe pattern \u2014 assert the version you read,\nand refresh instead of clobbering when someone else changed the file:\n\n\\`\\`\\`tsx\nexport default function Notes({ files, readFile, writeFile, commitFile }) {\n  const [file, setFile] = useState(files.find((f) => f.path.endsWith(\"notes.md\")));\n  const [text, setText] = useState(\"\");\n  useEffect(() => { if (file) readFile(file.path).then(setText); }, [file && file.etag]);\n\n  async function save() {\n    try {\n      // expect: file \u2192 the write fails (412) if the file changed since we read it\n      const next = await writeFile(file.path, { content: text, expect: file });\n      setFile(next); // the returned ViewFile is the new version \u2014 chain saves from it\n    } catch (e) {\n      if (e.name === \"ViewFileConflictError\") {\n        setFile(e.current); // someone else wrote \u2014 e.current is the fresh version; reload\n        return;\n      }\n      throw e;\n    }\n  }\n\n  return <div>\n    <textarea value={text} onChange={(e) => setText(e.target.value)} />\n    <button onClick={save}>Save</button>\n    <button onClick={() => commitFile(file.path, \"Edited notes from view\")}>Commit</button>\n  </div>;\n}\n\\`\\`\\`\n\n- \\`expect: someViewFile\\` \u2014 overwrite only if unchanged since you read it.\n- \\`expect: \"absent\"\\` \u2014 create-only; conflicts if the file appeared meanwhile.\n- Omit \\`expect\\` for unconditional writes (append-only logs rarely need it).\n\n### Calling external APIs (LLMs) from a view\n\nBrowsers can't call provider APIs directly: providers (correctly) refuse\nCORS so API keys never live in pages. Views go through the box's **API\nadapters** instead \u2014 \\`adapterFetch(adapter, {path, ...init})\\` hits\n\\`/api/adapters/<adapter>/<path>\\`, where the server injects the key from\n\\`config/connectors/<adapter>.secret.json\\` (\\`{\"apiKey\": \"...\"}\\`).\nAdapters: \\`replicate\\`, \\`mistral\\`, \\`anthropic\\`, \\`openai\\`.\n\n\\`\\`\\`tsx\nconst resp = await adapterFetch(\"replicate\", {\n  path: \"/v1/models/meta/llama-2-7b-chat/predictions\",\n  method: \"POST\",\n  headers: { \"Content-Type\": \"application/json\" },\n  body: JSON.stringify({ input: { prompt } }),\n});\nconst prediction = await resp.json();\n// Polling URLs from the provider are absolute; pass them straight back \u2014\n// the origin is stripped and routed through the adapter:\nconst poll = await adapterFetch(\"replicate\", { path: prediction.urls.get });\n\\`\\`\\`\n\nNever read a \\`*.secret.json\\` into the browser with \\`readFile\\` and never\nput an API key in view source \u2014 the adapter exists so keys stay\nserver-side.\n\n**Git semantics.** Writes never auto-commit \u2014 interactive saves are chatty\nand a commit per keystroke would spam history. \\`gitStatus\\` on each\nViewFile shows working-tree state (\\`\"dirty\"\\`, \\`\"untracked\"\\`, absent =\ncommitted clean) so a view can render an unsaved-changes indicator. Call\n\\`commitFile(path, message)\\` at meaningful boundaries \u2014 it commits the\nfile's card and attach scope (and nothing else); a card path sweeps its\nscope, an attachment path sweeps its owning card + scope. Anything left\nuncommitted is safe: box housekeeping sweeps stray changes on wakeup.\n\n## Query Parameters (path and others)\n\nViews receive query parameters via \\`params\\`. The most important parameter is \\`path\\`, which scopes what the view shows.\n\n**Always provide a \\`path\\` parameter** when linking to or embedding a view:\n- \\`path=/\\` \u2014 the entire box\n- \\`path=store/archive/bills/\\` \u2014 a specific directory\n- \\`path=store/archive/bills/Electric.record.card\\` \u2014 a specific card\n\nThe view component reads it from \\`params.path\\`:\n\n\\`\\`\\`tsx\nexport default function MyView({ cards, params }) {\n  const viewPath = params.path || \"/\";\n  // Filter cards by path, or use it as context\n  const filtered = viewPath === \"/\"\n    ? cards\n    : cards.filter(c => c.path.startsWith(viewPath));\n  // ...\n}\n\\`\\`\\`\n\nYou can also use custom query parameters for filtering, sorting, etc. \u2014 they all arrive in \\`params\\`.\n\n## React\n\nReact is provided automatically. **Do NOT import React** \u2014 the build system handles it. If you do write \\`import React from \"react\"\\`, it will still work (the compiler intercepts it), but it's unnecessary.\n\nYou can use all standard React hooks: \\`useState\\`, \\`useEffect\\`, \\`useMemo\\`, \\`useCallback\\`, \\`useRef\\`, etc.`;\n", "/**\n * Generate the views reference documentation for agents.\n *\n * Called by generate-docs.ts to produce docs/generated/views.md.\n */\n\nimport { dependenciesAndParamsSection } from \"./views-doc-files.js\";\n\nconst introSection = `# Views: Agent-Generated React Components\n\nViews are \\`.tsx\\` files in the \\`views/\\` directory at the box root. They get compiled server-side and rendered in the browser \u2014 either as standalone pages or embedded in chat messages.\n\n## When to Create a View\n\nCreate a view when:\n- The user asks to **see** data in a specific way (dashboard, summary, chart, timeline)\n- A collection of cards would benefit from a structured visual layout\n- You want to present data interactively (filtering, sorting, expanding details)\n- The user asks for a \"page\" or \"dashboard\" for something\n\nDon't create a view for:\n- Simple one-off answers (just reply in chat)\n- Static text that doesn't change (use a card or document)\n- Something that requires server-side processing (use a job instead)`;\n\nconst fileFormatSection = `## File Format\n\nEach view is a \\`.tsx\\` file with named exports for metadata and a default export for the component:\n\n\\`\\`\\`tsx\nexport const name = \"Ledger Overview\";\nexport const description = \"Summary of ledger assets and their status\";\nexport const dependencies = [\"store/archive/**/*.record.card\", \"store/archive/**/*.memo.card\"];\nexport const modes = [\"page\", \"chat\"];\n\nexport default function EstateOverview({ cards, navigate, boxSlug, params }) {\n  const viewPath = params.path || \"/\";\n  // Use viewPath to scope what the view shows\n  const records = cards.filter(c => c.tagName === \"record\");\n  const memos = cards.filter(c => c.tagName === \"memo\");\n\n  return (\n    <div>\n      <h2>Ledger Overview</h2>\n      <p>{records.length} records, {memos.length} memos</p>\n      <ul>\n        {records.map(card => (\n          <li key={card.path}>\n            <strong>{card.attrs.title || card.path}</strong>\n            {card.status && <span> \u2014 {card.status}</span>}\n          </li>\n        ))}\n      </ul>\n    </div>\n  );\n}\n\\`\\`\\``;\n\nconst metadataAndPropsSection = `## Metadata Exports\n\n| Export | Type | Required | Description |\n|--------|------|----------|-------------|\n| \\`name\\` | string | Yes | Human-readable name shown in UI |\n| \\`description\\` | string | Yes | What this view shows |\n| \\`dependencies\\` | string[] | Yes | Glob patterns for files that affect rendering |\n| \\`modes\\` | string[] | Yes | Where the view can appear: \\`\"page\"\\`, \\`\"chat\"\\`, or both |\n| \\`rendersCardTypes\\` | string[] | No | Card types this view renders \u2014 see below |\n\n### Rendering a card type\n\nA view that exports \\`rendersCardTypes\\` becomes the **default renderer for\nthose card types everywhere cards display** \u2014 the card page\n(\\`/card/<path>\\`), chat embeds, and peeks. This is how a custom card type\n(e.g. a box-local schema) gets a custom UI without touching the app:\n\n\\`\\`\\`tsx\nexport const name = \"Sandbox\";\nexport const description = \"Interactive sandbox card UI\";\nexport const dependencies = [\"**/*.sandbox.card\"];\nexport const modes = [\"page\", \"chat\"];\nexport const rendersCardTypes = [\"sandbox\"];\n\nexport default function Sandbox({ cards, params }) {\n  const card = cards.find((c) => c.path === params.path);\n  // params.path is the card being displayed; dependencies must cover the\n  // type so the card arrives in \\`cards\\`.\n  ...\n}\n\\`\\`\\`\n\nThe built-in renderers (Source, Card Tree, ...) stay available through the\nrenderer toggle. One view per type: if several views claim the same card\ntype, the first by slug order wins. Without \\`rendersCardTypes\\`, custom\ntypes fall back to the generic built-ins.\n\n## Component Props\n\nThe default export receives a \\`ViewProps\\` object:\n\n| Prop | Type | Description |\n|------|------|-------------|\n| \\`cards\\` | ViewCard[] | All cards matching the dependency globs |\n| \\`files\\` | ViewFile[] | Metadata for non-card files matching the globs: \\`{path, size, mtimeMs}\\` |\n| \\`readFile\\` | (path, opts?) => Promise<string> | Fetch a file's text; \\`{start, end}\\` byte range, negative start = tail |\n| \\`fileUrl\\` | (path) => string | URL for a box file \u2014 \\`<img src>\\`, \\`<audio src>\\`, download links |\n| \\`writeFile\\` | (path, {content, expect?}) => Promise<ViewFile> | Create/overwrite (parents made); returns the new ViewFile; never commits |\n| \\`appendFile\\` | (path, {content, expect?}) => Promise<ViewFile> | Append (creates when missing); same semantics |\n| \\`commitFile\\` | (path, message) => Promise<{committed, hash?}> | Commit the file + its attachments, nothing else |\n| \\`adapterFetch\\` | (adapter, {path, ...init}) => Promise<Response> | Call an external API with the box's key injected server-side |\n| \\`navigate\\` | (path: string) => void | Navigate within the box (e.g., \\`navigate(\"chat\")\\`) |\n| \\`boxSlug\\` | string | The current box slug |\n| \\`params\\` | Record<string, string> | Query parameters from the URL (e.g., \\`params.path\\`) |\n| \\`reportActivity\\` | (kind, detail?) => void | When open in the chat companion pane, tell the agent the user touched this card. Writes auto-report \\`\"modified\"\\`; call \\`reportActivity(\"explored\", detail)\\` when the user changes the view's *parameters* (filters, ranges, a selected tab) without changing data. The optional \\`detail\\` is a short free-text string surfaced to the agent as the \\`<card-activity>\\` element's text (e.g. the query the user typed and its top result) \u2014 it overwrites any prior detail for the same kind, so calling it on every keystroke is fine. A no-op for inline/page renders, so always safe to call. |\n\n### ViewCard Structure\n\nEach card in the \\`cards\\` array has:\n\n\\`\\`\\`typescript\n{\n  path: string;        // Relative path (e.g., \"store/archive/Foo.record.card\")\n  tagName: string;     // Root element name (e.g., \"record\", \"memo\")\n  attrs: Record<string, string>;  // All attributes on the root element\n  text?: string;       // Text content of the root element (if leaf node)\n  status?: string;     // Shortcut for attrs.status\n  children?: ViewCardChild[];     // Child elements (recursive)\n  attachments?: ViewFile[];       // Deep listing of the card's attach scope\n}\n\\`\\`\\`\n\nChild elements have the same shape: \\`{ tagName, attrs, text?, children? }\\`.\n\n\\`attachments\\` is how a view discovers what lives next to a card \u2014 every file\nin the card's attach scope, recursively, as \\`{path, size, mtimeMs}\\` with\nbox-relative paths (e.g.\n\\`store/playground/Playground.attach/sessions/history.jsonl\\`). Content is\nnever inlined \u2014 attachments can be huge or binary \u2014 fetch it with\n\\`readFile(path)\\` or point an \\`<img>\\`/\\`<audio>\\` at \\`fileUrl(path)\\`.`;\n\nconst showingFilesSection = `## Showing Files in Chat\n\nTo show a file to the user, use a \\`view:\\` link with the file path:\n\n\\`\\`\\`\n[Meeting Notes](view:store/notes/meeting.md)\n[Recipe](view:store/archive/Pasta.recipe.card)\n\\`\\`\\`\n\nThe system automatically picks the right viewer based on file type:\n- \\`.md\\` files render as formatted Markdown\n- \\`.card\\` files use the card viewer (card-type-specific renderers if available, generic tree view otherwise)\n- Directories show a listing of subdirectories and cards\n- Other files show as raw text\n\nTo open as a companion panel alongside chat, add \\`?zoom\\`:\n\\`\\`\\`\n[Meeting Notes](view:store/notes/meeting.md?zoom)\n\\`\\`\\`\n\nTo force a specific viewer, use \\`?view=\\`:\n\\`\\`\\`\n[Raw XML](view:store/archive/Pasta.recipe.card?view=raw)\n\\`\\`\\`\n\nDirectory paths work too:\n\\`\\`\\`\n[Catalog](view:store/catalogs/My_Catalog)\n\\`\\`\\`\n\n**Note:** \\`view:\\` links are for file and directory paths only. Do not use them for custom view slugs.`;\n\nconst companionViewsSection = `### Inline vs Companion Views\n\nThere are two ways views appear in chat:\n\n**Inline (default)** \u2014 the view renders inside the chat message, scrolls with the conversation:\n\\`\\`\\`\n[Meeting Notes](view:store/notes/meeting.md)\n\\`\\`\\`\n\n**Companion panel** \u2014 adding \\`?zoom\\` opens the view as a persistent side panel alongside the chat:\n\\`\\`\\`\n[Meeting Notes](view:store/notes/meeting.md?zoom)\n\\`\\`\\`\n\nThe companion panel:\n- Stays visible while the user continues chatting (sticky \u2014 doesn't scroll away)\n- Shows side-by-side with chat on desktop, stacked on mobile\n- Has a close button \u2014 the user dismisses it when done\n- Updates live when underlying files change (same SSE mechanism as inline views)\n- If the agent writes another zoom link and the user clicks it, it replaces the current companion\n\nUse inline views for quick, one-off data displays within a conversation turn. Use companion views when the user needs to reference the view while continuing to talk \u2014 collaborative editing, storybuilding, reviewing a document, exploring data.\n\n### How the Agent Knows a Companion View is Open\n\nWhen a companion view is open, every user message includes a \\`zoomed-view\\` attribute:\n\\`\\`\\`xml\n<typed zoomed-view=\"view:ledger-overview?path=/\">What about the furniture?</typed>\n\\`\\`\\`\n\nThis tells the agent what the user is looking at, so it can tailor its responses. The attribute value is the full view URI (without \\`&zoom\\`).\n\nThe per-turn \\`<chat-app>\\` snapshot also carries this as the read-only \\`open-card\\` attribute (box-relative path), plus a \\`<card-activity kind=\"\u2026\">\\` child element per kind of activity since the agent's last reply (\\`scrolled\\`/\\`navigated\\`/\\`explored\\`/\\`modified\\`), the element text being the optional free-text detail a view attaches via \\`reportActivity(kind, detail)\\` (e.g. the query typed). A view contributes the \\`explored\\` signal by calling \\`reportActivity(\"explored\", detail)\\` when the user changes its parameters; writes contribute \\`modified\\` automatically. For the precise change set, the agent runs \\`cb chat whats-changed --card <path>\\`.\n\n**Note:** Companion views are a chat-only feature. The \\`&zoom\\` parameter and \\`zoomed-view\\` attribute are only meaningful in the chat frontend \u2014 other agent contexts (jobs, wakeup) don't support them.`;\n\nconst reportingActivitySection = `## Reporting Card Activity (\\`reportActivity\\`)\n\nIf your view is meant to be opened beside the chat \u2014 a companion view the user pokes at while talking \u2014 report what they do, so the chat agent has context. Otherwise the agent sees only the card's *config file*, never the live state the user is looking at. For a static, read-only display there's nothing to report; skip this.\n\nThe signal reaches the agent as read-only \\`<card-activity kind=\"\u2026\">\\` child elements of the per-turn snapshot \u2014 one per kind (\\`scrolled\\`/\\`navigated\\`/\\`explored\\`/\\`modified\\`), with the element text being your optional free-text **detail** for that kind. \\`reportActivity\\` is a no-op outside the companion pane, so it's always safe to call.\n\n**What's automatic vs. what you wire:**\n- \\`modified\\` \u2014 automatic. A successful \\`writeFile\\`/\\`appendFile\\`/\\`commitFile\\` reports it with the path; don't call it yourself.\n- \\`scrolled\\` \u2014 automatic (the pane watches its own scroll).\n- \\`explored\\` \u2014 **you call it.** This is the important one: fire it when the user changes what the view is *showing* without changing data \u2014 the query they typed, a filter, a selected tab, a slider \u2014 and pass a detail describing the new state.\n- \\`navigated\\` \u2014 automatic when a link inside the view opens another card.\n\n**How to write the detail.** Report \\`explored\\` from your *primary* inputs, not every control. The detail is a short, human-legible line of what the user is now looking at \u2014 the input plus the salient result \u2014 because that exact string is what the agent reads (the \\`<card-activity>\\` element text). Keep it terse (a hint, not a dump): \\`boat-water+road -> boats (0.568)\\`, not the whole result list.\n\n**Pattern: report from a text input as the user types.** Reporting on every keystroke is fine \u2014 details overwrite per kind, so \\`b\\`,\\`bo\\`,\\`boat\\` collapse to the final state; no debounce needed.\n\n\\`\\`\\`tsx\nfunction NearestNeighbors({ reportActivity }) {\n  const [query, setQuery] = useState(\"king\");\n  const results = useNearest(query); // your computation\n\n  // Tell the chat agent what the user is exploring + the top hit.\n  useEffect(() => {\n    const q = query.trim();\n    if (!q) return;\n    const top = results[0];\n    const detail = top ? q + \" -> \" + top.word + \" (\" + top.sim.toFixed(3) + \")\" : q;\n    reportActivity(\"explored\", detail);\n  }, [query, results, reportActivity]);\n\n  return <input value={query} onChange={(e) => setQuery(e.target.value)} />;\n}\n\\`\\`\\`\n\nFor a tab or filter, call it in the handler instead: \\`onClick={() => { setTab(t); reportActivity(\"explored\", \"tab: \" + t); }}\\`. The agent can always run \\`cb chat whats-changed --card <path>\\` for the exact, git-grounded change set \u2014 \\`<card-activity> detail\\` is the cheap live hint, not the source of truth.`;\n\nconst examplesSection = `## Examples\n\n### Simple Card List\n\n\\`\\`\\`tsx\nexport const name = \"Todo List\";\nexport const description = \"Active todos\";\nexport const dependencies = [\"store/todos/**/*.card\"];\nexport const modes = [\"page\", \"chat\"];\n\nexport default function TodoList({ cards }) {\n  const todos = cards.filter(c => c.tagName === \"todo-list\");\n  return (\n    <div>\n      <h2>Todos</h2>\n      {todos.map(card => (\n        <div key={card.path} style={{ marginBottom: \"1rem\" }}>\n          <h3>{card.attrs.title}</h3>\n          {card.children?.filter(c => c.tagName === \"item\").map((item, i) => (\n            <div key={i} style={{ padding: \"0.25rem 0\", color: item.attrs.status === \"done\" ? \"#999\" : \"#000\" }}>\n              {item.attrs.status === \"done\" ? \"\\\\u2713\" : \"\\\\u25cb\"} {item.text}\n            </div>\n          ))}\n        </div>\n      ))}\n    </div>\n  );\n}\n\\`\\`\\`\n\n### Filtered Dashboard\n\n\\`\\`\\`tsx\nexport const name = \"Inbox Dashboard\";\nexport const description = \"Overview of pending inbox items\";\nexport const dependencies = [\"box/inbox/**/*.card\"];\nexport const modes = [\"page\"];\n\nexport default function InboxDashboard({ cards }) {\n  const [filter, setFilter] = useState(\"\");\n\n  const filtered = cards.filter(c =>\n    !filter || c.tagName.includes(filter) || c.path.includes(filter)\n  );\n\n  const byType = {};\n  for (const card of filtered) {\n    byType[card.tagName] = (byType[card.tagName] || 0) + 1;\n  }\n\n  return (\n    <div>\n      <h2>Inbox ({filtered.length} items)</h2>\n      <input\n        placeholder=\"Filter...\"\n        value={filter}\n        onChange={e => setFilter(e.target.value)}\n        style={{ padding: \"0.5rem\", marginBottom: \"1rem\", width: \"100%\" }}\n      />\n      <div style={{ display: \"flex\", gap: \"1rem\", marginBottom: \"1rem\" }}>\n        {Object.entries(byType).map(([type, count]) => (\n          <div key={type} style={{ padding: \"0.5rem 1rem\", background: \"#f0f0f0\", borderRadius: \"0.5rem\" }}>\n            <strong>{type}</strong>: {count}\n          </div>\n        ))}\n      </div>\n      <ul>\n        {filtered.map(card => (\n          <li key={card.path}>{card.path} ({card.tagName})</li>\n        ))}\n      </ul>\n    </div>\n  );\n}\n\\`\\`\\``;\n\nconst stylingAndErrorsSection = `## Styling\n\nViews render inside the app's existing layout. You can use:\n- Inline styles (as shown in examples)\n- Standard HTML/CSS\n- The app uses Tailwind CSS classes \u2014 these are available if you know them, but inline styles are fine\n\n## Error Handling\n\nIf your view has a syntax error, the browser shows the compile error instead of crashing. If your view throws at runtime, an error boundary catches it and shows the error with a retry button.`;\n\nexport function generateViewsDoc(): string {\n  return (\n    [\n      introSection,\n      fileFormatSection,\n      metadataAndPropsSection,\n      dependenciesAndParamsSection,\n      showingFilesSection,\n      companionViewsSection,\n      reportingActivitySection,\n      examplesSection,\n      stylingAndErrorsSection,\n    ].join(\"\\n\\n\") + \"\\n\"\n  );\n}\n", "/**\n * Generate the chat-voice reference documentation for agents.\n *\n * Called by generate-docs.ts to produce docs/generated/chat-voice.md.\n * Covers per-message TTS overrides in the chat frontend. The voice list\n * and base configuration live in the personality card rule\n * (docs/generated/card-personality.md).\n */\n\nexport function generateChatVoiceDoc(): string {\n  return `# Chat Voice: Per-Message TTS Overrides\n\nChat responses are spoken aloud when wrapped in \\`<speech>\\` tags. The base voice and delivery style come from the personality card's \\`<speaking-voice>\\` element \u2014 see \\`docs/generated/card-personality.md\\` for the available voices and style-instruction guidance.\n\nThis doc covers **per-message overrides** \u2014 changing the voice or instructions for a single spoken segment.\n\nOverrides apply only to the chat frontend. They have no effect in jobs, procedures, or non-chat contexts.\n\n## Base Behavior\n\nBy default, every \\`<speech>\\` segment uses the voice model and concatenated \\`<instruction>\\` text from the personality card's \\`<speaking-voice>\\`. An optional nested \\`<instructions>\\` tag inside \\`<speech>\\` *adds* to (not replaces) the base instructions:\n\n\\`\\`\\`xml\n<speech>I found three overdue items.\n<instructions>Gentle, not urgent.</instructions>\n</speech>\n\\`\\`\\`\n\nThe TTS model receives: \\`<base instructions from personality> Gentle, not urgent.\\`\n\nUse this for most delivery tweaks \u2014 emphasis, mood, pacing \u2014 where the underlying voice identity should stay the same.\n\n## Overriding the Voice\n\nUse the \\`voice\\` attribute on \\`<speech>\\` to pick a different voice for one segment. Valid values are the 13 voices listed in the personality card doc (\\`alloy\\`, \\`ash\\`, \\`ballad\\`, \\`cedar\\`, \\`coral\\`, \\`echo\\`, \\`fable\\`, \\`marin\\`, \\`onyx\\`, \\`sage\\`, \\`shimmer\\`, \\`nova\\`, \\`verse\\`).\n\n\\`\\`\\`xml\n<speech voice=\"onyx\">Stand by. Launching sequence initiated.</speech>\n\\`\\`\\`\n\nTypical uses:\n- Quoting someone else, or role-playing a different speaker\n- A voice whose qualities match the moment (a grave voice for bad news, a peppy one for celebration)\n- One-off dramatic effect\n\nAn unknown voice name logs a warning and falls back to the personality card's base voice.\n\n## Labeling the Speaker\n\nAdd a \\`name\\` attribute to show a small speaker label on that spoken chunk in the chat UI:\n\n\\`\\`\\`xml\n<speech name=\"Bob\" voice=\"onyx\">Hi, I'm Bob!</speech>\n\\`\\`\\`\n\nThe label is **display-only** \u2014 it changes how the chunk looks (and reads in the replay menu), not how it sounds. Pair it with \\`voice\\` when role-playing or quoting distinct speakers so each line is both voiced and labeled. Omit it for ordinary narration; an unlabeled chunk shows no label.\n\n## Replacing Base Instructions\n\nThe nested \\`<instructions>\\` tag normally appends to the base. To **replace** them entirely for one segment, add \\`override-instructions=\"1\"\\`:\n\n\\`\\`\\`xml\n<speech override-instructions=\"1\">\n<instructions>Urgent, sharp, near-whisper. Clipped consonants.</instructions>\nThe alarm just fired. Check the stove.\n</speech>\n\\`\\`\\`\n\nUse this sparingly \u2014 only when the base instructions actively conflict with the mood you want. Most of the time, *adding* context via a plain \\`<instructions>\\` tag is enough.\n\n## Combining Overrides\n\n\\`voice\\` and \\`override-instructions\\` combine freely:\n\n\\`\\`\\`xml\n<speech voice=\"ballad\" override-instructions=\"1\">\n<instructions>Theatrical, slow, with pauses for effect.</instructions>\nOnce upon a time, in a village at the edge of the woods...\n</speech>\n\\`\\`\\`\n\n## Experimenting\n\nThere's no dedicated voice-preview UI. To try out voices and instructions:\n\n1. Edit \\`config/main.personality.card\\` in the box.\n2. Reload the chat page \u2014 the frontend picks up the new \\`<speaking-voice>\\` config.\n3. Send a message and listen. Iterate.\n\nInstruction wording matters more than you'd expect. The TTS model responds best to sensory, concrete direction \u2014 pacing, pitch, affect, pronunciation \u2014 rather than abstract traits like \"be friendly.\" Good instructions read like stage directions: \"Low and hushed, with a slight tremble on emphasized words. Pause briefly after questions.\"\n`;\n}\n", "/**\n * Generate the narration-mode reference documentation for agents.\n *\n * Called by generate-docs.ts to produce docs/generated/narration-mode.md.\n * The chat system prompt has a tight 1-line pointer to this doc. Full\n * behavioral rules live here so the base prompt stays compact and the\n * agent only consults this when narration is on.\n */\n\nexport function generateNarrationModeDoc(): string {\n  return `# Narration Mode: Behavioral Rules\n\nActive when the \\`<chat-app>\\` snapshot at the top of a user message reports \\`narration=\"on\"\\`. Otherwise the chat behaves normally \u2014 these rules do not apply.\n\n## What changes\n\nThe user is dumping content (typically voice, long and loose, a stream of thoughts), not chatting. The mechanics of turns don't change \u2014 each user message gets a turn \u2014 but your turn defaults to **silent**:\n\n- No prose.\n- No \\`<speech>\\`. Voice-in does NOT imply voice-out here. The general \"respond with speech when the user speaks\" rule does not apply.\n- No \\`<callout>\\` unless the user explicitly asked you for something.\n- Don't echo the user, summarize what they said, or acknowledge-by-prose (\"I'll add that to your todos\"). The \\`<ack>\\` chip is the acknowledgement.\n- Don't reply to musings. A stream-of-thought dump may include rhetorical asides (\"maybe pasta?\", \"the kitchen is a mess\", \"I should probably do X\") that are NOT requests for input.\n\n## Tags\n\n**\\`<ack>\\`** \u2014 for discrete work you did. Icon-only when the action is the obvious thing the user asked for (e.g. they said \"add that to my recipe,\" you appended it \u2014 bare \\`<ack kind=\"appended\" ref=\"...\"/>\\` with no inner text). Inner text only when you did something the user couldn't have predicted from their input.\n\n**\\`<ack kind=\"no-response\"/>\\`** \u2014 for pure silence, when no work happened and no answer was called for. **Never** write \"No response requested\" or \"Got it\" as prose; use this tag.\n\n**\\`<callout context=\"...\">\\`** \u2014 for real questions, where the user explicitly asked you for something specific (information, lookup, double-check). Put the answer in the body; \\`context\\` is a short label that makes the callout standalone when surfaced detached (digest, notification preview). Use \\`<callout>\\`, not \\`<speech>\\` \u2014 the answer renders visually, not aloud.\n\n**\\`<speech>\\`** \u2014 only when (a) the user explicitly asked you to speak (\"read it back to me\"), or (b) they're clearly hands-busy and the answer is worth hearing aloud (driving, cooking, eyes-elsewhere). Default is silent even when the user spoke.\n\n## Capturing user content (recording into cards/files)\n\nThe user's input is a transcription of their speech, not their typed words. Punctuation is machine-inserted from prosody \u2014 don't infer meaning from a comma vs. a period, and trust sentence boundaries lightly. Homophones may be wrong (\"to/too/two\", \"their/there\", names that sound like common words); fix only when context makes the right one obvious.\n\nVoice-control trigger phrases (\"send message\", \"mic off\", \"start over\") are detected client-side and arrive as tags (e.g. \\`<send-message phrase=\"...\" />\\`), not words. If a trigger phrase still appears as plain words in the text \u2014 especially repeated, or right next to its tag \u2014 the first utterance most likely wasn't detected when spoken. Treat it as control machinery, not content: never record trigger phrases into cards, and don't read intent into the repetition.\n\nWhen you record content into a card, file, or todo, use the user's wording and voice \u2014 don't paraphrase or smooth into bland prose. Three fixes worth applying:\n\n1. **Self-corrections.** Use the revised version, not both. \"Call Maria Thursday. No, sorry, Friday.\" \u2192 record \"Call Maria Friday\".\n2. **Obvious mishears.** When context makes the correct word unambiguous, fix it. The user clearly talking about LLMs and one mention came through as \"elements\" \u2192 write \"LLMs\". Don't guess.\n3. **Word fillers, sparingly.** \\`like\\` as a comma-substitute (\"I was, like, so tired\") and \\`you know\\` / \\`I mean\\` as conversational tags drop cleanly. Words like \\`well\\`, \\`so\\`, \\`basically\\`, \\`actually\\` usually carry meaning \u2014 keep them. Collapse stuttering: \"the the meeting\" \u2192 \"the meeting\".\n\nWhen in doubt, keep the word.\n\n## Priorities\n\nTool-driven action (capture, file, follow up, schedule) is the primary work. Conversation is incidental.\n`;\n}\n", "/**\n * Generate the python-tools reference documentation for agents.\n *\n * Called by generate-docs.ts to produce docs/generated/python-tools.md.\n * Covers the project convention for invoking Python CLI tools: use `uvx`\n * with a version pin at the call site rather than installing globally.\n */\n\nexport function generatePythonToolsDoc(): string {\n  return `# Python Tools\n\nPython CLI tools (docling, OCR utilities, document converters, etc.) are invoked through \\`uvx\\` \u2014 the Python analog of \\`npx\\`. Each invocation runs the tool in an isolated, cached environment with no global install.\n\n## The Rule\n\n**Always pin a version at the call site.** Without a pin, a fresh box or an evicted cache resolves to whatever is latest on PyPI that day, which breaks reproducibility silently.\n\n\\`\\`\\`bash\nuvx docling@2.14.0 <args>\n# or, for tools where the CLI name differs from the package name:\nuvx --from 'docling==2.14.0' docling <args>\n\\`\\`\\`\n\n## What Not To Do\n\n- Don't \\`pip install\\` globally or into a shared venv \u2014 versions drift, environments collide.\n- Don't add Python deps to \\`package.json\\` or a project-level \\`requirements.txt\\` just to call a CLI. Use that path only when you need to **import** the library in Python code (in which case it belongs in a real project venv, not a CLI invocation).\n- Don't invoke \\`uvx <tool>\\` without a version \u2014 it works locally and surprises you later.\n\n## When Multiple Scripts Use the Same Tool\n\nIf two or more callers need the same tool at the same version, lift the pin to a single constant near the call sites (e.g., a \\`PYTHON_TOOLS\\` map in a shared module) rather than duplicating the literal across files. Don't graduate to a central manifest until there's actual duplication.\n\n## uv Itself\n\n\\`uv\\` is the runtime that \\`uvx\\` belongs to. It must be installed on the host (\\`curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh\\`). The tool/package cache lives at \\`~/.cache/uv\\` and is shared across all invocations by the same user, so the first \\`uvx docling@...\\` pays the download cost and subsequent runs reuse the cached wheels.\n`;\n}\n", "/**\n * Directory layout and intake mechanisms \u2014 the shape of the box and how\n * items get into it.\n *\n * This is the in-box agent-facing summary. The canonical directory list\n * lives in BOX_DIRS (src/cli/lib/paths.ts) and the developer-facing\n * reference is docs/box-layout.md. When you change directories here, keep\n * those two in sync \u2014 drift between them has caused confusion before.\n */\n\nexport function directoryLayoutSection(): string[] {\n  return [\n    \"## Directory Layout\",\n    \"\",\n    \"Location is state \u2014 a card's directory determines its lifecycle stage:\",\n    \"\",\n    \"| Directory | Purpose |\",\n    \"|-----------|---------|\",\n    \"| `box/inbox/` | Incoming items to be triaged |\",\n    \"| `box/inbox/intake/` | Items being prepared before triage (transcription, OCR, filename normalization). |\",\n    \"| `box/inbox/staged/` | Intake-complete; waiting for the triage agent. |\",\n    \"| `box/inbox/triaged/<category>/` | Categorized; awaiting the handler procedure. |\",\n    \"| `box/inbox/triaged/_unsure/` | Held low-confidence items, paired with a question card. |\",\n    \"| `box/inbox/unhandled/` | Items with no clear destination |\",\n    \"| `box/jobs/` | Pending job cards for the reactor to process |\",\n    \"| `box/questions/` | Pending questions for the user |\",\n    \"| `box/resources/` | Synced external state |\",\n    \"| `box/output/` | Outbound cards (telegram messages, etc.) \u2014 flushed by `cb finalize` |\",\n    \"| `box/pool/` | Items being actively worked on |\",\n    \"| `store/archive/` | Processed/completed items |\",\n    \"| `store/calendar/` | Calendar events (.ics files) \u2014 two-way sync with Google Calendar |\",\n    \"| `store/drive/` | Google Drive files (spreadsheets as JSON, docs as markdown) \u2014 two-way sync |\",\n    \"| `store/integrated/` | Feedback absorbed into guides |\",\n    \"| `store/recipes/` | Recipe collection (subdirectories for organization) |\",\n    \"| `store/reviews/retro/` | Retrospective run reports \u2014 what the retrospective observed in past chats and which belief edits it made |\",\n    \"| `store/todos/` | Active todo lists \u2014 human action items |\",\n    \"| `store/trash/` | Soft-deleted items |\",\n    \"| `people/` | Person cards \u2014 key people referenced from briefings |\",\n    \"| `config/` | Box configuration |\",\n    \"\",\n  ];\n}\n\nexport function howItemsEnterSection(): string[] {\n  return [\n    \"## How Items Enter the Box\",\n    \"\",\n    \"You do NOT manually place items in directories. Items arrive through these mechanisms:\",\n    \"\",\n    \"- **Capture UI** \u2014 the user records voice memos, takes photos, or types text in the web interface. These are saved to `box/inbox/` automatically and processed via the `process-captures` procedure.\",\n    \"- **Connectors** \u2014 external services (Gmail, Telegram, Google Calendar, Google Drive) sync during `cb wakeup`. Connectors create cards in `box/inbox/` and job cards in `box/jobs/` for processing.\",\n    \"- **`cb create`** \u2014 the CLI command creates cards from templates. Use this when YOU need to create a card (e.g., a question, todo, or record). Example: `cb create box/questions/Color.question.card -t question`\",\n    \"- **Chat** \u2014 users send messages through the chat UI, which creates/updates chat-thread cards.\",\n    \"- **Clerk browser extension** \u2014 the user's \\\"Comment on this page\\\" captures a web page as a `*.webpage.card`: the readable markdown rendering as its body, with `source`/`captured`/`frozen` frontmatter, plus a frozen self-contained snapshot at `attach/page.frozen`. The user's remarks live in a separate `*.commentary.card` *inside the webpage card's attach scope* (`<basename>.attach/`); the webpage view surfaces them inline, and bare `{% source %}` anchors there default to the containing page. \\\"Save page\\\" produces the same `*.webpage.card` without the commentary. It lands in the chosen `<destination for=\\\"commentary\\\">` landmark dir, or `box/inbox/` by default.\",\n    \"\",\n    \"Two parallel sorting paths process items that land in `box/inbox/`:\",\n    \"\",\n    \"- **Inbox jobs (legacy)** \u2014 the wakeup cycle creates job cards in `box/jobs/` for the reactor to process. This is the historical path; most current routing still goes through it.\",\n    \"- **The intake \u2192 triage \u2192 handle pipeline (new)** \u2014 see `docs/plans/triage-design.md`. Items move through `box/inbox/intake/` \u2192 `box/inbox/staged/` \u2192 `box/inbox/triaged/<category>/`, driven by `cb intake` / `cb triage` / `cb handle`. The two paths coexist; the new pipeline isn't wired into wakeup yet.\",\n    \"\",\n    \"You don't need to move items to the inbox yourself \u2014 connectors and capture handle arrivals.\",\n    \"\",\n    \"**Common mistake:** Do NOT tell users to \\\"put\\\" or \\\"place\\\" files in directories. Users interact through the web UI, chat, or external services. Only agents use `cb create` and `cb mv`.\",\n    \"\",\n  ];\n}\n", "/**\n * Key cb commands \u2014 the everyday surface for working with cards.\n */\n\nexport function keyCommandsSection(): string[] {\n  return [\n    \"## Key Commands\",\n    \"\",\n    \"Use `cb` for all card operations. See `docs/generated/cb-commands.md`.\",\n    \"\",\n    \"- `cb create <path>` \u2014 Create a card from template (auto-detects type from filename)\",\n    \"- `cb mv <src> <dest>` \u2014 Move a card, updating all references\",\n    \"- `cb rm <path>` \u2014 Soft-delete a card to `store/trash/`\",\n    \"- `cb validate <path>` \u2014 Validate a card against its schema\",\n    \"- `cb answer <path>` \u2014 Answer a pending question\",\n    \"- `cb reactor` \u2014 Process all pending jobs in `box/jobs/`\",\n    \"- `cb finalize` \u2014 Flush outbound cards in `box/output/` (telegram messages, etc.)\",\n    \"- `cb health` \u2014 Scheduled-task health: failing/overdue/blocked tasks + scheduler liveness (exit 1 when unhealthy)\",\n    \"- `cb scenario list|run` \u2014 Run scenario tests against boxes\",\n    \"- `cb finish <job-file>` \u2014 Complete a job (deletes the job card and commits)\",\n    \"- `cb procedure run <name-or-path>` \u2014 Run a procedure (see `docs/generated/procedures.md`)\",\n    \"- `cb calendar [timespan]` \u2014 View upcoming calendar events (default 7d; supports `today`, `3d`, `2w`, `1m`)\",\n    \"- `cb chat self-note \\\"<body>\\\" [--ref <path>] [--commit <hash>]` \u2014 Post an agent-authored record into the live chat session. For use by scheduled sub-agents (daily rumination, weekly research) to leave a short summary of what they did, so the boxholder sees it on next chat revisit. Not a conversational message \u2014 Claude in chat knows not to reply.\",\n    \"- `cb feedback \\\"<message>\\\"` \u2014 Record an observation about CLI friction, confusing options, odd file placements, or unclear conventions. Silent: writes a file to `config/feedback/` and commits it without interrupting the current task. Use this any time something feels off about the tooling \u2014 confusing flag names, unclear error messages, awkward workflows, surprising behavior. Good feedback is specific and describes what was confusing and why.\",\n    \"\",\n  ];\n}\n", "/**\n * Calendar (Google Calendar two-way sync via .ics files in store/calendar/).\n */\n\nexport function calendarSection(): string[] {\n  return [\n    \"## Calendar\",\n    \"\",\n    \"Calendar events live as `.ics` files in `store/calendar/`. Sync with Google Calendar is **two-way**:\",\n    \"\",\n    \"- **View events:** `cb calendar` shows upcoming events. `cb calendar today`, `cb calendar 2w`, etc.\",\n    \"- **Create an event:** Write a new `.ics` file in `store/calendar/`. Next sync pushes it to Google Calendar.\",\n    \"  - Include `X-CB-CALENDAR-ID:<calendar-id>` to target a specific calendar (defaults to primary).\",\n    \"  - Optionally include `X-CB-REASON:<why>` and `X-CB-REF:<path>` for tracking.\",\n    \"- **Edit an event:** Modify a tracked `.ics` file directly. Next sync pushes the changes to Google Calendar.\",\n    \"- **Delete an event:** Add `X-CB-DELETE:<reason>` property to a tracked `.ics` file. Next sync deletes it from Google Calendar.\",\n    \"\",\n    \"**Timezone requirement:** Non-all-day events MUST include a VTIMEZONE component and TZID parameter on DTSTART/DTEND. Never create floating-time events \u2014 they'll be rejected. Use the box's local timezone (e.g., `America/Chicago`).\",\n    \"\",\n    \"Example minimal .ics for a new event:\",\n    \"```\",\n    \"BEGIN:VCALENDAR\",\n    \"VERSION:2.0\",\n    \"PRODID:-//Callback Box//EN\",\n    \"BEGIN:VTIMEZONE\",\n    \"TZID:America/Chicago\",\n    \"BEGIN:STANDARD\",\n    \"DTSTART:19701101T020000\",\n    \"RRULE:FREQ=YEARLY;BYMONTH=11;BYDAY=1SU\",\n    \"TZOFFSETFROM:-0500\",\n    \"TZOFFSETTO:-0600\",\n    \"TZNAME:CST\",\n    \"END:STANDARD\",\n    \"BEGIN:DAYLIGHT\",\n    \"DTSTART:19700308T020000\",\n    \"RRULE:FREQ=YEARLY;BYMONTH=3;BYDAY=2SU\",\n    \"TZOFFSETFROM:-0600\",\n    \"TZOFFSETTO:-0500\",\n    \"TZNAME:CDT\",\n    \"END:DAYLIGHT\",\n    \"END:VTIMEZONE\",\n    \"BEGIN:VEVENT\",\n    \"UID:unique-id-here\",\n    \"SUMMARY:Dentist appointment\",\n    \"DTSTART;TZID=America/Chicago:20260401T140000\",\n    \"DTEND;TZID=America/Chicago:20260401T150000\",\n    \"END:VEVENT\",\n    \"END:VCALENDAR\",\n    \"```\",\n    \"\",\n  ];\n}\n", "/**\n * Google Drive sync (sheets and docs in store/drive/).\n */\n\nexport function driveSection(): string[] {\n  return [\n    \"## Google Drive\",\n    \"\",\n    \"Google Drive content is synced into `store/drive/` (or wherever the card is placed). Sync is **two-way** for both file types.\",\n    \"\",\n    \"### Spreadsheets (`.sheet.card`)\",\n    \"\",\n    \"- **Find:** Look for `.sheet.card` files. The card lists the title, Google link, and sheet tabs.\",\n    \"- **Read:** Each tab is a JSON file in a subdirectory matching the card basename. Plain cells are bare values; formula cells are `{\\\"f\\\": \\\"=SUM(A1:B1)\\\", \\\"v\\\": \\\"$42.00\\\"}` with both the formula and computed result.\",\n    \"- **Edit:** Edit the JSON file directly and commit. For formula cells, edit the `f` field. Next sync pushes to Google Sheets.\",\n    \"- **Move:** Move the `.sheet.card` and its data directory together. The `drive-id` in the card maintains the link.\",\n    \"\",\n    \"### Documents (`.gdoc.card`)\",\n    \"\",\n    \"- **Find:** Look for `.gdoc.card` files. The card sits next to a sibling markdown file with the same basename (e.g., `Notes.doc.card` + `Notes.md`).\",\n    \"- **Read:** Open the `.md` file. The card itself only carries metadata.\",\n    \"- **Edit:** Edit the `.md` file and commit. Next sync pushes to Google Docs (markdown is converted to Doc format on the server).\",\n    \"- **Lossy content:** A `<lossy>` block in the card lists features in the upstream Doc that don't survive markdown export (comments, footnotes, embedded images, drawings, equations, suggestions, complex tables). When present, pushing local edits will destroy them. Surface the loss to the user before encouraging a push.\",\n    \"- **Conflicts:** If both local and remote changed since the last sync, the card status flips to `conflict` and the upstream content is written to `<basename>.remote.md`. Resolve by merging the two files, deleting `.remote.md`, and committing.\",\n    \"- **Move:** Move the `.gdoc.card` and its `.md` together. The `drive-id` in the card maintains the link.\",\n    \"\",\n    \"CLI: `cb drive inspect <url>`, `cb drive add <url> <path>`, `cb drive sync`, `cb drive status`.\",\n    \"\",\n  ];\n}\n", "/**\n * Box extensibility surfaces \u2014 procedures, guides, schedules, tricks.\n *\n * Procedures and guides are dynamic (their lists vary per-box and are scanned\n * by generate-docs). Schedules and tricks are static prose.\n */\n\nimport type { ProcedureSummary, GuideSummary } from \"../generate-docs.js\";\n\nexport function proceduresSection(procedures: ProcedureSummary[]): string[] {\n  if (procedures.length === 0) return [];\n  const lines: string[] = [\n    \"## Procedures\",\n    \"\",\n    \"Available procedures in `config/procedures/`:\",\n    \"\",\n  ];\n  for (const p of procedures) {\n    lines.push(`- **${p.name}** \u2014 ${p.description}`);\n  }\n  lines.push(\"\");\n  lines.push(\"Run with `cb procedure run <name>`. Read `docs/generated/procedures.md` before writing or modifying.\");\n  lines.push(\"\");\n  return lines;\n}\n\nexport function guidesSection(guides: GuideSummary[]): string[] {\n  if (guides.length === 0) return [];\n  const lines: string[] = [\n    \"## Guides\",\n    \"\",\n    \"Guides contain the boxholder's preferences for how you handle specific domains.\",\n    \"They define interaction patterns, pacing, and actions you wouldn't know from general knowledge.\",\n    \"**Read the guide before acting** \u2014 even if you know the domain, the guide tells you how this user wants it done.\",\n    \"\",\n  ];\n  for (const g of guides) {\n    const note = g.appliesTo ? ` \u2014 ${g.appliesTo}` : \"\";\n    lines.push(`- **${g.name}**${note} \u2192 \\`${g.compiledPath}\\``);\n  }\n  lines.push(\"\");\n  return lines;\n}\n\nexport function schedulesSection(): string[] {\n  return [\n    \"## Schedules\",\n    \"\",\n    \"Scheduled scripts in `config/schedules/` automate recurring tasks (connector syncs, maintenance, custom jobs).\",\n    \"Each is a `.scheduled-script.card` with a cron/at/rrule schedule.\",\n    \"\",\n    \"- `cb tick` \u2014 evaluate and run due schedules\",\n    \"- `cb scheduled` \u2014 list all schedules with status and last-run time\",\n    \"- `cb scheduler status` \u2014 show scheduler daemon status and configured boxes\",\n    \"\",\n    \"A background scheduler daemon (`cb scheduler start`) runs `cb tick` every 60 seconds for all configured boxes.\",\n    \"It is managed via launchd and auto-starts at login. Scheduler logs for this box are at `.callback-box/scheduler.jsonl` (JSONL format, one entry per tick cycle).\",\n    \"Each entry records which scripts ran, were skipped, or errored, with timestamps and durations.\",\n    \"\",\n    \"Agents can create or modify scheduled scripts for custom automation.\",\n    \"Schedule format includes cron expressions, throttling (`not-before`), chaining (`create-after-success`), and one-shot options \u2014 see `docs/generated/card-scheduled-script.md`.\",\n    \"\",\n  ];\n}\n\nexport function tricksSection(): string[] {\n  return [\n    \"## Tricks\",\n    \"\",\n    \"Custom scripts live in `tricks/scripts/`. Each trick is a directory with an `index.ts`.\",\n    \"Run with `cb trick <name>`. See `tricks/scripts/CLAUDE.md` for how to write tricks.\",\n    \"\",\n  ];\n}\n", "/**\n * Things relevant when responding to chat messages and the user-facing\n * surfaces around them: external converters, file attachments, custom views.\n */\n\nexport function externalToolsSection(): string[] {\n  return [\n    \"## External Tools\",\n    \"\",\n    \"`pandoc` is installed for converting document formats (.doc, .docx, .rtf, .odt, etc.) to plain text or markdown.\",\n    \"\",\n    \"Python CLI tools: `docs/generated/python-tools.md`.\",\n    \"\",\n  ];\n}\n\nexport function chatAttachmentsSection(): string[] {\n  return [\n    \"## Chat Attachments\",\n    \"\",\n    \"When the user attaches files in chat, their message contains `[fileN]` tokens plus a sibling `<attachments>` block mapping each token to a path:\",\n    \"\",\n    \"```\",\n    \"<attachments>\",\n    \"[file1]: tmp/2026-04-27T15-30-12-987Z_report.pdf\",\n    \"</attachments>\",\n    \"```\",\n    \"\",\n    \"Files live in `<box-root>/tmp/` \u2014 gitignored, transient. Read them with the right tool: Read for text/images/PDFs; `pandoc <path> -t plain` for .doc/.docx/.rtf/.odt.\",\n    \"\",\n    \"**`tmp/` is not storage.** After you've used a file, decide:\",\n    \"\",\n    \"- **Worth keeping** \u2014 move or copy it into the box where it belongs (e.g., create a card that references it as an attachment, or place it under `box/inbox/` or `store/`). Don't leave keepers in `tmp/`.\",\n    \"- **Done with it** \u2014 delete it (`rm tmp/<filename>`).\",\n    \"- Otherwise leave it for `cb wakeup` housekeeping, which sweeps `tmp/` files older than 7 days.\",\n    \"\",\n  ];\n}\n\nexport function selectionsSection(): string[] {\n  return [\n    \"## Selections\",\n    \"\",\n    \"The user can select text in a document they have open and attach it to a message. It arrives as a `<user-selection>` element:\",\n    \"\",\n    \"```\",\n    \"<user-selection ref=\\\"/store/notes/Bread.doc.card\\\" pos=\\\"body; heading: Proofing the dough (#proofing-the-dough); paragraph 2; ~line 42\\\">let it rise until doubled in size</user-selection>\",\n    \"```\",\n    \"\",\n    \"- The wrapped text is **what the user saw** \u2014 the rendered text, verbatim. Treat it as a quote; don't re-derive it.\",\n    \"- `ref` is the source document (box-relative path). Use it if you need the exact source markup or surrounding context.\",\n    \"- `pos` is a **rough** locator (section, nearest heading + its `#id`, paragraph, approximate line) \u2014 a hint for finding the original, not an exact offset. Clauses are omitted when not determinable.\",\n    \"- A `placement=\\\"estimated, ~N% through the message\\\"` attribute means the selection's *spot in this message* is approximate: the user grabbed it mid-speech but the phrase it anchored to was reworded by transcription, so it was positioned by rough timing (N% of the way through). The `pos`/`ref` still point at the real source; only its order within the message is a guess.\",\n    \"- It may appear **inline** inside `<typed>` (the user typed around it) or **appended after** a `<speech>` body (the user spoke and attached it separately). Treat both the same.\",\n    \"\",\n  ];\n}\n\nexport function viewsSection(): string[] {\n  return [\n    \"## Views\",\n    \"\",\n    \"Views are React components (`.tsx` files) in the `views/` directory that render in the browser.\",\n    \"Use views to create dashboards, data summaries, interactive explorers, or any custom UI for box data.\",\n    \"\",\n    \"- Views appear as full pages at `/<box>/views/<slug>?path=/` and can be embedded in chat messages\",\n    \"- Each view declares metadata (name, description, dependencies, modes) as named exports\",\n    \"- Views receive query parameters via `params` \u2014 always include `path=` to scope what the view shows\",\n    \"- Views re-render automatically when files matching their dependency globs change\",\n    \"- Views can read AND write box files: cards arrive parsed; attachments and\",\n    \"  other files arrive as metadata (`{path, size, mtimeMs, etag, gitStatus?}`),\",\n    \"  with on-demand `readFile` (byte-range tails for large logs), `fileUrl` for\",\n    \"  images/audio, conflict-safe `writeFile`/`appendFile` (etag preconditions),\",\n    \"  and `commitFile` for deliberate git commits of a file + its attachments\",\n    \"- Views call external APIs (LLMs) via `adapterFetch` \u2014 the server injects\",\n    \"  the key from `config/connectors/<adapter>.secret.json`; never read a\",\n    \"  secret file into the browser or put a key in view source\",\n    \"- A view exporting `rendersCardTypes = [\\\"<type>\\\"]` becomes that card\",\n    \"  type's default UI on card pages, peeks, and chat embeds \u2014 the way a\",\n    \"  custom card type gets a custom interface\",\n    \"- **Read `docs/generated/views.md` before creating or modifying views.**\",\n    \"\",\n  ];\n}\n", "/**\n * Card creation and inquiry: type catalogue, the cb create flow, and asking\n * the user via question cards.\n */\n\nimport type { ElementSchema } from \"cardworks\";\nimport { getAllTemplates } from \"../../schemas/templates.js\";\n\nexport function cardTypesSection(allSchemas: ElementSchema[]): string[] {\n  const lines: string[] = [\n    \"## Card Types\",\n    \"\",\n  ];\n  for (const schema of allSchemas) {\n    const hasDoc = schema.instructions ? ` \u2014 see \\`docs/generated/card-${schema.tagName}.md\\`` : \"\";\n    lines.push(`- **${schema.tagName}**${hasDoc}`);\n  }\n  lines.push(\"\");\n  lines.push(\"New card types can be defined in `config/schemas/` using `cardSchema()` (YAML frontmatter + markdown body) + Zod \u2014 see `config/schemas/CLAUDE.md` for how. Run `cb init` after adding a schema to generate rules and docs.\");\n  lines.push(\"\");\n  return lines;\n}\n\nexport function creatingCardsSection(): string[] {\n  const templates = getAllTemplates();\n  const lines: string[] = [\n    \"## Creating Cards\",\n    \"\",\n    \"Prefer `cb create` with templates over writing XML directly:\",\n    \"\",\n  ];\n  for (const t of templates) {\n    lines.push(`- \\`cb create <path> -t ${t.name}\\` \u2014 ${t.description}`);\n  }\n  lines.push(\"\");\n  lines.push(\"For array arguments (like question options), repeat the key: `options=\\\"Red\\\" options=\\\"Blue\\\"` or use JSON: `options='[\\\"Red\\\",\\\"Blue\\\"]'`\");\n  lines.push(\"\");\n  lines.push(\"**Two-step pattern:** For complex cards, create a minimal card first with `cb create`, then edit it to fill in details. This is often easier than getting all arguments right in one command. Example: `cb create box/questions/Q.question.card -t question-text memo=\\\"...\\\" prompt=\\\"...\\\"` then edit to add a `<directive>`.\");\n  lines.push(\"\");\n  lines.push(\"Always run `cb validate <path>` after creating or editing a card.\");\n  lines.push(\"\");\n  return lines;\n}\n\nexport function questionsSection(): string[] {\n  return [\n    \"## Questions\",\n    \"\",\n    \"Create question cards in `box/questions/` to ask the user.\",\n    \"Set `answered-by` to your agent name so the answer routes back to you.\",\n    \"Always include a `<directive>` element describing what you'll do with the answer \u2014 when the user answers, the system creates a follow-up job using this directive.\",\n    \"See `docs/generated/card-question.md` for templates.\",\n    \"\",\n  ];\n}\n", "/**\n * General agent behavior: principles, the role of git history, and a guide to\n * choosing where to record discovered information.\n */\n\nexport function generalPrinciplesSection(): string[] {\n  return [\n    \"## General Principles\",\n    \"\",\n    \"- Prefer `cb create` with templates over writing card files by hand\",\n    \"- Always `cb validate` after creating or modifying cards\",\n    \"- Commit with meaningful messages describing what changed and why\",\n    \"- Use `cb mv` to change card state (not `git mv` or `mv`)\",\n    \"- Use **absolute paths** for `ref` attributes (e.g., `ref=\\\"/store/archive/Foo.record.card\\\"`). Absolute paths start with `/` and are resolved from the box root. Avoid relative paths like `../../../store/...` \u2014 they're fragile and hard to read.\",\n    \"- This guide and `docs/generated/` are code-generated by `cb init`. If docs seem stale, re-run `cb init` to regenerate.\",\n    \"\",\n  ];\n}\n\nexport function gitHistorySection(): string[] {\n  return [\n    \"## Git History\",\n    \"\",\n    \"Git history is the primary record of what happened in the box. To understand what an agent did, what was processed, or when something changed, **check `git log` first** \u2014 don't search the filesystem for clues.\",\n    \"\",\n    \"Commits use structured trailers (key-value metadata after the message body):\",\n    \"\",\n    \"| Trailer | Meaning |\",\n    \"|---------|---------|\",\n    \"| `Triggered-By: cb procedure` | What command/system initiated this work |\",\n    \"| `Phase: triage` | Which phase of a pipeline (triage, fetch, analyze, brief, etc.) |\",\n    \"| `Session: <uuid>` | Links the commit to a specific agent session |\",\n    \"| `Job-Type: <type>` | Card type of the job that was finished |\",\n    \"| `Fallback: true` | Agent didn't commit; system made a fallback commit |\",\n    \"| `Commit-Source: procedure-fallback` | Procedure engine's fallback commit |\",\n    \"| `Created-By: <connector>` | Connector that created the content (e.g., gmail, telegram) |\",\n    \"\",\n    \"Useful queries:\",\n    \"- `git log --oneline -20` \u2014 recent activity overview\",\n    \"- `git log --all --grep='Phase: brief'` \u2014 find all brief-creation commits\",\n    \"- `git log -- box/inbox/` \u2014 history of a specific directory\",\n    \"- `git show <hash>` \u2014 full diff of what a commit changed\",\n    \"\",\n  ];\n}\n\nexport function whereToRecordSection(): string[] {\n  return [\n    \"## Where to Record What You Find\",\n    \"\",\n    \"The box has its own files for capturing knowledge. Use these \u2014 they persist across agent sessions and are visible to all agents working in this box.\",\n    \"\",\n    \"**IMPORTANT: Do NOT use `.claude/memory/` files for box information.** The box's own files (briefing cards, other cards, guides, personality) are the correct storage. `.claude/memory/` is not shared with other agents and is not part of the box's state.\",\n    \"\",\n    \"### Briefing cards \u2014 core context\",\n    \"\",\n    \"The briefing card (`briefing.briefing.card` at the box root) is the **primary place** for situational context \u2014 what this box is for, who the key people are, and essential facts every agent needs. Edit the briefing card when you discover core information:\",\n    \"\",\n    \"- **`<purpose>`** \u2014 what this box is for\",\n    \"- **`<key-people>`** \u2014 people central to the box's purpose, with aliases so agents can map names (\\\"Dad\\\" = Tomas). Create a person card at `people/First_Last.person.card` for each person you add.\",\n    \"- **`<agent-needs-to-know>`** \u2014 anything every agent must know that doesn't fit other fields\",\n    \"- **`<project-phase>`** \u2014 current stage if the box has time-bounded work\",\n    \"- **`<corrections>`** \u2014 only in response to observed mistakes, with a `<test>` for verification\",\n    \"\",\n    \"Think of the briefing as notes for a new team member \u2014 what do they need to know before they start? Read `docs/generated/card-briefing.md`.\",\n    \"\",\n    \"Directory briefings (`briefing.briefing.card` in any subdirectory) can explain what that directory contains.\",\n    \"\",\n    \"### Record / memo / bookmark cards \u2014 individual items\",\n    \"\",\n    \"A specific bank account, a piece of furniture, a contact's phone number. These go in `store/archive/` as cards.   \"\",\n    \"# Archive a processed item\",\n    \"cb mv box/pool/item.memo.card store/archive/item.memo.card\",\n    \"```\",\n    \"\",\n    \"## cb rm\",\n    \"\",\n    \"Soft-delete a card by The procedure engine runs each step in order, checking preconditions, executing actions, and validating results. Everything is tracked in git.\n\n## Running Procedures\n\n\\`\\`\\`bash\ncb procedure run process-captures                   # Run by name\ncb procedure run config/procedures/my.procedure.card  # Run by path\ncb procedure run process-captures --step transcribe # Run one step only\ncb procedure run process-captures --dry-run         # Preview steps\ncb procedure run process-captures --directive \"skip the music clips\"  # Pass directive\ncb procedure list                                   # List available procedures\ncb procedure status                                 # Show latest run status\ncb procedure gc                                     # Delete expired run dirs\n\\`\\`\\`\n\nProcedure definitions live in \\`config/procedures/\\`. Each run creates a tracking card in \\`procedure/runs/<name>_<timestamp>/\\`. Run dirs are a recent cache, not an archive: a run where every step skips is removed at completion, and finished runs get an \\`expires\\` stamp (30d completed / 90d failed, or the procedure card's \\`run-expiry\\`/\\`failed-run-expiry\\` override) that \\`cb procedure gc\\` enforces daily. Git history retains every committed run. To pin a specific run, set \\`expires: never\\` on its run card.\n\n## Directives\n\nA **directive** is an opaque runtime string passed when invoking a procedure. It appears as \\`<directive>...</directive>\\` in every agent's system prompt within the procedure, allowing callers to customize behavior without modifying the procedure card.\n\n\\`\\`\\`bash\ncb procedure run process-captures --directive \"Only process today's session\"\n\\`\\`\\`\n\nThe directive is also recorded as the \\`directive\\` field on the procedure-run card for auditability. Step prompts can reference \"the Directive\" to act on it.\n\n## Procedures in Jobs\n\nJob cards can trigger a procedure directly using the \\`<procedure>\\` element:\n\n\\`\\`\\`xml\n<some-job-type>\n<procedure ref=\"process-captures\">\n<directive>Focus on the meeting recordings</directive>\n</procedure>\n</some-job-type>\n\\`\\`\\`\n\nThe reactor detects \\`<procedure ref=\"...\">\\` in job cards and runs the procedure engine directly \u2014 no nested agent session is needed. The job is automatically finished when the procedure completes. If the procedure fails, the job remains for retry.\n\n## How Steps Work\n\nEach step has three optional phases:\n\n1. **Precheck** \u2014 Should this step run? Shell script that exits 0 (proceed), \\`$CHECK_SKIP\\` (skip), or non-zero (fail).\n2. **Run** \u2014 The main action: a shell command or an agent invocation.\n3. **Validate** \u2014 Did it work? Shell check + optional model evaluation.\n\nThe engine enforces a clean git state between steps. Every step's work is committed before the next step begins.\n\n## Procedure Card Structure\n\n\\`\\`\\`yaml\n---\nname: my-procedure\ndescription: What this procedure does\nsteps:\n  - id: first-step\n    description: Human-readable description of this step\n    precheck:\n      shells:\n        - |\n          # Exit 0 to proceed, exit $CHECK_SKIP to skip\n          count=$(ls box/inbox/*.card 2>/dev/null | wc -l)\n          if [ \"$count\" -eq 0 ]; then exit $CHECK_SKIP; fi\n          echo \"Found $count items\"\n      whys:\n        - Explanation of when/why this step should be skipped\n    run:\n      agents:\n        - model: haiku\n          max-turns: 20\n          prompt: |\n            Agent prompt goes here. Use YAML block scalars (\\`|\\`) for multi-line scripts and prompts.\n`;\n}\n\nfunction procedureGuideDetails(): string {\n  return `## Building Blocks\n\n### Shell Commands\n\nShell scripts run in the box root via \\`bash -c\\`. Three outcomes:\n- **Exit 0**: success\n- **Exit \\`$CHECK_SKIP\\`**: skip this step (prechecks only)\n- **Other exit code**: failure\n\n**Important:** macOS ships bash 3.2. Avoid bash 4+ features like \\`declare -A\\` (associative arrays). Use \\`shopt -s nullglob\\` instead of \\`for f in glob 2>/dev/null\\`.\n\n### Agent Invocations\n\n\\`\\`\\`yaml\nagents:\n  - model: haiku\n    max-turns: 25\n    prompt: |\n      Prompt text here...\n\\`\\`\\`\n\n- \\`model\\`: \\`haiku\\` (fast/cheap), \\`sonnet\\` (balanced), \\`opus\\` (most capable). Default: sonnet.\n- \\`max-turns\\`: Maximum tool-use rounds. If it fails, the agent gets one retry attempt.\n- \\`severity=\"abort\"\\` \u2014 Stop the procedure immediately\n\n### Why Entries\n\n\\`whys\\` entries explain the purpose of a phase. They're shown to:\n- Humans reading the procedure\n- Review models evaluating validation failures\n- Agents retrying failed steps\n\n## Writing a New Procedure\n\n1. Agents in procedure steps should use \\`cb mv\\` for cards.\n\n### Agent Prompt Guidelines\n\nAgent prompts in procedures should:\n- Start with a clear role statement (\"You are triaging inbox items...\")\n- List concrete steps (STEP 1, STEP 2, etc.)\n- Include exact shell/command examples the agent can copy\n- Include a commit step marked \"REQUIRED \u2014 do not skip\" with the expected message format\n- End with \"GIT: Do NOT add Co-Authored-By to commits.\"\n\n**Important:** If an agent doesn't commit, the engine creates a fallback commit with a generic message (tagged \\`Commit-Source: procedure-fallback\\`). Always instruct agents to commit explicitly so the git history is meaningful.\n\n## System Procedures and Migration\n\nProcedure cards in \\`config/procedures/\\` are installed by \\`cb init\\` from built-in templates. for await (const line of rl) {\n    if (!line.trim()) continue;\n    let raw: Record<string, unknown>;\n    try {\n      raw = JSON.parse(line);\n    } catch (_e) {\n      continue;\n    }\n\n    if cacheReadTokens: 0,\n      messageCount: 0,\n    };\n\n    bucket.inputTokens += usage.input_tokens || 0;\n    bucket.outputTokens += usage.output_tokens || 0;\n    bucket.cacheWriteTokens +=     55	export const MANIFEST_PATH = "config/migrations.jsonl";
    56	
    57	export interface ManifestEntry {
    58	  readonly name: string;
    59	  readonly "applied-at": string;
    60	}
     1	/**
     2	 * `cb migrate` — apply pending data migrations to the box.
     3	 *
     4	 * Compares the box's `config/migrations.jsonl` against the canonical
     5	 * `MIGRATIONS` list in `src/core/migrations.ts`. Runs any pending
     6	 * migrations in order, appending a manifest entry after each success.
     7	 *
     8	 * No auto-commit: the migrators leave their changes (plus the manifest
     9	 * update) in the working tree. The user reviews and commits, normally
    10	 * with `git commit -m "Apply migration X"`.
    11	 */
    12	
    13	import * as fs from "node:fs/promises";
    14	import * as path from "node:path";
    15	import { spawn } from "node:child_process";
    16	import { Command } from "commander";
    17	import { requireBoxRoot } from "../lib/paths.js";
    18	import {
    19	  MIGRATIONS,
    20	  MANIFEST_PATH,
    21	  type Migration,
    22	  type ManifestEntry,
    23	} from "../../core/migrations.js";
    24	import { PACKAGE_ROOT } from "../../lib/package-root.js";
    25	
    26	const CALLBACK_BOX_ROOT = PACKAGE_ROOT;
    27	
    28	class ManifestReadError extends Error {
    29	  readonly manifestPath: string;
    30	  constructor(manifestPath: string, cause: unknown) {
    31	    super(`failed to read migration manifest: ${manifestPath}`, { cause });
    32	    this.name = "ManifestReadError";
    33	    this.manifestPath = manifestPath;
    34	  }
    35	}
    36	
    37	async function readManifest(boxRoot: string): Promise<ManifestEntry[] | null> {
    38	  const abs = path.join(boxRoot, MANIFEST_PATH);
    39	  try {
    40	    const text = await fs.readFile(abs, "utf-8");
    41	    const entries: ManifestEntry[] = [];
    42	    for (const line of text.split("\n")) {
    43	      const trimmed = line.trim();
    44	      if (trimmed === "") continue;
    45	      entries.push(JSON.parse(trimmed) as ManifestEntry);
    46	    }
    47	    return entries;
    48	  } catch (e) {
    49	    const err = e as NodeJS.ErrnoException;
    50	    if (err.code === "ENOENT") return null;
    51	    throw new ManifestReadError(abs, e);
    52	  }
    53	}
    54	
    55	async function appendManifestEntry(boxRoot: string, entry: ManifestEntry): Promise<void> {
    56	  const abs = path.join(boxRoot, MANIFEST_PATH);
    57	  await fs.mkdir(path.dirname(abs), { recursive: true });
    58	  await fs.appendFile(abs, `${JSON.stringify(entry)}\n`);
    59	}
    60	
    61	async function writeManifest(boxRoot: string, entries: ManifestEntry[]): Promise<void> {
    62	  const abs = path.join(boxRoot, MANIFEST_PATH);
    63	  await fs.mkdir(path.dirname(abs), { recursive: true });
    64	  const text = entries.map((e) => JSON.stringify(e)).join("\n") + (entries.length > 0 ? "\n" : "");
    65	  await fs.writeFile(abs, text);
    66	}
    67	
    68	function computePending(applied: ManifestEntry[]): Migration[] {
    69	  const seen = new Set(applied.map((e) => e.name));
    70	  return MIGRATIONS.filter((m) => !seen.has(m.name));
    71	}
    72	
    73	function runScript(args: { script: string; boxRoot: string }): Promise<number> {
    74	  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    75	    const scriptPath = path.join(CALLBACK_BOX_ROOT, args.script);
    76	    const child = spawn(
    77	      "npx",
    78	      ["tsx", scriptPath, args.boxRoot, "--apply"],
    79	      { cwd: CALLBACK_BOX_ROOT, stdio: "inherit" }
    80	    );
    81	    child.on("error", reject);
    82	    child.on("close", (code) => resolve(code ?? 1));
    83	  });
    84	}
    85	
    86	function formatStatus(applied: ManifestEntry[], pending: Migration[]): string {
    87	  const lines: string[] = [];
    88	  lines.push(`Applied (${String(applied.length)}):`);
    89	  for (const e of applied) {
    90	    lines.push(`  ✓ ${e.name}  (${e["applied-at"]})`);
    91	  }
    92	  if (applied.length === 0) lines.push("  (none)");
    93	  lines.push("");
    94	  lines.push(`Pending (${String(pending.length)}):`);
    95	  for (const m of pending) {
    96	    lines.push(`  • ${m.name}`);
    97	  }
    98	  if (pending.length === 0) lines.push("  (none — manifest is up to date)");
    99	  return lines.join("\n");
   100	}
   101	
   102	interface MigrateOptions {
   103	  apply?: boolean;
   104	  status?: boolean;
   105	  markAllApplied?: boolean;
   106	}
   107	
   108	export const migrateCommand = new Command("migrate")
   109	  .description("Apply pending data migrations to this box")
   110	  .option("--apply", "Run all pending migrations in order")
   111	  .option("--status", "Show applied + pending lists (default when no flag given)")
   112	  .option("--mark-all-applied", "Seed the manifest as if every known migration ran. Use only for legacy boxes that were already fully migrated before this command existed; new boxes get their manifest seeded automatically by `cb init`.")
   113	  .action(async (options: MigrateOptions) => {
   114	    const boxRoot = await requireBoxRoot();
   115	
   116	    if (options.markAllApplied) {
   117	      const existing = await readManifest(boxRoot);
   118	      if (existing !== null && existing.length > 0) {
   119	        console.error(
   120	          `Manifest already exists at ${MANIFEST_PATH} with ${String(existing.length)} entries; --mark-all-applied refuses to overwrite. Delete the file if you really want to reseed.`,
   121	        );
   122	        process.exit(1);
   123	      }
   124	      const now = new Date().toISOString();
   125	      const entries: ManifestEntry[] = MIGRATIONS.map((m) => ({
   126	        name: m.name,
   127	        "applied-at": now,
   128	      }));
   129	      await writeManifest(boxRoot, entries);
   130	      console.log(`Wrote ${String(entries.length)} entries to ${MANIFEST_PATH} (no migrations actually ran).`);
   131	      return;
   132	    }
   133	
   134	    const applied = await readManifest(boxRoot);
   135	    if (applied === null) {
   136	      console.error(
   137	        `No migration manifest at ${MANIFEST_PATH}.\n\nThis box predates the cb migrate command. If it has already had all data migrations applied, seed the manifest with:\n  cb migrate --mark-all-applied\n\nNew boxes (via cb init) get their manifest automatically.`,
   138	      );
   139	      process.exit(1);
   140	    }
   141	    const pending = computePending(applied);
   142	
   143	    if (!options.apply || options.status) {
   144	      console.log(formatStatus(applied, pending));
   145	      return;
   146	    }
   147	
   148	    if (pending.length === 0) {
   149	      console.log("Nothing to do — manifest is up to date.");
   150	      return;
   151	    }
   152	
   153	    console.log(`Running ${String(pending.length)} pending migration(s) in order:\n`);
   154	    for (const m of pending) {
   155	      console.log(`=== ${m.name} (${m.script}) ===`);
   156	      const code = await runScript({ script: m.script, boxRoot });
   157	      if (code !== 0) {
   158	        console.error(`\nMigration "${m.name}" failed (exit code ${String(code)}). Manifest not updated for this entry. Subsequent migrations not run.`);
   159	        process.exit(code);
   160	      }
   161	      await appendManifestEntry(boxRoot, { name: m.name, "applied-at": new Date().toISOString() });
   162	      console.log(`✓ ${m.name} applied and recorded.\n`);
   163	    }
   164	    console.log("All pending migrations applied.");
   165	  });

callback-box/src/core/reactor/DESIGN.md:3:The reactor is the main orchestration loop that turns pending job cards into completed work. It coordinates syncing external sources, discovering jobs, dispatching them to agents or the procedure engine, and flushing results outbound.
callback-box/src/core/reactor/DESIGN.md:35:All pending non-chat jobs are described in a single prompt and processed by one agent session. The agent works through them sequentially, calling `cb finish` after each. This is efficient for small, independent jobs — one session startup cost amortized across many jobs.
callback-box/src/core/reactor/DESIGN.md:61:`runReactor` accepts a `sourceFilter` option. When set, jobs whose root `source` attribute does not match are skipped — left in `box/jobs/` for a later run that does match them. This is how `cb wakeup --connector X` keeps a partial sync from draining unrelated work: the gmail tick processes only `source="gmail"` jobs, even if telegram or feedback jobs are also pending.
callback-box/src/core/reactor/DESIGN.md:67:Some jobs don't need an agent at all — they just need to run a procedure (a scripted sequence of steps). The reactor detects these by looking for `<procedure ref="...">` in the job XML, then runs the procedure engine directly. This avoids wasting an agent session on what is essentially a function call.
callback-box/src/core/reactor/DESIGN.md:81:Job descriptions inline referenced files (from `<thread ref="...">` and `<item ref="...">` attributes) and look up schema-defined processing instructions for the job's root tag. This gives the agent everything it needs in the initial prompt.

In the rare case the transcript isn't enough — the words matter and look mangled, or the sound itself is the subject (pronunciation, tone) — \`cb chat retranscribe\` re-transcribes the latest voice message with the high-quality pass, and \`cb chat ask-about-audio "<question>"\` answers questions about its actual audio (\`cb chat get-last-audio\` fetches the raw file).
callback-box/src/core/chat-session-prompts.ts:69:To display an image from the box filesystem: \`![description](/<box-root-path>)\` (e.g. \`![front view](/store/notes/photos/front.png)\`). When you're authoring inside a markdown file, you can also use a path relative to that file (e.g. \`![front view](photos/front.png)\` from a note in the same directory). The renderer rewrites both forms — don't include \`api/files/\` (it still works for back-compat, but the leading-slash form is preferred). The description is shown as a one-line caption under the image (truncated) and in full when the user clicks to zoom — so write it as a useful caption, not just a filename.

callback-box/src/core/chat-session-prompts.ts:86:User-position messages wrapped in \`<self-note>\` tags are records of background agent activity — usually a scheduled sub-agent run (daily rumination, weekly research, etc.). Findings, ranked:

- **High: Track A/B are not actually box-state independent.** The plan says Tracks A+B can land while boxes migrate out of band (`remove-cardworks-package.md:273-277`, `420-432`), but Track A chunk 2 removes box-local `element()` loading (`407-411`). Today that path is live: `loadBoxSchemas` still loads `elementSchemas` and `createSchemaRegistry` registers them (`src/schemas/registry.ts:220-257`, `278-289`), and the known ledger box schemas still import `element` from `cardworks` (`/Users/ianbicking/src/boxes/ledger-copy/config/schemas/bill.ts:1`, `/Users/ianbicking/src/boxes/ledger-shrink-test/config/schemas/bill.ts:1`). Track A chunk 2 must be gated from merge/deploy until the box-schema audit is clean, not just Track C.

- **High: box-local frontmatter schemas need a new import contract.** The plan catches runtime `cardworks` imports via grep (`remove-cardworks-package.md:193-198`) and says repoint imports to `src/cards` (`241-243`, `278-280`), but box-local `config/schemas/*.ts` cannot import an internal source path. The current resolver only special-cases bare `cardworks` and `zod` from box schema files (`src/schemas/registry.ts:97-139`), and `callback-box/package.json` has no `exports` map (`package.json:1-8`). Add a public specifier such as `callback-box/cards` or an explicit resolver mapping before deleting `cardworks`.

- **Medium: the concrete “drop box-local XML” list is incomplete, though the broad gates would catch much of it.** The plan names `loadBoxSchemas`’s `elementSchemas`, `isElementSchema`, the gadget doctest, and `box-templates.ts` (`remove-cardworks-package.md:86-90`, `407-411`). Also explicitly remove/reshape `createSchemaRegistry`, `getAllSchemas`, XML pieces of `getSearchableTypes`, `load-context.ts`, and generated guide/docs plumbing (`src/schemas/registry.ts:278-324`, `src/core/load-context.ts:7-18`, `src/core/generate-docs.ts:416-421`, `src/core/agent-guide/cards.ts:6-19`). `SchemaRegistry` is still used today only through XML/CardLoader bridges (`src/cli/lib/loader.ts:7-37`, `src/core/load-context.ts:7-18`); after those bridges go, drop it rather than adapt it.

- **Medium: migrator strategy is sound, but the wording still conflicts.** Keeping `MIGRATIONS` entries and replacing scripts with successful no-op stubs matches the runner: pending entries spawn the script path, and the manifest is appended only after exit code 0 (`src/cli/commands/migrate.ts:73-80`, `153-162`; `src/core/migrations.ts:4-8`). But Track C also says the migrators are “deleted” (`remove-cardworks-package.md:268-271`, `283-285`). That should say “stub script files remain at the same paths.”

- **Medium: `todos.updateItem` is broken, but the plan under-scopes the UI half.** Backend is XML-only (`src/webapp/trpc/routers/todos.ts:21-30`, `35-58`) while the schema is frontmatter `items:` (`src/schemas/todo-list.ts:36-42`). Also, frontmatter card responses set `element: undefined` (`src/webapp/trpc/routers/card.ts:145-153`), and `TodoListView` currently returns “No todo list data” without `data.element` and parses XML children (`src/frontend/src/components/TodoListView.tsx:31-69`, `141-145`). So rewrite both: frontend should read `data.frontmatter.items`, and backend should parse with `card-io`, mutate `fields.items`, and write via `serializeCardText` or equivalent YAML serialization.

- **Low: `card.patch` deletion has a test/docs tail.** The “no frontend caller” claim looks true, but the REST PATCH route and doctest still exist (`src/webapp/routes/api-card-routes.ts:71-120`, `test/routes-api.doctest.md:112-128`). Deleting it is fine if those tests/docs are removed or rewritten.

Net: the revised plan is much closer, but not quite ready to build. The single most important remaining issue is to make the box-local schema transition explicit and gated: no shipping the `element()` removal until current boxes are migrated, and define the replacement import path for future frontmatter box schemas.
